chapters.title: About This Guide
chapters.content:
This is a full-game companion for **Final Fantasy VIII Remastered**, built around a single playthrough that captures every achievement, missable, rare card, and GF. Everything is cross-referenced — decisions in Disc 1 that matter in Disc 4 are flagged the moment they become relevant.

{{CALLOUT:hint|General strategy baseline}} MT means multi-target and ST means single-target. Treat junctioning like equipment: keep GFs assigned, keep key commands equipped, and update stat, elemental, and status junctions whenever the walkthrough flags a new spell or threat. Elemental junctions can raise attack damage or reduce incoming damage; status junctions can add useful attack effects or block dangerous ailments.

{{CALLOUT:hint|Combat priorities}} Physical attacks and Limit Breaks are usually better damage options than spending stocked magic. Offensive magic has specific uses, but casting from your stock lowers the same magic pool that powers your junction stats. Curative and status magic remain valuable, especially when drawn-and-cast directly from enemies or used to stabilize a boss fight.

{{CALLOUT:card|Triple Triad priority}} Triple Triad is available immediately and is one of the strongest progression systems in the game. Play often, but avoid spreading or mixing unwanted rules before reading the Triple Triad Rules page and the local walkthrough notes for the region you are in.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Draw command habits}} Keep Draw on at least one active character during story progression. Several bosses carry missable GFs, and many hold powerful spells far earlier than normal refinement routes. As soon as you control the party, set the in-game Cursor option to Memory so repeated Draw commands are much faster.

{{CALLOUT:point|Use free-roam windows}} The story is linear, but character growth is heavily driven by scavenging, cards, refinement, draw points, and optional errands. When the walkthrough opens a free-roam window, use it to update junctions, collect cards, solve sidequests, and prepare before pushing the next plot trigger.

{{CALLOUT:note|How to navigate}} Use the **chapter list in the sidebar** (or the menu button on mobile) to move through the walkthrough. The guide is split into four discs plus this Reference section, which sits above Disc 1. Tabs across the top (or the bottom bar on mobile) switch between the main views.

{{CALLOUT:note|Guide}} The walkthrough itself. Each chapter contains step-by-step instructions, boss cards with stats and draw lists, encounter tables for each area, local visual aids, and inline callout cards for anything that benefits from special attention. Work through these in order.

{{CALLOUT:note|Checklist}} Every achievement and missable pulled out into a single scrollable list, grouped by disc. Useful for a quick scan of what is still outstanding mid-game or after finishing a chapter.

{{CALLOUT:note|Sidequests}} Optional routes are available in two places: collapsed inside the walkthrough at the moment they open, and in the dedicated **Sidequests** tab for later cleanup. Use the tab when you decide to postpone a route and want the full steps without finding the original story chapter.

{{CALLOUT:note|Cards}} The full 110-card Triple Triad collection with acquisition notes. Cards you have checked off are shown as collected. The Queen of Cards quest and rare-card locations are covered in the walkthrough, but this view lets you see the whole picture at a glance.

{{CALLOUT:note|Guardian Forces}} All 16 GFs with their draw locations, ability lists, and recommended learn orders. Abilities with a junction value (like Spr-J or Spd-J) are noted so you can prioritise accordingly.

{{CALLOUT:note|Refine}} Every refinement recipe organised by GF ability. Use this when you have items you do not recognise or when you want to know what a material converts into.

{{CALLOUT:note|Items / Bestiary}} Item and weapon databases, and an enemy reference with HP ranges, elemental affinities, draw lists, mug items, and card drops.

{{CALLOUT:note|Story, Lore & Music}} Spoiler-gated plot recap, lore glossary, and soundtrack reference material live in the Reference section so optional context stays findable without interrupting the walkthrough.

{{CALLOUT:note|Callout cards}} Typed cards appear inline throughout the walkthrough. Missables, achievements, perfect-game requirements, sidequests, card-rule work, shops, controls, enemy intel, mechanics, draw points, points of interest, hints, warnings, and spoilers each receive their own visual treatment so the page can be scanned quickly without losing detail.

{{CALLOUT:note|Search}} Press **⌘K** (or **Ctrl+K** on Windows) from anywhere to search across chapters, enemies, cards, GFs, items, and refinement recipes. Selecting a result takes you straight to the relevant view.

{{CALLOUT:note|Progress}} Checkboxes on achievement and missable cards save to your browser. Clearing site data resets them. Nothing is sent anywhere — everything lives locally.

{{CALLOUT:note|Steam achievements — start tracking from the very beginning of the game}}
- **100 Kills / 1,000 Kills**: defeat 100 and 1,000 enemies. If cleanup is needed, farm the forest near Dollet where encounters often include three weak enemies.
- **Magician**: use Draw on enemies and choose **Stock** 100 times. The **Use** option does not count, so keep Draw equipped from the start and stock from every new enemy.
- **Magic Miner**: draw from field draw points 100 times. For late cleanup, the fastest route is on the Island Closest to Hell, which has more than 30 hidden draw points.
- **Top Rank**: reach SeeD Rank A. Written tests raise the rank and are available in Tutorial → TEST only up to Squall's current level; answer tables are in the SeeD Rank & Salary reference.
- **Card Player**: play one Triple Triad game.
- **Handyman**: upgrade any weapon once at a Junk Shop.
- **Remastered boosters**: Speed ×3, Battle Assist, and No Encounters do not disable achievements. Separate in-game Cheats do permanently disable achievement tracking for that save file.

chapters.title: Controls & Interface
chapters.content:
The control tables below use the original PlayStation labels used by the original PlayStation release. Modern ports may display different platform prompts or allow remapping, so follow the action name when your prompt differs.

{{CALLOUT:controls|World Map Controls}}
| Button | Action |
|---|---|
| X | Examine / Confirm / Exit vehicle |
| Circle | Enter menu or cockpit |
| Square | Move vehicle forward |
| Triangle | Cancel |
| Start | Pause |
| Select | Toggle map |
| D-Pad | Move / steer |
| L1 / R1 | Rotate camera |
| L2 / R2 | Change camera angle |

{{CALLOUT:controls|Field Controls}}
| Button | Action |
|---|---|
| X | Talk / Examine / Confirm |
| Circle | Enter menu |
| Square | Challenge to cards / Talk / Examine / Confirm |
| Triangle | Cancel |
| Start | Pause |
| Select | No function |
| D-Pad | Move character |
| L1 / R1 | No function |
| L2 / R2 | No function |

{{CALLOUT:controls|Battle Controls}}
| Button | Action |
|---|---|
| X | Confirm |
| Circle | Switch to the next character with an active turn |
| Square | Show target status details |
| Triangle | Cancel |
| Start | Pause |
| Select | Hide battle menu |
| D-Pad | Move cursor |
| R1 | Pull gunblade trigger |
| L2 + R2 | Hold both to run from battle |

{{CALLOUT:controls|Steam Remastered booster keys}} On the Steam Remastered release, **F1** activates Battle Assist, **F2** activates No Random Encounters, and **F3** activates 3× Speed. These boosters do not disable achievements; the separate in-game Cheats do.

{{CALLOUT:controls|Gunblade timing}} Squall and Seifer do not roll normal weapon critical hits. Press R1 during the attack impact window to trigger 150% of normal attack damage. The same timing applies to each Renzokuken strike.

{{CALLOUT:controls|Triple Triad shortcut}} Square is the field prompt used to challenge eligible NPCs to cards. If Square instead talks or examines, the NPC or object is not currently accepting a card challenge from that position.

{{CALLOUT:controls|Menu and interface notes}} Junction changes, GF ability targets, Card Mod, refinement abilities, SeeD tests, Battle Report, and Tutorial entries live in the in-game menu. The app's search and checklist systems are separate local tools and do not modify the save file.

chapters.title: Shop Reference
chapters.content:
Tonberry abilities change shop prices, reveal extra stock, and let you call registered shops remotely.

Use the **Items view** (accessible via the bottom nav) to browse all items and their buy prices. Shop-specific inventories are listed below for quick reference.

{{CALLOUT:shop|How to use shops efficiently}} General item shops handle core consumables and basic ammo. Specialty shops in Timber and Esthar add pet magazines, GF scrolls, junction scrolls, and late-game accessories. Tonberry's Familiar reveals hidden stock, Haggle lowers buy/remodel costs, Sell-High increases sale value, and Call Shop lets you revisit registered shops remotely.

{{CALLOUT:warning|Disc 4 shop access}} Before the point of no return, visit each important shop to register it with Call Shop. Esthar Shop!!! is normally closed; enter repeatedly until it opens once.

chapters.title: Sidequest Index
chapters.content:
This index tracks the optional quest chains, optional GFs, optional bosses, and dedicated mini-game routes that live outside the main story path. Routine missable pickups, shop visits, card prep, and one-time dungeon loot stay in the chronological walkthrough and Checklist instead of being treated as sidequests.

{{CALLOUT:sidequest|Disc 1 sidequests}} - **The Magical Lamp**: Use Cid's Magical Lamp when ready, defeat Diablos, and unlock Enc-Half, Enc-None, Mug, and Time Mag-RF early.
- **Timber Maniacs Collection**: Start the magazine collection in Balamb and keep collecting each town/ship issue before access windows close.
- **Zell Love Quest**: Speak to the Library Girl with pigtails at each required Garden window; the final route leads to Combat King 003 and the Zell scene payoff.
- **The Novice SeeD Candidates**: Speak to the three Cafeteria candidates across all five windows, keep talking until their dialogue repeats, then return after Trabia Canyon for the payoff scene.
- **Queen of Cards**: Lose MiniMog, Sacred, Chicobo, Alexander, and Doomtrain at the correct times to create Kiros, Irvine, Chubby Chocobo, Doomtrain, and Phoenix.
- **Timber Journalist**: Encourage the Timber journalist on Disc 1, then return after Missile Base for the Pet Nametag.
- **Dollet Bone Quest**: Use the artist-house painting clues and the dog route to find Dollet's hidden rewards.
- **Tomb of the Unknown King**: Go beyond the required student ID number to recruit Brothers and earn Sacred/Minotaur.

{{CALLOUT:sidequest|Disc 2 sidequests}} - **Master Fisherman's Quest**: Start the FH fisherman route before advancing too far through the town scenes, then finish it for Occult Fan III and SeeD experience.
- **CC Group**: Defeat Jack, Joker, Club, Diamond, Spade, Heart, and King before the end of Disc 3 so the group appears on the Ragnarok in Disc 4.
- **Centra Ruins**: Recruit Odin and Tonberry from the optional ruins route when their long-term effects fit your plan.
- **Shumi Village**: Complete the sculptor stone hunt and the later Moomba Doll phase for Phoenix Pinion and Status Guard.
- **Chocobo Forests**: Solve all six forests, claim each forest treasure, and reach Chocobo Sanctuary for Chicobo.
- **Winhill Revisited**: Return to Winhill with Quistis or Irvine and collect all four vase fragments.

{{CALLOUT:sidequest|Disc 3 sidequests}} - **Acquiring Doomtrain**: Collect Solomon Ring, 6 Remedy+, 6 Steel Pipe, and 6 Malboro Tentacle, then use the ring.
- **Acquiring Cactuar**: Defeat Jumbo Cactuar on Cactuar Island to obtain Cactuar GF and unlock Bonus ability planning.
- **Deep Sea Research Center**: Obtain Bahamut, descend through the steam puzzle, and draw Eden from Ultima Weapon before defeating it.
- **Obel Lake**: Complete the shadow, Mr. Monkey, rock-clue, Mordred Plains, and Minde Island treasure route.
- **PuPu's Quest**: Trigger all UFO sightings, defeat the UFO, then feed PuPu five Elixirs for the PuPu Card.

{{CALLOUT:sidequest|Disc 4 sidequests}} - **Disc 4 Ragnarok Recovery**: Use the compressed-time portal route to regain Ragnarok access for final cleanup.
- **The Ultimate Monster**: Restore the needed castle commands, ring the bell, switch parties, and defeat the optional superboss before the timer expires.

{{CALLOUT:point|Where the other optional work lives}} Triple Triad has its own Cards tab, while storyline mini-games, rare-card pickup prep, Esthar shop visits, prison floor rewards, final equipment checks, and Perfect Game prerequisites are still covered in Checklist, Cards, Items, Shops, Bestiary, or the chronological walkthrough rather than the Sidequests tab.

chapters.title: Character Reference
chapters.content:
Use this page when choosing a party, checking Limit Break mechanics, or confirming which magazine/item unlocks a character-specific option. The exact Limit Break tables live in the cards below so combo inputs, Crisis Level behavior, and unlock requirements stay easy to scan.

{{CALLOUT:character|How to read this page}} Each character starts with profile fields plus detailed tables. The main party has full Limit Break and unlock tables; temporary party members have availability, base stat growth, weapon behavior, and automatic Limit details so their short playable windows are still documented.

{{CALLOUT:hint|Practical party building}} Base stats matter less than junctions, but Limit Break behavior matters a lot. Squall, Zell, Rinoa, and Irvine are the major damage engines; Quistis brings utility through Blue Magic; Selphie has unique emergency tools through Slots. Temporary party members inherit junction sets during dream or story sequences, so check the walkthrough for who maps to whom before each sequence.

chapters.title: Combat Mechanics
chapters.content:
This page explains the battle rules that sit underneath the walkthrough: how encounters start, how units act, how actions resolve, how Limit Breaks become available, and how rewards are awarded. Use it when something in a boss strategy depends on ATB timing, battle-end flags, or reward behavior.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Starting battle flow}} Battles can be random, forced, or triggered by dialogue and quest paths. The active party can contain up to three characters, and a battle field can contain up to six enemies. The selected formation determines which enemies appear and also controls the opening position: normal, attacked from behind, struck first, chance for first strike, or back attack. Alert prevents non-forced attacked-from-behind or struck-first openings. Statuses already present when a unit enters battle remain active and can be cured normally. Enemy opening attacks, when scripted, resolve before ordinary ATB activity begins.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Battle unit stats}} Every participant in battle is a unit. Reducing HP to zero inflicts KO even if that unit would normally be immune, and KO flags the unit as dead while still allowing any final attack script to fire. Units also carry status immunities and elemental properties, which determine whether statuses land and how elemental damage is multiplied.
| Stat Name | Abbr. | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Level | LV | General indication of the strength of the unit; also used to determine if certain attacks will hit |
| Strength | Str | Determines the power of any physical attacks used by the unit |
| Vitality | Vit | Reduces damage taken from physical attacks |
| Magic | Mag | Determines the power of any magical attacks used by the unit |
| Spirit | Spr | Reduces damage taken from magical attacks |
| Speed | Spd | Determines how much time is required to fill ATB gauge |
| Evade | Eva | Reduces hit rate of physicals targeting the unit |
| Hit Rate | Hit | Hit rate of regular physical attacks |
| Luck | Luck | Determines critical hit rate and also increases hit rate and evasion |

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Battle timing and ATB}} ATB gauges fill whenever battle time is allowed to move; some actions and menus pause time depending on settings, but choosing a target does not. Speed controls fill rate. Haste makes the gauge fill 1.5x as fast, Slow halves it, and KO, Petrify, Sleep, and Stop freeze the gauge; KO also resets it to zero. Characters start with full ATB during chance-for-first-strike and back-attack openings, or with Initiative equipped. Enemies start full during back and ambush attacks. When a unit acts, its ATB resets after the action; Limit Breaks jump ahead of normal queued actions.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Action resolution}} Attacks can be single-target or multi-target. Once an action executes, hit rate and evasion are checked first where applicable, then the action resolves through its physical, magical, status, elemental, row, and multiplier rules. Physical actions primarily use Strength against Vitality; magical actions primarily use Magic against Spirit. Fixed-damage attacks bypass normal stat formulas and use their own special calculations.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Ending a battle}} Battle ends when all units on one side are flagged dead or removed. KO, Eject, Petrify, and The End count as dead flags; escaped units are removed but do not use Eject status. Some boss scripts end the battle before every enemy falls, so a living enemy can still contribute EXP proportional to damage dealt. Characters who end a battle KO receive no EXP or AP; their equipped GFs still receive a share if those GFs are not KO or Level 100. A successful Mug prevents that enemy from dropping an item after battle. Each ending method’s EXP/AP/drop results are listed below.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|EXP and AP — how battle endings change rewards}} The method used to end a battle determines whether EXP, AP, and item drops are awarded.
- **Normal victory** (kill all enemies): full EXP, full AP, normal item drops apply
- **Card command** (use Card on an enemy): AP is awarded, but **zero EXP** and no drop from that enemy — the cleanest way to end battles without gaining levels
- **Devour command** (Tonberry ability): AP is awarded, **zero EXP**, no drop — same as Card for level control
- **Escape** (L2+R2): **no AP**, and you receive a fraction of EXP proportional to how much HP damage you dealt — e.g., if the enemy gives 200 EXP and you dealt 30% of its HP in damage, you earn 60 EXP regardless of the escape; this partial EXP gain is unavoidable when escaping
- **All enemies fully Petrified** (Petrify/Break ending): treated identically to escape — **no AP**, partial EXP proportional to HP dealt, no item drops; avoid accidental full-party Petrify when farming for drops
- **Petrify (shattered)**: if a physically petrified enemy is shattered with a physical hit, normal rewards apply; it is the slow-Petrify-then-shatter approach that avoids the "escape" calculation
- Key takeaway for low-level play: use **Card or Devour** to end battles with zero EXP, since both escaping and Petrify-ending still yield partial EXP

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Crisis Level — how Limit Breaks trigger}} Every playable character’s Limit Break command appears only when their Crisis Level reaches 1. The primary factor is HP at or below 32% of max; lower HP raises the level. Crisis Level ranges from 1 near 32% HP through 4 near zero, with character-specific effects: Squall gets more Renzokuken hits and a better finisher chance; Zell gets more Duel time; Irvine’s Shot window stays open longer; Selphie’s Slots pool becomes stronger and the chosen spell fires more times; Quistis deals more damage with most Blue Magic. Other factors can raise Crisis Level: Slow adds 6%; Poison, Petrifying, Darkness, or Silence add 12% each; Doom adds 18%; and one or two KO’d allies add 8% or 16%. Zombie and Vit 0 add nothing. **Aura** bypasses the HP threshold and raises Crisis Level to its maximum. Seifer can rarely access his Limit at much higher HP than other characters. If the command does not appear, cycle to another active character and back to refresh availability. Aura is especially useful before boss fights.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Magic casting mechanics and interactions}}
- **Draw-and-cast**: in the Draw menu, choose **Use** to cast an enemy-held spell immediately without spending stocked magic. This is useful for emergency Cure, support magic, or testing a boss draw list.
- **Double / Triple and Draw**: Double and Triple multiply magic casts, not Draw actions. A Draw command still draws once.
- **Meteor targeting**: Meteor's 10 hits are distributed randomly across all living targets. Against one enemy, every hit lands on that enemy.
- **Quake and flying targets**: Quake misses airborne or Float targets. Use Wind or non-elemental magic instead; Float on the party can neutralize enemy Quake.
- **Gravity spells**: Demi removes 25% current HP up to 9,999 damage. The cap matters against enemies above roughly 40,000 current HP.
- **Bio and Poison**: Bio's Poison-element damage and Poison-status chance are separate. Poison-absorbing enemies may be healed by Bio even if the status portion can still land.
- **Undead / Zombie healing reversal**: Cure, Regen, Phoenix Down, Tent, and similar healing damage undead or Zombie targets; Life and Full-Life instead instantly KO them. Cure Zombie before using party-wide recovery items, or healing will damage that ally. Drain reverses against undead and hurts the caster.
- **Life and Full-Life:** Life revives allies at 12.5% max HP; Full-Life revives to full HP.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Enemy level scaling formula}} Random encounter enemies appear at either the average party level +20% or −20% (rounding applied). For example, with an average party level of 10, enemies will be either Lv 8 or Lv 12. The single exception is the **Deep Sea Research Center**, where an additional **+15 levels** are added on top of the standard calculation — meaning DSRC enemies at an average party level of 10 will be either Lv 23 or Lv 27. Most boss enemies have a maximum level cap beyond which they cannot scale. Enemies in the **Fire Cavern** are all fixed at Lv 5; those in the **Lunatic Pandora** with Squall are all fixed at Lv 1; and enemies on the **Islands Closest to Heaven/Hell** are all fixed at Lv 100. Ultimecia's Castle is the sole exception where enemy levels are completely random (not tied to party average). Use Tonberry's **LV Up** or **LV Down** commands to adjust enemy levels within the ±20% range to hit draw-list or drop-list thresholds during farming sessions.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Mug and Drop item slot probabilities}} Every enemy has four possible mug items (Slots A–D) and four possible drop items (Slots A–D). The probability of landing each slot follows the same distribution for both Mug and Drop: **Slot A = 178/256 (~70%)**, **Slot B = 51/256 (~20%)**, **Slot C = 15/256 (~6%)**, **Slot D = 12/256 (~5%)**. A successful Mug or post-battle Drop yields exactly one item from these four slots. When the **Rare Item** party ability is equipped, the probabilities shift to: **Slot A = 128/256 (50%)**, **Slot B = 114/256 (45%)**, **Slot C = 14/256 (5%)**, **Slot D = 0/256 (0%)**. This means Rare Item increases Slot B results substantially but makes Slot D items completely unobtainable — never equip Rare Item when the target item is in Slot D. Additionally, the mugger's Speed stat adds to the Mug success chance (the base chance is listed per-enemy; final chance = base + Spd ÷ 2), which is why high-Speed characters are better muggers. A successful Mug exhausts that enemy's steal and prevents any post-battle item drop from it; a failed Mug can be attempted again.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Defend command mechanics}} Selecting Defend puts the character in a guarded stance until their next action input. While defending: physical attacks deal **zero damage** (completely blocked, not just reduced) and magic attacks deal **50% reduced damage**. This is the primary survival tool against Omega Weapon's Terra Break (16 random physical hits) and other high-physical-output bosses. Defend has 100 AP cost and is taught by Cactuar.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Devour command outcome guide}}
Devour ends the enemy encounter without EXP or a post-battle drop, but it does award AP. Success improves when the target's current HP is lower than the user's current HP, so enter at full HP and weaken the target first.

| Outcome | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Delicious! | Full HP restore |
| Refreshing! | Full HP restore and status cure |
| Tastes okay... | Restores 50% max HP |
| Gained strength | Full HP, status cure, Str +1 |
| Feel healthier | Full HP, status cure, Vit +1 |
| Clear head! | Full HP, status cure, Mag +1 |
| Increased morale | Full HP, status cure, Spr +1 |
| Light on my feet! | Full HP, status cure, Spd +1 |
| All systems go! | Full HP, status cure, max HP +10 |
| Tastes awful!!! | 12.5% max HP damage and Poison |
| Can't see anything | 6.25% max HP damage and Darkness |
| It's rotten... | 6.25% max HP damage and Zombie |
| Barf...bwahhh!!! | 50% max HP damage and Poison |
| Tastes funny... | Petrify |
| Shouldn't have...eaten...it | 75% max HP damage plus Poison, Darkness, Silence, Sleep, Slow, and Curse |
| No good! | No effect |

| Stat target | Enemy and level |
| --- | --- |
| Str +1 | T-Rexaur at Lv30+ |
| Vit +1 | Adamantoise at Lv30+ |
| Mag +1 | Behemoth at Lv40+ |
| Spr +1 | Malboro at Lv30+ |
| Spd +1 | PuPu at Lv30+ |
| max HP +10 | Ruby Dragon at Lv45+ |

PuPu is a special choice: devouring it prevents completing the UFO sidequest for the PuPu Card. Most boss-class and humanoid enemies cannot be devoured.

chapters.title: Status Effects
chapters.content:
Here you'll find a list of the status effects that appear in Final Fantasy VIII.

{{CALLOUT:status|Drain (Effect)}} Internally, "Drain" effects (that is, spells/attacks that drain HP from the target and give it to the user) are treated as status ailments (you can Junction to defend the effect, and some enemies have partial or complete resistance), but this is only to calculate the HP total transferred; no actual status is inflicted solely by nature of having a "drain" effect, and the damage dealt is likewise unaffected. If targeting a unit under Zombie, the effect will be reversed, with the user giving HP to the target.

{{CALLOUT:status|Status Ailments}} These effects will debilitate a unit in some way. Unless otherwise noted, all ailments can be removed by the Esuna spell, a Remedy or Remedy+ item (Elixir/Megalixir include a Remedy+ effect on their targets), or the Treatment ability. Any other methods of removing the status will be listed as well (if a status wears off over time, ending battle will also remove it, except for inherent abilities). Tents, Cottages, and Inns will remove ALL status ailments, and thus will not be mentioned in individual entries.

{{CALLOUT:status|Darkness}} Unit's Hit stat is reduced by 75%, decreasing hit rate of physicals (if the attack is magical, unblockable, or has 255% Hit, it will not be affected). Permanent until healed. Remove with Eye Drops.

{{CALLOUT:status|Poison}} Unit takes roughly 5-9% of its maximum HP as Poison-elemental damage every time it takes a turn. Permanent until healed. Remove with Antidote.

{{CALLOUT:status|Silence}} Prevents use of Magic in addition to the GF and Draw commands. Permanent until healed. Remove with Echo Screen.

{{CALLOUT:status|Sleep}} Unit cannot act, and physicals targeting it have a perfect Hit Rate. Wears off over time, or remove by inflicting KO or striking with a physical attack.

{{CALLOUT:status|Confuse}} Randomly uses the Attack/Mug, Magic (if equipped), or Item (if equipped) Command against random targets. Remove by striking with a physical attack, inflicting KO, or ending battle.

{{CALLOUT:status|Berserk}} Unit attacks with a physical targeted to a random opponent, dealing 50% extra damage. Remove by ending battle or inflicting KO.

{{CALLOUT:status|Slow}} Nullifies Haste and reduces by half the rate at which the unit's ATB gauge increases. Wears off over time, or remove by inflicting Haste or Stop.

{{CALLOUT:status|Stop}} Nullifies Haste and Slow, and stops the unit's ATB gauge and any status timers completely. Wears off over time; it can also be removed with Haste, Slow, Esuna, Remedy+, or Treatment.

{{CALLOUT:status|Zombie}} All healing effects deal damage, while the unit gains immunity to Doom and instant KO. Drain effects are reversed, the target gains a weakness [2x] to Holy, and its attack power increases. Permanent until healed. Remove with Holy Water (Elixir/Megalixir will inflict unblockable KO to Zombified targets, and cannot remove the status).

{{CALLOUT:status|Curse}} Prevents use of Limit Breaks. Remove by ending battle or with Holy Water.

{{CALLOUT:status|Vit0}} Unit's Vit and Spr stats are reduced to 0. Remove by ending battle or using Remedy+ (Esuna and Remedy cannot remove it).

{{CALLOUT:status|Petrifying}} When the timer reaches 0, Petrify status is inflicted (ignoring immunities). Remove with Soft or by ending battle.

{{CALLOUT:status|Petrify}} Unit cannot act and is flagged as "dead." Remove with Soft.

{{CALLOUT:status|Doom}} When the timer reaches 0, KO status is inflicted (ignoring immunities). Remove with Remedy+ (Esuna and normal Remedy items will not work).

{{CALLOUT:status|KO}} Unit's HP is reduced to 0. Unit cannot act and is flagged as "dead." Can be inflicted by reducing HP to 0 (ignores immunity in this case) or through attacks that directly inflict the status. Normal healing methods will not work to remove this; you must use Phoenix Down, Mega Phoenix, Phoenix's Summon, Life/Full-Life, or the Revive command to remove the status.

{{CALLOUT:status|Eject}} Unit is flagged as "dead" and removed from battle. Remove by ending battle.

{{CALLOUT:status|The End (Status)}} The End is a special form of KO that uses its own resistance check. It instantly KO's anything not immune to it. In mutli-stage battles, a successful The End will advance the battle to the next stage (the same as a KO inflicted by any other method). Almost all enemies, including most bosses but excluding some Undeads, are vulnerable to it.

{{CALLOUT:status|Positive Statuses}} These effects assist the unit in some way, ranging from reducing damage to increasing battle speed to allowing Limit Break use to flat-out nullifying damage. All positive statuses (except Angel Wing and Invincible) can be removed with Dispel.

{{CALLOUT:status|Protect}} Halves physical damage taken.

{{CALLOUT:status|Shell}} Halves magical damage taken.

{{CALLOUT:status|Reflect}} Reflects most Magic back at the opposing party. Cannot Reflect a spell that has already been Reflected.

{{CALLOUT:status|Float}} Grants immunity to ground-based attacks (note that not all Earth-elemental attacks are ground-based, and those that aren't will still land regardless of Float status).

{{CALLOUT:status|Regen}} Heals target for 5% its maximum HP 16 times during the duration of the status (in other words, 80% in total).

{{CALLOUT:status|Haste}} Unit's ATB guage fills 50% faster.

{{CALLOUT:status|Double}} Allows double-casting of Magic.

{{CALLOUT:status|Triple}} Allows triple-casting of Magic. Does not allow double-casting unless Double status is also present.

{{CALLOUT:status|Aura}} Unit gains ability to use Limits much more easily, and with a higher Crisis Level.

{{CALLOUT:status|Angel Wing}} Only available to Rinoa in her Angel Wing Limit. Rinoa gains immunity to Berserk, Confuse, and Silence. Angel Wing status causes her to cast, at random, any Attack or offensive status magic in her inventory, dealing 5x normal damage. Spells cast under Angel Wing are not expended, and Double/Triple statuses are ignored. Higher-level spells tend to have a lower probability of being cast, but you can remove the lower-level spells from Rinoa's inventory to make her use the better spells.

{{CALLOUT:status|Defend (Status)}} Nullifies all physical attacks (including statuses they can inflict) and halves magical damage. Lasts until character takes another action.

{{CALLOUT:status|Invincible}} Character is immune to all forms of damage and status effects (positive or negative). Restorative actions or ones that remove statuses will still work, unlike the status's FFVII counterpart. Dispel is not able to remove the status.

chapters.title: Junction Quick Reference
chapters.content:
Junctions are the core stat system: stocked magic boosts character stats, adds elemental/status behavior to attacks, and protects against elements/statuses on defense.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Stat junction values}} Exact 100-stock stat values for every spell are available in the Magic Quick Reference. Use the Stat Junctions table here to confirm which GF abilities open each slot, then use Magic when deciding the best spell for HP-J, Str-J, Mag-J, and the other numeric stat slots.

{{CALLOUT:hint|Practical early priorities}} Early game: Water, Tornado, Double, and Curaga are strong stat fillers. Status attack setups like Blind, Sleep, or Death are situationally powerful. For defense, spread Esuna/Reflect/Holy style multi-status protection where possible rather than overprotecting one character.

chapters.title: SeeD Rank & Salary
chapters.content:
Squall holds a SeeD rank that determines the salary paid automatically at regular step intervals. Starting rank comes from the Fire Cavern and Dollet field exam, then later story choices, written tests, battles, and salary payouts move the hidden SeeD Exp value up or down.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|SeeD Experience system}} SeeD Rank is based on hidden **SeeD Exp**: Rank = floor(SeeD Exp / 100). Rank A is the maximum and starts at 3,100 SeeD Exp. The hard cap is 3,110 SeeD Exp, so receiving salary at Rank A costs 10 SeeD Exp and drops you back to Rank 30 unless you earn at least 10 enemy kills before the next salary interval.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Routine SeeD Exp changes}}
| Event | SeeD Experience Change |
| --- | --- |
| Defeat an enemy with a party member | +1 |
| Receive SeeD salary | -10 |
| Pass a SeeD Test from the menu | Rounded up to the next 100 SeeD Exp |

GF kills and delayed-status kills do not count for the +1 enemy-kill gain. SeeD Tests do not add a flat 100; they raise the hidden value only to the next rank threshold. Tests are capped by Squall's current character level.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Salary payment interval}} Salary is paid every **24,575 internal steps**. One visible footstep usually counts as several internal steps. Chocobo movement and car movement count; moving Balamb Garden or the Ragnarok does not.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Initial SeeD Rank formula}} The starting rank is calculated from five exam categories. Add the category modifiers to 500, divide by 100, round down, then clamp to Rank 1-10. Destroying X-ATM092 adds 100 points before the final rank clamp; showing off the gunblade to the students on Balamb Garden 2F removes 100 points before the final rank clamp.

{{CALLOUT:hint|High starting rank}} The SeeD Exam chapter puts the Conduct, Judgment, Attack, Spirit, and Attitude targets into the story route so you can raise your rank without backtracking through Dollet.

chapters.title: Triple Triad Rules
chapters.content:
Triple Triad is played on a 3×3 grid with each player placing five cards. Cards have four numeric values (Top, Bottom, Left, Right; A represents 10). When you place a card adjacent to an opponent's card and your touching side exceeds theirs, you flip it to your color. The player controlling more cards when the grid is full wins.

{{CALLOUT:card|Play Rule: Open}} Both players can see all cards in each other's hand before placement begins. Eliminates guesswork entirely — play becomes a pure strategy game with full information.

{{CALLOUT:card|Play Rule: Same}} When the placed card's values match two or more sides touching adjacent opponent cards simultaneously, all matching opponent cards flip at once. Chains with Combo.
- Example: you place a card with Right=7 and Bottom=7 next to two opponents cards whose touching sides also show 7 each — both flip simultaneously

{{CALLOUT:card|Play Rule: Same Wall}} Treats the outer grid border as a value of A (10) for the purpose of the Same rule. Allows edge placements to trigger Same even without two adjacent opponent cards.

{{CALLOUT:card|Play Rule: Plus}} When the placed card's value plus the touching side of one opponent card equals the same sum as the placed card's value plus a second adjacent touching side, all involved opponent cards flip simultaneously.
- Example: your Right=5 touches opponent's Left=3 (sum 8) and your Bottom=6 touches opponent's Top=2 (sum 8) → both flip. More complex to set up than Same but catches experienced opponents off guard.

{{CALLOUT:card|Play Rule: Combo}} Cards that flip due to Same, Plus, or Same Wall then act as though freshly placed, potentially flipping additional adjacent opponent cards through normal value comparisons. Can cascade across the entire board in a single turn.

{{CALLOUT:card|Play Rule: Elemental}} Random elemental symbols are assigned to some grid squares before the game. A card placed on a matching element gains +1 to all four values; a mismatched element imposes −1 to all four. Elements correspond to the eight GF affinities (Fire, Ice, Thunder, Earth, Wind, Water, Holy, Poison).

{{CALLOUT:card|Play Rule: Sudden Death}} If the final score is tied at 5–5, both players keep only the cards currently showing their color, then replay with those cards. Continues until a winner emerges.
- Warning: avoid ties when playing for specific rare cards — if you don't own the card you want at the replay start, you cannot win it

{{CALLOUT:card|Play Rule: Random}} Instead of choosing five cards, both players have five cards dealt randomly from their entire deck.
- Mitigate by keeping your full deck stocked with high-value cards; low-value cards in the collection become a liability

{{CALLOUT:card|Trade Rule — One}} Winner takes one card from the loser's hand. The most common rule; standard for most NPC opponents.

{{CALLOUT:card|Trade Rule — Diff}} Winner takes a number of cards equal to the score difference. Winning 7–3 earns four cards; if the score margin exceeds the loser's five-card hand, the winner simply takes all five. Most rewarding for dominant victories.

{{CALLOUT:card|Trade Rule — Direct}} Each player claims the cards that display their color at game end, regardless of who originally played them. This means an opponent can take one of your original cards if it finishes on their color.

{{CALLOUT:card|Trade Rule — All}} Winner takes the opponent's entire five-card hand. High stakes for both sides — only play All against easy opponents when your own deck contains no irreplaceable cards.

{{CALLOUT:card|Regional rules}} Starting rules differ by region. Use the combined table at the end when checking a region’s rules or looking for the Queen.

{{CALLOUT:card|How Play Rules Spread}} When you challenge someone in a different region from the last region you played in, the game may mix rules between them. One of three outcomes randomly occurs: a rule from your previous region may spread to the new region; a rule from the new region may be abolished; or nothing changes. This happens whether you win, lose, or quit.
- The most dangerous spread is **Random** reaching Balamb or any low-rule region — it makes card-farming unreliable since you cannot choose your own hand
- To limit spreading: repeatedly challenge NPCs in the same region without crossing into new areas
- The **Queen of Cards** NPC has her own personal trade rule and can influence the region she's in: every challenge in her region has a ~1/3 chance of adopting her personal trade rule. Challenge anyone in her region (not the Queen herself) to push the trade rule toward her personal rule

{{CALLOUT:card|Remove an Unwanted Rule}} To remove an unwanted rule from a region, challenge someone there with mixed rules (from a different region) and hope for abolition — save before attempting. Each attempt has a random chance of abolishing a rule, adding a rule, or no change.
- **Fastest method**: challenge the Student Skipping Class by the Balamb Town harbor to clear all Balamb special rules; this does not change its trade rule
- Priority targets: remove Random from any region you plan to farm cards in; Random makes card selection impossible

{{CALLOUT:card|How Trade Rules Spread}} The game tracks a dominance counter (0–10) for trade rules. Playing a card game in the currently dominant region raises the counter by 1; playing in any other region lowers it by 1. When the counter reaches 0 and you play in a different region, that region becomes the new dominant region and the counter resets to 1. To reliably lock a region as dominant, play 11 consecutive games there to bring the counter to its maximum. Once dominant, that trade rule slowly spreads to other regions as you play there. The trade rule degrades through the chain One ← Diff ← Direct ← All (each step goes down one tier; One stays at One). Check the current dominant region and pattern by speaking to the Queen of Cards.

{{CALLOUT:card|Queen of Cards — Service and Movement}} The Queen of Cards offers two services: changing the local trade rule (free — just play a card game against her) and spreading a play rule to her current region for 30,000 gil. The 30,000 gil service cycles through play rules in this order: Open → Same → Plus → Random → Sudden Death → Same Wall → Elemental — she always offers the first rule in this sequence that the current region does not yet have. If you want a specific region to have a specific rule, bring the Queen there first (by losing to her) and use this service.

{{CALLOUT:card|Queen of Cards movement table}} To move her, lose a card game against her; she then travels to one of the following locations. The number in parentheses is the probability she moves to each destination.
- From **Balamb**: Dollet (37.5%), Deling City (62.5%)
- From **Dollet**: Balamb (37.5%), Deling City (62.5%)
- From **Deling City**: Balamb (12.5%), Dollet (12.5%), Winhill (12.5%), FH (62.5%)
- From **Winhill**: Deling City (37.5%), Dollet (37.5%), FH (25%)
- From **FH**: Dollet (12.5%), Winhill (25%), Esthar (62.5%)
- From **Esthar**: Dollet (12.5%), Shumi Village (25%), FH (12.5%), Lunar Gate (50%)
- From **Shumi Village**: Balamb (25%), Dollet (50%), Lunar Gate (25%)
- From **Lunar Gate**: Random — any area, with no hint given

{{CALLOUT:card|Last Queen setup window}} The Queen’s final Disc 3 setup for Ragnarok card farming is in **Back on Earth**, before the Mobile Type 8 cutoff.

{{CALLOUT:card|Changing Regional Rules}} These tables are for deliberate card-rule work. They are not required for ordinary play, but they help when removing Random, preserving Open, or steering trade rules for rare-card cleanup.

chapters.title: GF Mechanics
chapters.content:
Guardian Forces (GFs) are summonable beings that grant passive junction slots and commands as well as an active summon attack. Each GF learns abilities by accumulating AP from battles while assigned to a character. Learned abilities must be equipped to affect stats, commands, or passive effects. All 16 junctionable GFs can be collected and distributed across the party, with multiple GFs assigned to each character; every GF has its own level and AP progression independent of the character carrying it.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|GF ability learning and teaching}} The default GF learning order is usually poor, so manually choose the next AP target after every learned ability. Menu/refinement abilities are early priorities because they unlock magic, items, and card conversion. Stat Bonus abilities are long-term priorities before leveling. When teaching abilities with items, remember that GFs have limited ability slots: use Amnesia Greens first if needed, and prefer deleting easily relearned universal commands such as Magic, GF, Draw, or Item before deleting rare abilities that cannot be retaught.

{{CALLOUT:hint|Weapon upgrade priority}} Weapon upgrades are modest for most characters until late Disc 3 or Disc 4. The major exceptions are Squall, whose weapon tiers unlock stronger Renzokuken finishers, and Selphie, whose Strange Vision gives perfect Hit. If you already have materials, upgrading is fine; grinding only for routine weapon stats is usually less valuable than better junctions, cards, and refinement.

{{CALLOUT:refinement|Working backward for rare items}} For rare materials, start from the target item, then walk backward through Items and Refine until you reach a repeatable source: shop purchase, card mod, Angelo Search, draw point, or enemy mug/drop. Prefer higher yield and repeatable routes over one-off sources. Be careful with chained refinements where each step consumes multiple inputs; a 5-to-1 chain repeated twice needs 25 original inputs for one final result.

{{CALLOUT:sidequest|Angelo Search planning}} Angelo Search is a Disc 3+ Rinoa passive route for rare items such as Jet Engine, Hero, Gold Armor, Aegis Amulet, Healing Ring, and Hungry Cookpot. Automated searching is safest with Rinoa in the party against a disabled Turtapod in the Esthar world-map city area: put the Turtapod into defense mode, Confuse it, keep the battle stalled, and let Angelo Search trigger over time. The full Angelo Search item pool and probabilities are in Rinoa's character card. Gilgamesh, Angelo Recover, and Angelo Reverse can interrupt long search setups; avoid teaching Recover/Reverse until Search farming is done if you plan to use this method.

{{CALLOUT:refinement|High-value rarity route notes}} Dark Matter and Shaman Stone routes revolve around Curse Spikes from Tri-Face plus Lv100 Siren Tool-RF. Full-Life is most efficiently stocked from Phoenix Card refinement or Regen Ring routes. Triple can come from Quistis/Irvine/Squall card mods or Cerberus draws. Pain and Dark Matter both point back to Tri-Face farming. Aura can be made by buying Power Wrists or Hypno Crowns from Esthar Pet Shop with Familiar, refining them to Aura Stones, then refining those into Aura magic. Pulse Ammo is most cleanly made from Energy Crystals through Ammo-RF, with a small Disc 2 Pulse Ammo gift available from Grease Monkey if Irvine visits during the concert sequence.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Summoning}} Selecting the GF command begins a charge animation that fills a bar over several seconds. During the charging phase, incoming damage to the junctioning character is taken from the GF's HP instead.
- If the GF's HP drops to zero mid-summon, the summon cancels and that character must try again next turn
- GF HP scales with GF level and persists between battles; restore it with GF recovery items, a Cottage, or other GF-healing effects
- Once the bar fills, the summon animation plays and damage is dealt

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Boost}} While a GF is charging, pressing Square repeatedly increases the final damage multiplier.
- The counter starts at **75%** on the first press; each subsequent successful press adds **+1%** to summon damage
- The **maximum achievable value is 250%** (2.5× base damage) — only achievable with Eden's very long animation (72.6 seconds); most GFs cap out in the 180–240% range given their shorter animations (e.g., Quezacotl ~180% in 13.3 sec; Brothers ~220% in 19.3 sec; Eden is the only GF that can reach 250%)
- Pressing Square while the cross marker is displayed resets the counter to 75%
- The GF must have the Boost ability unlocked via AP before the Boost prompt appears
- **Status attacks affect the summoner, not the GF**, during the summon animation — Silence, Berserk, or KO on the summoner cancels the charge; Petrify also interrupts. Healing items and recovery magic used on the summoner during charging restore the summoner's HP, not the GF's

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|GF Compatibility}} Each GF has a separate Compatibility value with every character, ranging from 0 to 1,000. Higher Compatibility reduces the summon charge time for that GF with that character.
- Compatibility rises when: the GF is summoned in battle, or the character uses a Compatibility-raising item
- Compatibility can fall when you summon other GFs in the same battle; rival pairs take an additional penalty (see below)
- Summon time benchmarks by Compatibility: **0** ≈ 16.8 sec · **500** ≈ 10.2 sec · **1,000** ≈ 2.8 sec — at max Compatibility the charge bar fills almost immediately, making GF summons viable even in fast-paced fights

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Compatibility-Raising Items}} Using certain consumable items in the menu raises a GF's Compatibility with the current character. Most specific items give **+3.2** to the target GF but **−1.6** to every other junctioned GF. Half-value items (Arctic Wind, Bomb Fragment, Poison Powder, Shear Feather) give +1.6/−0.8 instead. Fish Fin is a further exception at +2/−1. **LuvLuv G** is the only item with no penalty — it raises every junctionable GF by +20 simultaneously and is the fastest single method to max all compatibilities. Values per use:
- Quezacotl: Dynamo Stone (+3.2) | Shiva: North Wind (+3.2), Arctic Wind (+1.6)
- Ifrit: Red Fang (+3.2), Bomb Fragment (+1.6) | Siren: Silence Powder (+3.2)
- Brothers: Dino Bone (+3.2) | Diablos: Steel Orb (+3.2)
- Carbuncle: Dragon Skin (+3.2) | Leviathan: Fish Fin (+2, special case — not the standard +3.2)
- Pandemona: Windmill (+3.2), Shear Feather (+1.6) | Cerberus: Dragon Fin (+3.2)
- Alexander: Moon Stone (+3.2) | Doomtrain: Venom Fang (+3.2), Poison Powder (+1.6)
- Bahamut: Shaman Stone (+3.2) | Cactuar: Cactus Thorn (+3.2)
- Tonberry: Chef's Knife (+3.2) | Eden: no item; summoning Eden gives +2 to Eden and +1 to every other junctioned GF
- LuvLuv G: +20 to all 16 junctionable GFs (no negative side-effect)

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|AP Spending Priorities}} Each GF unlocks abilities from a branching tree using battle-earned AP. Recommended early targets:
- **HP+20/40/80%** (any GF): passive HP expansion — unlock as early as possible
- **Card** (Quezacotl, 40 AP): enables card capture in battle and provides a useful zero-EXP route
- **T Mag-RF / I Mag-RF / F Mag-RF / L Mag-RF** (Quezacotl, Shiva, Ifrit, Siren): refine items into magic stocks
- **Enc-None** (Diablos, 60 AP): eliminates random battles — invaluable for exploration and farming efficiency
- **Move-Find** (Siren, 40 AP): reveals hidden field Draw Points and Save Points
- **Mug** (Diablos or Cactuar): steal items during battle — replaces the Attack command with a steal-and-strike
- **Auto-Haste** (Cerberus): character begins battle with Haste and also blocks Slow and Stop without using ST-Def-J

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Rival Pairs (Compatibility Penalty)}} Summoning any GF gives that GF +20 Compatibility, costs all other junctioned GFs −1.6, and costs the opposed (rival) GF an additional −10. Complete rival pairs:
- Quezacotl ↔ Leviathan | Shiva ↔ Ifrit | Siren ↔ Carbuncle
- Brothers ↔ Pandemona | Alexander ↔ Doomtrain
- Diablos, Cerberus, Bahamut, Cactuar, Tonberry, and Eden have no rival
- Minimize penalties by assigning rival GFs to separate characters so their summons don't overlap

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|GF leveling — EXP per level}} Most GFs need **500 EXP** to gain a level. Three GFs level faster: **Siren**, **Carbuncle**, and **Cerberus** each require only **400 EXP per level**. **Eden** levels much slower, requiring **1,000 EXP per level**. All GFs gain EXP from battles as long as they are junctioned to a character who participated in the fight. All GFs cap at level 100.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Damage cap exceptions}} Two GF attacks break the standard battle damage cap of 9,999: **Eden's Eternal Breath** can reach **60,000 damage** at maximum Boost; **Lv100 Cactuar's 1000 Needles** deals exactly **10,000 damage** (ignores the 9,999 cap).

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Eden — Unique Properties}} Eden is the last GF available and has unique properties compared to the others.
- Deals non-elemental magic damage regardless of the target's elemental affinities
- Draw Eden from Ultima Weapon in the Deep Sea Research Center; final chance is drawing from Tiamat in Ultimecia's Castle

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Early GF learning order}} The actionable starting-GF learning order appears in **Preparing for the Exam** and **After the Exam**, at the points when each GF joins. Use those routes for the first Card, Mag-RF, and stat targets.

{{CALLOUT:refinement|Starting-GF card routes}} The early card-to-magic and ammunition routes are listed in **Preparing for the Exam**, where Card Mod and the starting GFs first become part of the player’s choices.

| Ability | AP |
| --- | --- |
| Boost | 10 |
| T Mag-RF / I Mag-RF / F Mag-RF / L Mag-RF | 30 |
| Time Mag-RF / ST Mag-RF / Supt Mag-RF | 30 |
| Card | 40 |
| Mid Mag-RF / High Mag-RF | 60 |
| Card Mod | 80 |
| Str+20% | 60 |
| Str+40% | 120 |

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Level-gated GF abilities}} Some abilities only appear in a GF's ability list once it reaches a minimum level:
- **Shiva**: learns **Doom** and teaches the command at **Lv 10**. The Status Effects reference explains the Doom timer and its interaction with Zombie.
- **Ifrit**: learns **Ammo-RF** (refines items into ammo) at **Lv 10** — prioritize leveling Ifrit to Lv10 early for the ammo refinement chain
- **Siren**: learns **Treatment** at **Lv 12**. Unlike a normal Remedy, Treatment also removes **Zombie** and **Vit 0**. A **Med Kit** teaches Treatment to any GF (100 AP); Eden’s **GFAbl Med-RF** makes one from 100× Dragon Fangs, which Grendels can drop. This lets you put Treatment on another GF when Siren is busy or below Lv 12
- **Cerberus**: learns **Expend×2-1** (under Double status, magic costs only 1 stock instead of 2) at **Lv 30** — distinct from Expend×3-1 which only applies under Triple. Having both means a character under Double expends 1 stock per cast instead of 2, and under Triple expends 1 instead of 3. Both abilities must be equipped simultaneously to benefit from each effect. Expend×2-1 is only available from Cerberus; Expend×3-1 is taught by Three Stars items (Card Mod Squall Card or Omega Weapon drop)

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Quistis Blue Magic}} Blue Magic is Quistis’s Limit Break collection. She learns abilities by using each learning item from the Item menu outside battle. Finding or refining an item does not teach its ability; mark it learned only after using it on Quistis. Laser Eye is known by default.

The tracker below lists every ability and its learning item. Other Guide sections connect relevant pickups, Card Mod results, refinements, Drops, and Mugs to the same learned state.

White Wind heals based on Quistis's missing HP, but it instantly KOs Zombie-status allies because it counts as healing. Mighty Guard and Shockwave Pulsar are the highest-value late-game picks.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Post-Diablos card routes}} Diablos adds **Time Mag-RF** and **ST Mag-RF**; **Card Mod** still belongs to Quezacotl. For the new refinements those abilities unlock, see the contextual card-route reminder after Diablos joins in **After the Exam**.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|SumMag bonus tier items}} All four tiers stack cumulatively up to +100% total GF damage: **SumMag+10%** (40 AP) → teach item: **Steel Pipe** (Card Mod Elastoid Cards, or mug from Wendigo/Iron Giant). **SumMag+20%** (70 AP) → teach item: **Star Fragment** (mug from Iron Giant, or Card Mod 9× Iron Giant Cards for weapon use vs. GF use — prioritize weapons first). **SumMag+30%** (140 AP) → teach item: **Energy Crystal** (Card Mod 10× Elnoyle Cards, or mug from Elnoyle; **Behemoth** at Lv30+ also drops Energy Crystal — useful as an alternative source; also used for ultimate weapons and Pulse Ammo — plan supply accordingly). **SumMag+40%** (200 AP) → teach item: **Samantha Soul** (from the Quistis Card route in After the Exam or Adel’s Mug in The Final Mission; each Soul also refines into 20× Triple, so choose between the GF ability and junction stock). Equipping all four tiers on a primary GF summon character raises that GF's damage output to double its base.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Spell-casting compatibility effects}}
Casting magic in battle shifts GF Compatibility, not just summoning GFs. Habitual spell use can shape which GFs charge fastest for that character over a long playthrough.

| Spell family | Compatibility effect |
| --- | --- |
| Fire / Fira / Firaga | +Ifrit, -Shiva |
| Blizzard / Blizzara / Blizzaga | +Shiva, -Ifrit |
| Thunder / Thundara / Thundaga | +Quezacotl, -Leviathan slightly |
| Water | +Leviathan, -Quezacotl / Pandemona |
| Quake | +Brothers |
| Aero / Tornado | +Pandemona |
| Bio / Zombie / Slow / Stop / Blind / Berserk / Sleep | +Doomtrain, +Siren slightly |
| Silence | +Siren most (+1.6), +Doomtrain |
| Dispel | -Carbuncle (-1.2), -Siren (-0.8), +Cerberus slightly |
| Esuna | -Siren (-1.2), +Carbuncle and +Cerberus |
| Holy | +Alexander (+2.0), +Carbuncle, +Leviathan |
| Protect / Shell / Reflect / Aura / Haste / Double | +Carbuncle, +Cerberus |
| Triple | +Cerberus most (+2.0), +Carbuncle (+1.0) |
| Demi | +Diablos (+2.0) |
| Drain / Meltdown / Scan | No compatibility effect |

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Non-junctionable GFs}} The six non-junctionable summons are Odin, Gilgamesh, Phoenix, Chocobo, MiniMog, and Moomba. Chocobo's advanced growth, MiniMog, and Moomba use PocketStation/Chocobo World features from the original PlayStation release; those routes are not available in Remastered.

- **Odin:** Defeat Odin within the Centra Ruins timer. He may then appear at the start of eligible battles and use Zantetsuken. If obtained before the end of Disc 3, he is replaced by Gilgamesh during the Seifer battle.
- **Gilgamesh:** After replacing Odin, he may intervene during battle with one of four random attacks: Zantetsuken, Masamune, Excalibur, or the 1-damage Excalipoor.
- **Phoenix:** Use a Phoenix Pinion once to register Phoenix. It can thereafter appear when the active party is wiped out, damaging enemies and reviving the party; Phoenix Pinions can also summon it deliberately.

chapters.title: Magic Quick Reference
chapters.content:
This reference lists every spell with its exact 100-stock junction values, elemental/status junction behavior, cast effect, draw difficulty, and primary refine routes. Use the stat focus control to compare spells for a specific junction slot.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Using this reference}} Stat values assume 100 stocked spells and scale linearly with smaller stocks. Ranks in parentheses come from the spell tables and are useful for quick comparison, but the numeric value is what affects the junction. Refinement recipes stay in the Refine tab when you need a full recipe search; this page keeps each spell focused on what it does and why you would stock it.

chapters.title: Story, Lore & Music
chapters.content:
This reference collects non-mechanical context: a spoiler-controlled plot recap, a concise lore glossary, and the soundtrack list. It is meant for after-session review or for players who want context without digging through the walkthrough while they are actively playing.

{{CALLOUT:spoiler|Disc 1 plot recap}} Squall begins as a Balamb Garden cadet, earns SeeD status through the Fire Cavern and Dollet field exam, then joins the Timber mission with Zell and Selphie. The first disc introduces the resistance against Galbadia, Laguna's dream sequences, Rinoa's role with the Forest Owls, and the assassination plan in Deling City. The major reveal for active play is that Edea is not just a political figurehead; she is the sorceress driving Galbadia's escalation.

{{CALLOUT:spoiler|Disc 2 plot recap}} The party survives imprisonment, splits across the Missile Base and Balamb Garden crisis, resolves the Garden conflict, reaches Fisherman's Horizon, and sees Squall pushed into leadership. Optional open-world work becomes important after Garden is mobile. The disc builds toward Trabia's revelations and the battle between Balamb Garden and Galbadia Garden, ending with the confrontation against Edea and the first clear shift in Rinoa's condition.

{{CALLOUT:spoiler|Disc 3 plot recap}} Disc 3 explains the orphanage connection, Ellone's importance, Esthar's isolation, Laguna's past, Adel's imprisonment, the Lunar Cry, and the Ragnarok. Rinoa's sorceress status moves from mystery to central conflict. The party's goal changes from pursuing Edea to stopping Adel, Seifer, and the chain of events that makes time compression possible.

{{CALLOUT:spoiler|Disc 4 plot recap}} The final disc is the aftermath of time compression. The world is mostly locked, but the Ragnarok, portals, CC Group, and prepared sidequest state determine what can still be cleaned up. Ultimecia's Castle strips commands until bosses are defeated, then the final sequence resolves the sorceress cycle, Squall and Rinoa's promise, and Laguna's memories.

chapters.title: Preparing for the Exam
chapters.content:
After the opening cinematic, Squall wakes in the Garden infirmary. Dr. Kadowaki asks a question - answer freely, because the choice only changes dialogue. Name Squall when prompted, watch the classroom scenes, then take control at Squall's desk.

Squall begins at **Lv 7** with the Revolver gunblade. Starting inventory: **5,000 Gil** · **6× Potion** · **4× Phoenix Down** · **2× Remedy** · **5× Tent**.

{{CALLOUT:perfect|Perfect Game Alert #1}} Decide before moving whether this save is aiming for a perfect-game file. FFVIII tracks character KOs and escaped battles; a perfect file keeps every character at **0 KOs** and finishes with exactly **one escaped battle**, because a later battle forces an escape. Keep levels low when practical until stronger level-management tools arrive, but do not paralyze the route - learning early GF abilities matters more than avoiding every point of EXP. Missable-item alerts also apply to perfect files.

Once back in the classroom, **examine the desk in front of Squall** and choose "Turn on the power and...", then open **Tutorial**. This awards **Quezacotl** (GF 1/16) and **Shiva** (GF 2/16). Leave the tutorial/computer, junction one of them to Squall, and equip **Draw**, **GF**, and **Item** so Draw Points are usable during the first Garden circuit. Set the initial GF priorities now: **Quezacotl -> Card** and **Shiva -> I Mag-RF**. The default learning order wastes early AP.

Speak with Quistis to advance, then walk down the second-floor hallway. A late student bumps into Squall; agreeing to the tour is useful for orientation and has no penalty beyond tiny later dialogue changes. In the elevator hallway, **talk to the student near the elevator** to receive the starter card set: **Geezard**, **Funguar**, **Red Bat**, **Gayla**, **Gesper**, **Fastitacalon-F**, and **Caterchipillar**. Take the elevator down to 1F.

{{CALLOUT:achievement|Card Player}} If **Card Player** is still unearned, challenge any Garden student who accepts a match; you do not need to win.

{{CALLOUT:point|Balamb Garden orientation}} Balamb Garden is arranged like a wheel: the **Lobby Hall** circles the elevator, and spokes lead to the **Cafeteria** (northwest), **Dormitory** (north), **Parking Lot** (northeast), **Training Center** (east), **Library** (southeast), **Front Gate** (south), **Infirmary** (southwest), and **Quad** (west). The directory near the entrance can warp Squall directly to a facility once the option is available.

{{CALLOUT:relationship|Zell Love Quest #1}} On this first Garden circuit, visit the **Library** and speak to the **Library Girl with the pigtail**. The scene is understated, but it affects the ending path of Zell's Library sidequest. Draw **Esuna** from the Draw Point just inside the Library, then examine the second bookshelf, nearest the aisle, to collect **Occult Fan I** (1/4).

Save near the directory, then head to the **Front Gate**. Use the **Cure Draw Point** on the left side of the outer gate area; it counts toward **Magic Miner**. Continue south to Quistis, who gives the junction tutorial and joins the party. Junction **Quezacotl** to Squall and **Shiva** to Quistis, then equip both characters with **Draw**, **GF**, and **Item** commands. Save card matches until after the Fire Cavern; the Ifrit Card gives you a stronger opening hand.

{{ENCOUNTERS:0}}

Before the Fire Cavern, save on the world map. The stone road is encounter-free, but the nearby forests can produce a **T-Rexaur**. If one appears, normal files can escape; perfect-game files should reset from the save or try to survive with GF summons. If you need early junction stock, draw a modest amount from Bite Bugs, Glacial Eyes, and Caterchipillars before heading east to the Fire Cavern. Use Squall's gunblade trigger action on attack impact for the 50% damage bonus; the exact input depends on platform.

{{ENCOUNTERS:2}}

Enter the Fire Cavern. Quistis explains magic junctioning and gunblade settings on the approach. Choose the **10-minute** limit; it is enough, and finishing close to zero improves the later Judgment score. All regular Fire Cavern enemies are fixed **Lv 5**, regardless of party level. Use physical attacks for Buel and Red Bat, consider Shiva only for multiple Bombs, and do not spend timer time drawing. Ignore the Fire draw point on the way in - the timer disappears after Ifrit, and the backtrack is the better time to draw.

**Boss: Ifrit** (Lv 6) — HP: 1,068 | AP: 20 | EXP: 0
- Draw: Fire, Cure, Scan
- Mug: Nothing (0% overall chance)
- Drop: 3x G-Returner (69.5%); 4x G-Returner (19.9%); 5x G-Returner (5.9%); 6x G-Returner (4.7%)
- Card drop: Ifrit Card (100%)
- Gravity: Vulnerable
- Weakness: Ice
- Absorb: Fire
- Status weak: The End

Strategy: Ifrit is fixed at Lv 6 and does not scale with the party. He casts Fire on one character or uses Jump Punch for roughly 100 damage. Have Quistis summon **Shiva** while Squall attacks physically; use Limit Breaks if they appear. If either character falls below 100 HP, draw **Cure** from Ifrit and cast it immediately. Ifrit also carries **Scan** if you want the spell recorded early. **G-Returner revives a KO'd GF**, so the drop is useful even though this fight is simple. Do not reset for a larger G-Returner drop - the minimum three is already enough, and the Ifrit Card is guaranteed.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|SeeD Rank timer tip}} When Ifrit's naming screen appears, aim to leave the cavern with the timer as close to zero as possible. On original PSX, idling at the naming screen can let the hidden timer reach zero safely. On Steam/Remaster, track the time yourself and leave the naming screen between **0:00 and 0:03**; the original idle trick does not behave the same way.

After Ifrit joins, junction him to Squall and put your best Strength magic on Squall. Recommended GF Learning order: Quezacotl learns Card Mod after Card, Shiva learns Str-J after I Mag-RF, and Ifrit learns F Mag-RF. The timer is gone, so draw from the Fire Draw Point on your way out. Return to Balamb Garden; Quistis gives the GF ability/HP tutorial and leaves the party.

{{ENCOUNTERS:1}}

{{CALLOUT:card|Pre-exam card setup - Queen of Cards and trade rules}} Before serious card farming, detour to **Balamb Town** after Ifrit. On this first visit, collect the Balamb **Timber Maniacs** issue from the upstairs hotel guest room before boarding for Dollet; this is its earliest opportunity. The later hotel and station copies are alternatives, so take only one. Then find the Queen of Cards by the train station. Set the local trade rule to **Diff** before farming: strong wins can earn multiple cards, while Direct risks taking one of your cards. Save first, then challenge the Queen. If the opening rules do not show Diff, quit without playing and challenge her again. If they do, play and win, then check with a local player such as the train conductor that Diff has spread. If it has not, reload and repeat the Queen match. Once it is active, farm in Balamb and avoid carrying unwanted rules into another region. If Diff later slips back to One, reset it with the Queen while she is still in Balamb.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Balamb Beach AP farming}} The beach south of Balamb Town is the best early AP stop because **Fastitocalon-F** often appear in pairs, making a quick **6 AP** battle; their Fish Fins feed the Water route below. Junction Thunder to Elem-Atk if available. If you want to limit EXP, finish enemies with Quezacotl's **Card** command, though this slows the grind. Use AP on the next targets in the GF learn order below, then move on; do not camp here solely for **Mid Mag-RF** or **Ammo-RF**.

Fish Fins refine via **I Mag-RF** into **20× Water** each. Do not waste turns trying to draw Water from Fastitocalon-F here - at this level they do not carry it. Water is excellent early junction filler, especially before stronger card-mod magic is ready.

{{CALLOUT:card|Rare cards available now}} With the Ifrit Card and the Diff trade rule, build a real deck. Win the **Quistis Card** from the Trepe Groupies in the 2F classroom or Cafeteria; this should be the first rare-card target because it is powerful in play. Win the **MiniMog Card** from the boy running laps around the lower-level Garden hallway. MiniMog is weak as a playing card, but do **not** mod it - it is needed for a later Queen of Cards step. Do not mod the **Ifrit Card** either; it is both a strong playing card and required for a later rare-card trade.

{{CALLOUT:achievement|Loser — optional}} **Loser** requires losing a rare card in Triple Triad. If you still need it, surrender the newly earned **Ifrit Card** to a Trepe Groupie. This gives up a strong card needed later, so you can wait and lose another eligible rare card instead. If an ordinary NPC takes one of your rare cards, that player keeps it until you win it back. Queen of Cards losses pass to her son when the replacement card is created; the first Ifrit loss to General Caraway passes it to Martine; and the Disc 4 CC Group can redistribute rare cards you do not own.

{{CALLOUT:refinement|Card Mod routes to Quistis Blue Magic items and other uses}}
- Gesper Card -> Black Hole
- 4× Malboro Card -> Malboro Tentacle
- 10× Ruby Dragon Card -> Inferno Fang
- 10× Behemoth Card -> Barrier
- SAM08G Card -> Running Fire
- Fastitocalon Card -> Water Crystal
- Creeps Card -> Coral Fragment
- Gayla Card -> Mystery Fluid
- Tri-Face Card → Curse Spike
- Caterchipillar Card -> Spider Web
- Elastoid Card -> Steel Pipe
- Geezard Card -> Screw -> 8 Normal Ammo
 Degenerator is the standout because it ejects almost every regular non-boss enemy for the whole game.
Steel Pipes teach **SumMag+10%** and unlock **SumMag+20%** on a GF, and spare pipes have later weapon and GF-quest uses. Do not grind Elastoid Cards at the expense of the exam route, but keep and mod any extras that fall into your hand.
**Normal Ammo** is used by a future party member.

{{CALLOUT:refinement|Early magic refinement targets}} Implementing these refinements for junctioning stats can very quickly make your party overpowered in the early-game. Utilize this in a way that allows you to still enjoy the game.
- 10x Ruby Dragon Card -> Inferno Fang -> 20x Flare
- Abyss Worm Card -> Windmill -> 20× Tornado
- Snow Lion Card -> North Wind -> 20× Blizzaga
- Blitz Card -> Dynamo Stone -> 20× Thundaga
- 3× Hexadragon Card -> Red Fang -> 20× Firaga
- Thrustaevis Card -> Shear Feather -> 20× Aero
- Bomb Card -> Bomb Fragment -> 20× Fira
- Glacial Eye Card -> Arctic Wind -> 20× Blizzara
- Creeps Card -> Coral Fragment -> 20x Thundara
- Fastitocalon Card -> Water Crystal -> 50x Water

{{CALLOUT:card|Who to play for common cards}} These level ranges describe each Garden player's card pool, not a guaranteed hand each game. In the 2F hallway, let the students finish their conversation before challenging them.

**Regular Garden players**
- **Lobby:** The student running laps plays Levels 1–3; the student at Reception, by the in/out doors, plays Levels 1–3 and 5.
- **Library:** The male player on the first screen plays Levels 1 and 3–5; the female player on the second screen plays Levels 1–5.
- **Infirmary:** Dr. Kadowaki plays Levels 1–5.
- **Cafeteria:** The Cafeteria Lady plays Levels 1–2 and 4–5; Trepe Groupie #1 plays Levels 2 and 5.
- **Classroom:** Trepe Groupie #2 plays Levels 1, 3, and 5; Trepe Groupie #3 plays Levels 1–2 and 5.
- **Other fixed players:** Trepe Groupie #1’s friend plays Levels 1–3; Cid plays Levels 1, 3, and 5.

**Players who appear randomly**
- **2F hallway:** The black-haired girl plays Levels 1 and 3–4; the brunette plays Levels 2–3 and 5; her brother plays Levels 2–4. Either the two girls or the black-haired girl and her brother may appear; let their conversation finish first.
- **Lobby:** The boy in a brown shirt plays Levels 1–2; the SeeD walking north plays Levels 1–3.
- **Other roamers:** The player on the bench outside the Library plays Levels 1–3; the yellow-jacket student near the exit plays Levels 1–4.

Trepe Groupie #1 is a reliable Level 5 target because his card pool is limited; the second-screen Library player also uses Level 5 cards regularly. No currently accessible Garden player uses Level 6 or 7 cards, and PuPu is not normally played.

{{CALLOUT:sidequest|Novice SeeD Candidates quest}} This five-window sidequest rewards scenes rather than items. Speak to the three students at the Balamb Garden Cafeteria table until their dialogue repeats. Do this now, before the SeeD Exam. The later windows are: after the exam but before leaving for Timber; after visiting Balamb Garden's MD Level but before Fisherman's Horizon; any time on Disc 2 after visiting Fisherman's Horizon; and on Disc 3 before the Trabia Canyon sequence. Complete all five windows and return after Trabia Canyon to see them as full SeeDs; otherwise, they disappear for the rest of the game.

In the Cafeteria, talk to the **Cafeteria Lady** until she stops giving new dialogue; this minor dialogue chain appears to close later. Then return to the Library.

{{CALLOUT:relationship|Zell Love Quest #2}} Speak to the **Conceited SeeD** in the Library. He can fail to appear; if he is missing, do not reset the route just for him, because later opportunities exist.

{{CALLOUT:card|CC Group prerequisite — wins that count later}} The CC Group quest cannot begin until Disc 2 or 3, but you can work toward its prerequisite now. You need at least **15 Triple Triad wins in Balamb Garden**; games in the Cafeteria, Library, and 2F Classroom do **not** count. When the quest becomes available, Jack appears in the main hall. Joker is encountered later on the Training Center bridge, not in a classroom.

{{CALLOUT:perfect|Perfect Game Alert #2}} Before moving on, perfect-game files should get **100× Tornado** (or **100× Flare**, if you are willing to grind the cards) and junction it to Squall's **Strength**. Other magic stocks are flexible here; this Strength benchmark is the important preparation for an upcoming score-sensitive task.
