chapters.title: The SeeD Exam
chapters.content:
{{CALLOUT:point|Exam briefing}} Return to Balamb Garden and change into the SeeD uniform in the **Dormitory**. Rest in the bed first if HP is low. In the main hall, the forced briefing scene does not count as speaking to someone, so let it play normally. Set **Config -> Cursor -> Memory** before leaving so repeated Draw commands are much faster during the mission.

{{CALLOUT:warning|Exam scoring discipline}} From this point until the exam ends, do **not** speak to anyone unless the walkthrough explicitly tells you to. Unnecessary conversations reduce the exam score, even when the person seems harmless. Do not talk to Quistis or Cid after the briefing. Drive the car to Balamb Harbor, board the vessel, and when prompted during the briefing choose **Do nothing**. When Seifer orders Squall to look outside, obey him to continue without a penalty.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Party setup on the beach}} Junction before fighting. Give Shiva to Zell and Quezacotl to Seifer, then use Switch/Junction Exchange to move magic off Quistis and onto the active party. Seifer uses a gunblade and can use the same trigger action as Squall, but his Hyperion timing window is tighter. Speaking to Seifer or Zell is safe from here; speaking to other people still risks deductions. If you need more junction stock, refine Fish Fins or other spare items before moving into town.

{{ENCOUNTERS:0}}

Climb the stairs and use the Save Point before entering Dollet. The first fixed battle is two G-Soldiers; draw Cure stock if needed, then finish them. Continue through town without entering the shop or talking to the Garden students who exit the pub. Defeat the G-Soldiers in the street, the central square, and the truck-blocked checkpoint. Do **not** take the upper-left street out of town yet because it causes an exam deduction.

At the truck checkpoint, speak to Seifer twice for the required scene. When the camera changes, speak to Zell first, then Seifer, then walk away and re-approach Seifer for the next scene. Follow Seifer toward the communications tower. On the mountain road, do not speak to wounded Dollet soldiers. A fixed Anacondaur ambush occurs after the bridge; for a perfect record, make sure Seifer does not land the killing blow.

When Selphie appears, do **not** jump from the cliff. Take the path around to the tower base; jumping causes a major exam deduction. Seifer leaves the party here, and the magic and GF he was carrying transfer to Selphie. Recheck Selphie's junctions immediately. At the tower base, save, draw **Blind** from the draw point, and make sure at least one character has the **Draw** command equipped. Missing Draw here can cost a GF.

{{CALLOUT:point|Tower battle setup}} At the top of the communications tower, Biggs and Wedge open the fight before Elvoret interrupts. They have a one-time mid-fight scene if Biggs survives long enough; if you want to see it, avoid finishing the battle too soon.

**Boss: Biggs** (Lv 1-10) - HP: 467-705 | AP: 4 | EXP: 0
- Draw: Fire, Thunder, Blizzard, Esuna
- Drop: 2x Elixir (100%)
- Card drop: Nothing
- Gravity: Vulnerable
- Weakness: None
- Resist: None
- Status weak: The End

**Boss: Wedge** (Lv 1-10) - HP: 416-640 | AP: 4 | EXP: 0
- Draw: Fire, Thunder, Blizzard, Cure
- Drop: 2x Cottage (100%)
- Card drop: Nothing
- Gravity: Vulnerable
- Weakness: None
- Resist: None
- Status weak: The End

Strategy: The battle ends as soon as either soldier is defeated; prioritize Biggs for his stronger reward.

{{CALLOUT:missable|Missable now — Draw Siren from Elvoret}} Draw **Siren** from Elvoret before finishing the fight. Missing her here leaves only a much later Disc 4 fallback from Tri-Point in Ultimecia's Castle, so treat this as the practical opportunity.

**Boss: Elvoret** (Lv 1-11) - HP: 1,563-3,523 | AP: 10 | EXP: 0
- Draw: Thunder, Cure, Double, Siren
- Drop: 3x G-Returner (69.5%), 4x G-Returner (19.9%), 5x G-Returner (5.9%), 6x G-Returner (4.7%), Weapons Monthly March Issue (100%)
- Card drop: Nothing
- Gravity: Vulnerable
- Weakness: None
- Resist: Flying and Poison nullified
- Status weak: Confuse (90%), Darkness (60%), Drain, Slow (90%), The End

Strategy: Elvoret has no elemental weakness and its offense is dangerous. **Storm Breath** hits all party members for heavy non-elemental damage; its physical attack also hurts more than its Fire/Thunder casting. If you are drawing spells before ending the fight, inflict Darkness from the Blind draw point to reduce its physical accuracy. Slow and Confuse also have high success rates. Prioritize **Siren**, then stock Double and Thunder as time allows.

With Siren acquired, Double is an excellent early junction spell. Elvoret guarantees **Weapons Monthly March Issue**, so the magazine is secured when the battle ends.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Siren setup during the timer}} After Elvoret falls, name Siren and the **30-minute countdown** begins. Do **not** speak to Biggs. Ride the elevator down, save quickly at the tower base if desired, and junction Siren immediately. A strong learn order is **L Mag-RF -> Tool-RF -> Mag+% abilities -> Mag Bonus -> Move-Find -> ST Med-RF -> Boost -> junction abilities -> remaining abilities**. The timer continues in menus, so make changes cleanly and move.

{{CALLOUT:refinement|Elvoret Card refinement}} If you have an **Elvoret Card**, Card Mod it into a Death Stone, then use Siren’s L Mag-RF to refine the stone into **10 Death**. Death is a strong St.Atk-J spell.

Exit the tower and begin the X-ATM092 escape. The first X-ATM092 encounter is scripted; knock it down once, then escape when the game permits. It will chase you again later.

**Boss: X-ATM092** (Lv 1-11) - HP: 5,072-5,872 | AP: 50 | EXP: 0
- Draw: Fire, Blizzard, Cure, Protect
- Drop: Power Wrist (25%), Orihalcon (25%), Hypno Crown (25%), Force Armlet (25%)
- Card drop: Nothing
- Weakness: Lightning x1.5
- Resist: Poison nullified
- Status weak: The End

Strategy: Use Lightning attacks as your main damage. X-ATM092 uses Clash on the full party, Arm Crush on one target, and Ray-Bomb as heavy non-elemental damage. Protect helps blunt its physical attacks; Shell reduces Ray-Bomb. After losing roughly 20% of its max HP, it collapses and begins repairing. To earn its 50 AP, deplete all of its HP once, let it recover, then knock it down a second time and escape. Keep attacking through the repair cycle if you want to destroy it and claim an item drop.

{{CALLOUT:point|Dodging route}} To evade X-ATM092, run until the screen after Selphie jumps from the cliff. On the cracked-road screen, use the walk action; running makes the ground slam knock Squall down. On the bridge, let X-ATM092 leap over, run left, let it leap again, then run right into town. In the square, examine the dog to move it out of danger if the machine is still chasing you. For a perfect-game file, destroy X-ATM092 before entering the town screen with the shop. Do **not** enter the cafe or hide in the pub; ignore the beach save point and head straight to the vessel.

Each possible item drop teaches a GF a +40% stat ability.

chapters.title: After the Exam
chapters.content:
{{CALLOUT:point|After-exam freedom}} After the Dollet return scenes, Quistis dismisses the party in Balamb Town and the exam is over. Conversation penalties no longer apply, so it is safe to talk to people again. The exact scene flow depends on whether X-ATM092 was destroyed and whether Squall hid in the pub during the escape.

{{CALLOUT:missable|Timber Maniacs - Balamb fallback}} If you did not take the Balamb **Timber Maniacs** issue before the Dollet mission, collect it now: after staying the night, check the upstairs Hotel guest room, or inspect the train station. These are alternate locations for the same issue; taking one prevents collecting the other. The Hotel copy was available before the exam, so use this as the cleanup window if you missed it.

{{CALLOUT:card|Zell Card}} Visit the Dincht house near Balamb Town's central intersection and challenge Ma Dincht to cards for the **Zell Card**. Keep Zell in the active party so his mother offers it. The rare card may take several games to appear; if she will not play or the game does not start, leave and re-enter. Once won, return to Balamb Garden by following the road to avoid random encounters.

{{CALLOUT:achievement|Handyman — early Junk Shop chance}} Balamb Town has a **Junk Shop** one screen west of the Dincht house. If you already have enough materials for any weapon, choose **Remodel** to earn Steam's **Handyman** achievement. A Weapons Monthly issue is not required for a recipe to appear once you have its materials; the Weapons reference lists the ingredients. If you are short on materials, continue the story and try a later Junk Shop instead of grinding here.

{{CALLOUT:hint|Do not grind the beach yet}} It is tempting to farm AP on the beach for Siren, but a better opportunity is coming very soon. Return to Garden and keep the story moving.

In Balamb Garden's main hall, approach Cid, Quistis, and Xu for the post-exam scene. Go to the right hallway and speak to Seifer, then return to the main hall directory to receive the 2F Hallway instruction. On the 2F Hallway, talk to Raijin, Fujin, Zell, and the unnamed boy on the right side; the other unnamed students can be ignored. Try to leave, let the scene play, then speak to Cid again for the **Battle Meter**. Take the elevator down and head to the classroom to receive the SeeD score and salary explanation.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|SeeD score and tests}} The score screen breaks the exam into Conduct, Judgment, Attack, Spirit, Deduction, and Bonus categories. Detailed scoring tables and salary ranks live in the **SeeD Rank & Salary** reference page. Once your SeeD rank is awarded, written tests are available from **Menu → Tutorial → TEST**; each passed test raises SeeD Exp to the next rank threshold, and the highest test you can take is capped by Squall's level. They are a useful rank and salary tool as more tests unlock.

Back in the dormitory, change into the SeeD uniform, then speak to Selphie outside to begin the graduation party. When Selphie asks, answer **Yeah, I guess so.** After the balcony scenes, Squall returns to the dormitory. Change back into normal clothes and head to the Training Center with Quistis.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Training Center junction setup}} If Siren was drawn from Elvoret, Quistis gives the Status Junction tutorial here. Put Quezacotl and Ifrit on Squall, and Shiva and Siren on Quistis. Use Switch/Junction Exchange to move Zell's magic onto Quistis quickly. Junction Ice magic to Elem-Atk before entering the Training Center.

{{ENCOUNTERS:0}}

Grat is the immediate source for status magic because ST Mag-RF is not available yet. At the party's normal low level, draw **Sleep** and **Silence** from Grat, then junction Sleep to ST-Atk. Berserk enters Grat's draw list at Lv 20 and Confuse at Lv 30, so they will not normally be available here. If T-Rexaur appears early, run unless you are prepared; Quistis can one-shot it with Degenerator if her Limit Break is available, but normal attacks are risky and physical hits wake a sleeping T-Rexaur.

At the first Training Center fork, either direction is fine. While following the north path, collect the visible **Blizzard Draw Point** before continuing through the loop. When Quistis says you have reached the secret area, enter for the scene, then leave by either route. A distress scene triggers the boss battle near the exit.

**Boss: Granaldo** (fixed encounter Lv 1-11) - HP: 1,314-1,538 | AP: 5 | EXP: 0
- Draw: Sleep, Blind, Shell
- Drop: 4x Wizard Stone (100%)
- Card drop: Nothing
- LV Up/Down: Yes
- Gravity: Vulnerable
- Weakness: Wind
- Resist: Flying
- Status weak: Doom (40%), Drain, Eject, KO (10%), Poison (40%), Sleep (40%), Slow (90%), Stop (10%), The End

**Boss: Raldo** (fixed encounter Lv 1-11) - HP: 111-287 | AP: 3 each | EXP: 0
- Draw: Fire, Thunder, Protect
- Drop: 4x Wizard Stone (100%)
- Card drop: Nothing
- LV Up/Down: Yes
- Gravity: Vulnerable
- Weakness: None
- Resist: None
- Status weak: Darkness (40%), Doom (40%), Drain, Eject, KO (20%), Poison (40%), Sleep (40%), Slow (90%), Stop (10%), The End

Strategy: Defeat the Raldos first to remove Granaldo's strongest throw attacks. Granaldo is vulnerable to Sleep, Slow, Poison, and Gravity; Sleep plus magic or Limit Breaks keeps the fight controlled.

After the battle, return to the dormitory. The next morning, Squall has a private room; collect the **Weapons Monthly April Issue** from the desk before leaving. Then head to the Front Gate for the Timber mission briefing.

{{CALLOUT:missable|Cid before Timber}} At the Front Gate mission briefing, do **not** leave the screen when it ends: speak to **Cid** again to receive the **Magical Lamp**. Then visit Cid's 3F office before boarding the Timber train; he will supply the Lamp or **Battle Meter** if either was missed. This is the last window for both items. Challenge Cid there for the **Seifer Card**, a strong rare card. If you skip it now, you can play Cid for it again at Edea's House on Disc 3, so this is a convenient no-backtracking opportunity rather than a permanent cutoff.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Magical Lamp setup}} If fighting Diablos immediately, use a balanced setup: Ifrit on Squall, Quezacotl and Shiva on Zell, and Siren on Selphie. Junction Blind to Selphie's ST-Atk if you stocked it from the Dollet tower or Granaldo. Rest, save, then use the Magical Lamp from the item menu.

**Boss: Diablos** (Lv 1-100) - HP: 1,600-80,800 | AP: 20 | EXP: 0
- Draw: Lv 1-19: Cure, Demi | Lv 20-29: Cura, Demi | Lv 30+: Curaga, Demi, Holy, Flare
- Mug: Nothing (0%)
- Drop: Lv 1-29: 8x G-Returner | Lv 30+: 4x Hero
- Card drop: Diablos (100%)
- Gravity: Vulnerable
- Weakness: Wind x1.5
- Resist: None
- Status weak: Darkness (50%), Drain, Slow (90%), The End

Strategy: Open by inflicting Blind; it nearly removes Diablos' physical threat. Demi and Gravija are percentage-based and cannot kill by themselves, so they set up low-HP Limit Breaks without ending the run. Draw Demi, and at Lv 30+ stock Holy and Flare because they are excellent junction spells. Diablos is weak to Wind and vulnerable to Slow. Finish with Squall, Zell, and Selphie Limit Breaks once HP is low.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Diablos ability order}} After the fight, name the GF and learn Diablos abilities in this order: **ST Mag-RF -> Time Mag-RF -> Enc-Half -> Enc-None -> Mug -> junction abilities -> everything else**. Enc-Half reduces random encounter frequency by exactly 50%; Enc-None is invaluable when drawing, carding, or Mug farming is complete. Mug unlocks steal data shown throughout later enemy cards.

{{CALLOUT:refinement|Card refinements after Diablos}} Diablos adds **Time Mag-RF** and **ST Mag-RF**. Once Quezacotl has learned **Card Mod**, these extra routes become available:
- **Quistis Card** → 3 Samantha Souls → **60 Triple total** through Time Mag-RF (20 per Soul), or save a Soul to teach a GF **SumMag+40%**.
- **Gayla Card** → Mystery Fluid → **10 Meltdown** through ST Mag-RF if you do not need the Acid Blue Magic route.
- **Caterchipillar Card** → Spider Web → **20 Slow** through ST Mag-RF if you do not need the Ultra Waves Blue Magic route.
- **Mesmerize Card** → Mesmerize Blade → **Regen** through L Mag-RF.

{{CALLOUT:refinement|Healing Water route}} Now that Diablos teaches **Mug**, an optional trip back to Dollet can stock healing items: Jelleye can be mugged for Healing Water. Tool-RF converts each Healing Water into **2 Tents**; Recov Med-RF converts it into **2 Hi-Potions**. A Tent restores party HP in the field and cures Poison, Petrify, Darkness, Silence, Zombie, and KO, but not Berserk, Sleep, Slow, Stop, Curse, Confuse, Vit 0, or Doom.

{{CALLOUT:sidequest|Start the Queen of Cards quest before Timber}} If you want to advance the rare-card quest now, save in the Balamb Hotel, then challenge the Queen at the **train station** and lose **MiniMog** to her. Speak to her afterward and note the town she names. Aim to send her to **Dollet**; if she announces Galbadia/Deling City, reload before the loss. If reloading keeps the same result, play and quit a local game to change the sequence, save, and try again. Do not mod MiniMog before this step. The card you surrender is held by the Queen's son once the replacement card is created, so plan to win it back from him later. Then board the train to Timber when ready.

checkpoints.label: Diablos
checkpoints.description: Unlock Guardian Force Diablos. Use the Magical Lamp (received from Cid after graduation) to trigger the Diablos battle. Save beforehand; cast Demi twice to reduce its HP, then defeat it.

checkpoints.label: First Salary
checkpoints.description: Receive the first SeeD salary. Awarded automatically after the Training Center incident and the return to the dormitory.

checkpoints.label: Battle Meter, Magical Lamp
checkpoints.description: Obtain both items from Cid before boarding the train to Timber. (Diablos can be obtained at any point in the game so long as you have the Magical Lamp.)

checkpoints.label: Handyman
checkpoints.description: Upgrade any weapon at Balamb Town’s Junk Shop if the materials are available. This is an early opportunity; Deling City and later Junk Shops remain alternatives.

enemies.name: Grat
enemies.notes: Before ST Mag-RF is available, fill status-magic stocks here; Sleep helps keep T-Rexaurs under control.

chapters.title: The Timber Mission
chapters.content:
{{CALLOUT:relationship|Zell Love Quest and novice candidates}} Before boarding the train, return to the Library and talk to the Library Girl again for the **Good-bye Pururun** conversation with Zell. This must be done before the Timber departure. Also visit the Cafeteria and speak to the three Novice SeeD Candidates for their second dialogue window.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Mission preparation checklist}} Before leaving Balamb Garden, confirm you collected **Weapons Monthly April**, received the **Magical Lamp**, obtained Diablos, and challenged Cid for the **Seifer Card**. If you want a long-term Stat Bonus route, continue the earlier GF plan until Siren learns **Mag Bonus** and Diablos learns **Enc-Half** and his key refinement abilities. Otherwise, stop once the core refinement tools are learned and keep moving.

{{ENCOUNTERS:0}}

Board the train. Follow Selphie and Zell into the hallway, keep speaking to Selphie until she says she will meet you in the cabin, then enter the cabin and speak to Zell. Speak to Zell in the cabin to receive **Pet Pals Vol. 1** automatically. When asked about Timber, answer **Not too much**. The party then enters the first Laguna dream.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Laguna dream transfer rules}} Squall, Zell, and Selphie become Laguna, Kiros, and Ward. Junctions, stocked magic, items, levels, EXP, and stat growth transfer between the associated characters. Laguna inherits Squall's junctions, Kiros inherits Zell's, and Ward inherits Selphie's. Laguna has a separate 3,000 Gil stash during the dream, normal SeeD salary does not pay out, and weapons remain character-specific. Quistis cannot learn Blue Magic during the dream, but Blue Magic items found there remain usable afterward.

{{ENCOUNTERS:1}}

Follow the linear Timber Forest path. Funguar can provide status magic if you did not refine much from cards. There is a **Cure draw point** on the second forest screen and a **Water draw point** near the truck. Enter the truck to reach Deling City. In Deling City, ignore the sewers unless you deliberately want pointless encounters, go to the Galbadia Hotel, head downstairs, and choose **Let's take a load off**. The other options are optional flavor. Approach the piano, return to the table, then speak to the receptionist for Julia's room.

Back in Timber, approach the man by the stairs where Squall got off the train. Answer **But the Owls are still around** to proceed; the souvenir kiosk to the right is an optional stop for local hints. Follow the contact to the Forest Owls train and save in the next car before doing anything else.

{{CALLOUT:card|Watts and Angelo Card}} Before starting the operation, challenge Watts to Triple Triad. If the rule-mixing prompt appears, try to spread **Open** to Galbadia while keeping **Same** in the region; reload if Same is abolished or Watts stops offering rule mixing. Win the **Angelo Card** now, because Watts will not be available for another long stretch. After the game, go to the rear cabin, meet Rinoa and Angelo, and complete the Combine tutorial. Return to the group for Zone’s briefing; inspect the board nearby for optional Anarchist Monthly clippings about the President. Save before speaking to Watts to launch the mission. Angelo Card can be Card Modded into **100x Elixir**, but that consumes the rare card; keep it if you want the full collection, or plan to recover it later.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Forest Owls train mission}} Save before talking to Watts to begin. The operation has seven phases and a strict **5-minute** timer; running out is Game Over. Phase 1: climb onto the 2nd escort car. Phase 2: sneak across the roof; move only while the red guard scans below, stop when the blue guard scans, and remember that closed blinds mean neither guard is scanning. Phase 3: cross the President car roof. Phase 4: descend by rope and enter three correct 4-code sequences to uncouple the first escort car. Phase 5: watch the dummy/base car movement. Phase 6: descend again and enter five correct 4-code sequences to uncouple the second escort car. Phase 7: escape. The code-entry prompts use the four face-button positions; use the Controls page for your selected platform mapping rather than memorizing PlayStation labels.
| Times Caught | SeeD Rank Change |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | +1 |
| 1-9 | 0 |
| 10+ | -1 |

{{CALLOUT:warning|Train mission retries}} If caught, choosing to try again counts as being caught. Declining the retry gives Game Over, which can be useful if you want to reload and preserve the 0-catch rank bonus. Wrong inputs or timeouts during a code sequence clear that sequence but do not count as being caught.

After the train mission, the game opens the menu. Re-check every junction: Zell and Selphie can lose GF assignments after the dream/mission swap, so re-equip Quezacotl/Shiva/Siren and restock commands. Junction Fire or Earth to Elem-Atk and Slow to ST-Atk if available. Keep **Draw** available to collect Gerogero’s useful spells, and equip **Item** so you can use an Elixir or X-Potion against the undead boss. A Phoenix Down can also defeat it, but only sometimes. If commands are tight, remove Mug for this fight. Grab **Pet Pals Vol. 2** from Rinoa's bed/bench, save, then speak to Rinoa and say you are ready.

**Boss: Fake President** (Lv 1-12) - HP: 58-778 | AP: 0 | EXP: 0
- Draw: Cure
- Mug: Nothing (0%)
- Drop: Nothing (0%)
- Card drop: Nothing
- Gravity: Vulnerable
- Weakness: None
- Resist: None
- Status weak: Slow (90%), The End

**Boss: Gerogero** (Lv 1-12) - HP: 350-3,650 | AP: 20 | EXP: 0
- Draw: Esuna, Double, Berserk, Zombie
- Mug: 2x Phoenix Down (50%)
- Drop: 8x Zombie Powder (100%)
- Card drop: Nothing
- Undead: Yes
- Gravity: Vulnerable
- Weakness: Fire x3, Earth x3, Holy x3
- Resist: Poison nullified
- Status weak: Slow (90%)

Strategy: The Fake President is a short first phase. Gerogero is undead. An **Elixir** or **X-Potion** kills it immediately; a **Phoenix Down** has only a 25% chance to do so, while restorative magic such as Curaga deals damage rather than guaranteeing an instant kill. Before finishing, draw **Esuna**, **Double**, **Berserk**, and **Zombie**. Physical attacks are poor; use healing items/magic or exploit Fire, Earth, and Holy weakness. Gerogero's **Brrawghh!** can inflict Curse, Darkness, and Slow, so cure Curse quickly because it blocks Limit Break access.

After the boss, Rinoa must join the party. Swapping her in for Selphie is the cleanest route, but immediately move junctions and magic so the active party remains functional. Speak to Watts when ready to return to Timber.

{{CALLOUT:shop|Timber Pet Shop and town services}} Visit the Pet Shop beside the station stairs first. Buy **Pet Pals Vol. 3** and **Pet Pals Vol. 4** if you plan to train Angelo’s remaining abilities; it also sells **Amnesia Greens** and command scrolls for **5,000 Gil each**: Magic Scroll, GF Scroll, Draw Scroll, and Item Scroll. With Tonberry’s Familiar later, it adds **HP-J**, **Str-J**, **Vit-J**, **Mag-J**, and **Spr-J Scrolls** for **10,000 Gil each**. Pet Pals Vol. 5 and Vol. 6 are later Esthar purchases and unlock Angelo Search and Wishing Star. The Timber Junk Shop is farther down the street near the Hotel; check its remodeling list if you already have weapon materials. The general Item Shop is by the Pub if you need supplies. Leave enough Gil for later train fare.

{{CALLOUT:missable|Angelo Recover and Reverse}} Do **not** teach Rinoa **Angelo Recover** or **Angelo Reverse** until after Angelo Search farming is finished much later. Recover and Reverse trigger automatically and can interrupt idle Angelo Search setups. Pet Pals Vol. 1 teaches Angelo Strike after 800 steps. Vol. 2 teaches Angelo Recover after 200 steps. Read the magazine when convenient, then use the Pet Pals menu to decide which skills Angelo should learn; reading alone does not activate the skill. Vol. 3 teaches Invincible Moon after 920 steps. Vol. 4 teaches Angelo Reverse after 260 steps. Vol. 5 teaches Angelo Search after 400 steps. Vol. 6 teaches Wishing Star after 1,060 steps.

{{CALLOUT:enemy|Optional Timber guard fight}} South of the station, past the Junk Shop and Hotel, two Elite Soldiers threaten Timber guards. The fight is optional; skip it if you want to keep moving. The Timber Junk Shop and Hotel are on this same detour.

Enter the **Timber Maniacs** building. From the floor magazine piles, take **Girl Next Door** from the back of the right-hand pile; it is used later on the White SeeD Ship for Zone’s Shiva Card reward. The left door has a hidden **Blizzaga draw point**. The newsroom at the end of the hall contains a **Timber Maniacs** issue and optional NPC stories.

{{CALLOUT:point|House window and Old Man’s House}} In the house next to Timber Maniacs, inspect the second-floor window to see the back-alley route. The Old Man’s House is a separate stop farther along the street, beyond the stairs. Talk to him and use the tap to heal the party before opening the cupboard; checking it four times gives **500 Gil** but locks out the free heal.

Go to the Pub screen. Two G-Soldiers block the way and drop a **Buel Card** after defeat. The general Item Shop is nearby, and there is a **Cure Draw Point** on this street. In the pub, the drunk blocks the back exit. Tell him about the card to receive a **Tonberry Card**, or buy him a drink to receive a **Forbidden Card**. The **Tonberry Card** is marginally more useful for refinement because it leads to Death rather than the Forbidden Card’s Confuse, though either route clears the exit. Use the back door after he moves.

Use the Save Point and follow the path to the TV station. Scenes play through the broadcast and the party eventually returns outside. Return to the pub, then to the house with the second-floor window for more scenes. Back in control, talk to Quistis twice, then try to leave the house to advance.

{{CALLOUT:spoiler|TV broadcast scene}} The broadcast reveals how Galbadia presents its Sorceress to the public. Pause here if you want to discover the scene for yourself.

{{CALLOUT:item|Chief's supply package}} Before leaving Timber, Chief gives **Potion**, **Phoenix Down**, **Soft**, **Antidote**, and **Remedy** for the journey. Accept the free supplies; Remedy is especially useful this early.

Speak to the G-Soldier outside, head toward the pub, and receive the ticket to East Academy. Board the train near Zone. Speak to Rinoa, follow Selphie into the hallway, and talk to her until she has no new lines; then return and speak to Zell, choosing **Leave him alone**. Stay aboard when the train reaches East Academy and continue to **Dollet Station** for an optional town visit. Afterward, return to East Academy and continue toward Galbadia Garden.

checkpoints.label: Angelo Recover, Angelo Reverse
checkpoints.description: Do not teach Rinoa these skills until you're completely finished with Angelo Searching.

checkpoints.label: Girl Next Door
checkpoints.description: Pick it up from the Timber Maniacs magazine piles during the town visit; it is used later in Zone’s White SeeD Ship card reward.

chapters.title: Dollet Exploration
chapters.content:
Stay aboard the train through East Academy as directed at the end of the previous chapter, then get off at **Dollet Station**. Walk down to the road and follow it into town; keep right and climb the steps beside the scooters to reach the fountain square. This is the recommended story detour before Galbadia Garden. **Do not play Triple Triad yet:** Dollet's **Random** rule can take away control of your hand.

{{ENCOUNTERS:0}}

{{CALLOUT:enemy|Useful Dollet-area encounters}} The beaches are the place to look for **Adamantoise**. With **Mug** equipped, steal a **Whisper**; no card-refinement route supplies this item. Adamantoise has heavy defenses and can blind the party, so expect a slower fight. Away from the shore, forests and cliff bases can produce **Anacondaur**. Its **Dragon Skin** drop is a weapon ingredient for Zell, but the drop is unreliable at lower levels; do not grind for it unless you want to spend time on the chance.

{{CALLOUT:point|Town Square and Hotel}} Take the **Silence Draw Point** beside the fountain. Stay at the Dollet Hotel for **100 Gil** and pick up the **Timber Maniacs** issue from the room's desk. Approach the desk carefully so you do not leave the room before collecting it. Save here before changing card rules.

{{CALLOUT:card|Safer Triple Triad rules}} Enter Dollet carrying Galbadia’s rules with **Open** already spread from Watts. Do not start a card game while **Random** is active. If the Queen is in Dollet, use the hotel girl's rule-mix sequence to spread Open and then target Random: save in the hotel and fully close/reopen the game, step out to the square and return, then challenge the girl in the green dress. Refuse the regional mix twice; on the third challenge accept and cancel at the rules screen. If Open is new to Dollet, this first pass should spread it. After Open spreads, return to Timber for the rule carry below, then repeat this sequence to target Random. If an unwanted rule spreads or the result is unclear, reload and try again. If the Queen is elsewhere, use the slower fallback: refuse four mixes with the girl, then accept-and-cancel at the fifth rules screen. These are rule-spread attempts, so cancel before any card game.

{{CALLOUT:missable|Timber journalist and rule carry}} On the required return to Timber between Dollet rule passes, speak to the man outside Timber Maniacs and answer **No way** when he says he is quitting. This sets up the later **Pet Nametag** reward. While there, challenge the left-side entrance guard and refuse rule mixing until he offers a plain game; play that game to carry Galbadia’s rules back to Dollet. Return by the road to avoid random encounters. Before returning to Dollet, you can also make an optional stop in Roshfall Forest for Ochu and nearby Wendigo materials.

{{CALLOUT:enemy|Optional Timber-side materials}} If you want Quistis weapon ingredients, detour through **Roshfall Forest** during the Timber return. **Ochu** can provide a Pain Draw at higher levels and an Ochu Tentacle with Mug; **Wendigo** are another Steel Pipe source, which Siren’s Tool-RF can refine into Aura Stones. Treat this as optional gathering, not a required level grind.

{{ENCOUNTERS:1}}

{{CALLOUT:card|Finish rule cleanup before card prizes}} Back in Dollet, repeat the hotel sequence above until **Random** is gone. Keep **Elemental** for later regions. Once Random is gone, stop adjusting rules and begin card games.

{{CALLOUT:card|Queen of Cards in Dollet}} The Queen is upstairs in the pub. If she is present, challenge her only to inspect the Trade Rule; quit at the rules screen and repeat until the trade is **All**, then stop playing her for now. Once the local rules are settled, ask about her **artist father** to start the Dollet Bone Quest and learn the next Queen-card lead for later in Deling City. If she is not in Dollet, continue the town route without these Queen-specific steps.

{{CALLOUT:card|Pub Owner's cards and Siren}} Pick up the second local **Timber Maniacs** issue from a table upstairs in the pub. If you have **Move-Find**, it also reveals a Save Point in this room. Challenge the man on the left; winning opens his private room. Speak to him there to receive **5 Geezard**, **4 Red Bat**, **3 Buel**, **2 Anacondaur**, and **1 Cactuar** cards. Challenge him again in the private room to win the unique **Siren Card**. Keep it for a complete collection, or use Card Mod for **3 Status Atk-J Scrolls** if you accept giving up the card; each scroll teaches a GF **Status Atk-J**, a useful early junction ability.

{{CALLOUT:missable|Occult Fan II}} In the Pub Owner's private room, inspect the magazine pile closest to the exit until it yields **Occult Fan II**. The pile awards at most three items during one visit; if you get three without the magazine, leave the room, return, and try again. It is a one-time magazine, so keep cycling the room until you have it.

{{CALLOUT:sidequest|Dollet Bone Quest timing}} The optional Bone Quest begins in the Artist's House south of the pub. It can be completed on Discs 1-3, but the reward tier improves on Disc 3: earlier completion gives a **Potion**, **Phoenix Down**, and **Soft**; Disc 3 gives an **X-Potion**, **Mega-Potion**, and **Elixir**. If you prefer the stronger set, wait until the Disc 3 window.

{{CALLOUT:sidequest|Bone Quest route}} After asking the Queen about her artist father, go to the Artist’s House where the boy and dog are outside. Examine the painting and speak to the boy, then search for the dog at the location shown: first the fountain square for the Potion, next the street by the pub entrance for the Phoenix Down, and last outside the house for the Soft. Between rewards, return to the house, inspect the updated painting, and speak with the boy again. Completing all three rounds adds a short scene.

{{CALLOUT:card|Recovering Queen of Cards losses}} If you gave MiniMog to the Queen in Balamb, challenge her son in the Artist's House to win it back. If he does not offer the card, make sure you have asked the Queen about her artist father first; the son may take several games to play it. Recover the card before choosing to Card Mod it if you want to keep a complete collection.

The **Nautilus** shop on the main street contains both the Item Shop and Junk Shop. Browse the Item Shop once to register it for later Call Shop use. If **Handyman** is still unearned, remodel one weapon here when you have the materials; any one upgrade counts. If X-ATM092 survived the exam, the car outside is wrecked and the owner's dialogue changes.

{{CALLOUT:card|Dollet card-player tiers}} After Random is gone, use the town players when you need specific common cards: the woman in yellow near the store plays Level 1, the pub bartender Level 2, the blue-sleeved man near the beach stairs Level 3, and the car-rental girl Level 4. No local player uses Level 5 cards. If your Trade Rule is not **All**, quit at the rule screen whenever a different trade appears and wait for All before playing.

For an optional return to the exam route, speak to the guard blocking the path toward the Communications Tower twice and choose to push through. The path leads to a G-Soldier scene, after which you can turn back. There is no useful reward, and the tower itself cannot be re-entered.

When the Dollet errands are finished, head for **East Academy Station**. Follow the road beside the railway to avoid random encounters; from the station, go to the nearby small forest for the Laguna dream and Galbadia Garden route.

checkpoints.label: Pet Nametag #2
checkpoints.description: After leaving Timber, return and encourage the man outside the Timber Maniacs building by choosing ‘No way!’ before finishing Disc 1; return after the Missile Base mission for the reward.

enemies.name: Adamantoise
enemies.notes: Adamantoise has high defenses and can inflict Darkness, which can make the fight slow.

enemies.name: Wendigo
enemies.notes: Steel Pipes feed later Doomtrain and Aura Stone refinement routes.

encounters.area: Roshfall Forest and nearby Timber roads (optional)

chapters.title: Journey to Galbadia Garden
chapters.content:
From **East Academy Station**, look for the nearby circular forest. Before entering, move all junctions to **Squall, Quistis, and Selphie**, even if they are not currently the active party. The next dream sequence maps Squall to Laguna, Quistis to Kiros, and Selphie to Ward; Zell and Rinoa do not participate, so anything junctioned to them is unavailable during the sequence.

{{ENCOUNTERS:0}}

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Excavation site setup}} Lightning on Elem-Atk is useful here because nothing resists it and the strongest enemies, Elastoid and Cyborg Esthar Soldier, are weak to Lightning. This dream works like the first Laguna sequence: magic, items, levels, EXP, and stat growth transfer between paired characters. Actions taken here also change Disc 3 Lunatic Pandora rewards, so follow the route carefully.

{{CALLOUT:enemy|Elastoid priority}} If your party is Lv 30+, equip **Mug** before entering to get a **Laser Cannon**; it teaches Quistis **Homing Laser** and refines via Ammo-RF into **5x Pulse Ammo**. Draw **Meltdown** while it is available for a powerful Vit-J stock.

{{CALLOUT:warning|Gesper's Degenerator}} Gesper can use **Degenerator** to eject a character from battle, and the effect cannot be blocked. Defeat Gespers quickly if you are avoiding KOs or removals.

Choose whichever dialogue option you like, then follow the linear path to the first fork. There is a **Sleep draw point** here. Continue for a back attack against an Esthar Soldier, then defeat three more soldiers in the next battle.

{{CALLOUT:point|Disc 3 reward triggers}} Take the right fork and follow the path down into the blue area. Near the junk on the ground, walk until a dialog opens and choose **Pick it up**; this Old Key unlocks a later **LuvLuv G**. Continue left to the screen with three door-like panels, fiddle with the **middle** lever, then leave; this opens a later **Silence draw point**.

Return to the early fork and take the other path to a three-way fork. The right path has a **Confuse draw point**. Take the center ladder down. Behind the broken barricade on the left in the blue area is another **Old Key**; pick it up to unlock a later **Ultima draw point**. Continue and mess with the large hatch to unlock a later **Phoenix Pinion**.

Return to the right-hand path and go back to the door panels. This time tamper with the **right** panel to unlock a later **Power Generator**, one of the rarest items. Continue north from the first Old Key junction until you reach the detonator. Press the **red switch first**, then the **blue switch**; this opens both sides and unlocks later **Combat King 005** access. Farther up, examine the large rock on the left wall and push it aside to unlock a later **Spd-J Scroll**. Use the Save Point at the three-way intersection, then head upward.

The final section is forced E-Soldier encounters. If every setup step above was done, only the final battle occurs; otherwise, up to five battles can happen. The last battle ends with **Soul Crush** on Kiros and Ward, followed by the wake-up scene.

{{CALLOUT:warning|Wake-up HP check}} Back in the real world, Selphie and Quistis will be at **1 HP** after Soul Crush. Heal before using them. The forest can now be walked on the world map.

{{CALLOUT:refinement|Dragon Fang route}} If you want Squall's Lion Heart early, farm **4x Dragon Fang** from Grendels in the Yaulny Canyon forest. Run along the cliff walls to trigger them. **Do not Mug**: Mug gives a Dragon Fin and cancels the post-battle drop. Check the Grendel entry in the encounter panel before farming because its Dragon Fang drop changes with level.

{{ENCOUNTERS:1}}

If you are done farming or do not care about Lion Heart now, leave the forest and head west to **Galbadia Garden**. It is very close and should appear shortly after exiting the forest.

chapters.title: Galbadia Garden
chapters.content:
{{CALLOUT:point|Galbadia Garden arrival}} Run toward the main building. If Quistis was in the party, the game forces a party change. When the announcement calls for the 2F Reception Room, cross the Main Hall, take the far hallway, go upstairs, and enter the room at the top.

In the 2F Reception Room, speak to the party members in this exact story order: **Zell -> Quistis -> Rinoa -> Zell -> Selphie**. The other conversations are optional commentary.

{{CALLOUT:character|Irvine joins}} Return to the front gate and talk to Rinoa. After the scene, **Irvine Kinneas** joins with **20x Normal Ammo**. Once you receive your orders, talk to anyone to advance, choose the active party, and review the Switch tutorial.

{{CALLOUT:drawing|Hidden Haste draw point}} Before leaving the Garden, visit the center of the Main Hall and draw from the invisible **Haste** point. It is easy to pass through this hall without noticing the interaction spot.

{{CALLOUT:card|First Level 6 cards}} After choosing the party, you can re-enter Galbadia Garden before taking the train. From the Main Hall, go right into the hallway and enter the classroom through the door on the right. The girl there plays Level 6 Boss Cards; this is the earliest chance to start winning that card tier. Challenge her if you want stronger cards or early Card Mod materials. For example, Krysta can be refined into Holy materials and X-ATM092 into a Turtle Shell. This is optional card preparation.

{{CALLOUT:card|Set Trabia's rules while you're here}} The Trabia exchange student is in the locker room beyond the ice rink, through the other door from the right-side hallway. This is the practical early window to make Trabia more comfortable for later card play: aim to spread **Open** and remove **Random** and **Plus**. Save in the Main Hall first.

Challenge the exchange student, agree to mix rules, then quit at the rules screen. Repeat until the game reports that Open has spread to Trabia. Return to the classroom girl and keep declining rule mixing until she no longer asks; this carries Galbadia's rules back onto your next challenge. Save again in the Main Hall, return to the exchange student, agree to mix, and quit at the rules screen to try to abolish a bad rule. Keep Open and avoid letting Same spread. If you see Same spread or Open abolished, reload your save. If Plus is abolished first, that result is still useful; repeat the classroom reset and exchange-student attempt to remove Random as well. Read each rule announcement before continuing. Do this now if you want to clean up Trabia's rules; later chances to change them are harder to control.

The **Life** draw point is in the locker room near the exchange student. Collect it while you are there, then return through the Main Hall and leave by the front gate.

When ready, pay **3,000 Gil** at the nearby station for the Deling City train. Once aboard, try to leave to trigger the party scene; enter the corridor, then return to the entrance. Stay with the group through the remaining dialogue. The train then arrives in Deling City.

chapters.title: Deling City
chapters.content:
{{CALLOUT:point|Deling City arrival}} Leave the station and use the bus loop from the central plaza to reach Caraway's Mansion. If you spoke with the Queen about her artist father in Dollet, stop at the Shopping Arcade first and challenge the man in black across from the Junk Shop to win the **Kiros Card** she mentioned.

{{CALLOUT:refinement|Kiros Card refinement}} The **Kiros Card** Card Mods into **3x Accelerator**. Accelerators teach **Auto-Haste**, one of the strongest passive abilities in the game. If you want to use them now, teach one GF in the Strength group and one GF in the Defense group; the Magic group can learn Auto-Haste naturally later. If you prefer stable endgame GF layouts, hold the Accelerators until those groups settle. Rare cards can be reacquired on Disc 4 with the right preparation, but do not mod cards still needed for Queen of Cards quest steps.

Deling's Item Shop has nothing new, but the **Junk Shop** is useful if you already have weapon ingredients for Squall or Selphie.

{{CALLOUT:hint|Later Junk Shop option}} If you did not have enough materials for an upgrade at Balamb, Deling City has another Junk Shop opportunity. Any weapon qualifies, and its recipe appears once you have the required materials; you do not need to read the matching Weapons Monthly issue.

{{CALLOUT:missable|Location Displayer}} Speak to the soldier outside Caraway's Mansion. He asks for the randomly assigned student ID number from the Tomb, sells the unique **Location Displayer** for **5,000 Gil**, and offers two unnecessary hints for **3,000 Gil** each. Buy the Location Displayer before giving him the ID; you cannot purchase it afterward.

After accepting the ID-number objective, let the guard escort you out and choose the car-rental drop-off. Rent a car if desired, or leave on foot. The Tomb of the Unknown King is on the small cape northeast of Deling City; roads do not reach it, so random encounters are possible unless you use Enc-None or a car for part of the trip.

{{ENCOUNTERS:0}}

{{CALLOUT:drawing|Tomb entrance and student ID}} Two students flee the ruins shouting “Float,” hinting at the Tomb boss strategy. Draw from the **Protect** point outside and use the Save Point before entering if needed. Follow the straight entry passage to the sword and examine it for the randomly generated student ID. Write the number down exactly; there is no fixed answer, and forgetting it means returning to the sword. You can leave after reading it, or clear the optional route below during the same visit.

{{CALLOUT:sidequest|Optional Tomb route - Brothers}} The ID number is the only required objective, but finishing the Tomb now recruits the **Brothers GF** and awards the **Sacred** and **Minotaur** cards. Use the in-game map and the route map below: the camera-relative directions can feel reversed after backtracking, so orient yourself by the numbered chambers. Taking the map command to leave the Tomb lowers SeeD rank; walk back through the entrance instead.

{{CALLOUT:point|Tomb route map}} After recording the number, return to the first four-way junction and take the right-hand branch. Follow **up, right, up, right**, then continue upward to the statue in chamber **1**. The numbered route image shows where to turn after you leave this first fight.

{{ENCOUNTERS:2}}

**Boss: Sacred**

Strategy: Before entering the statue room, heal and make sure Draw is available. Draw **Life** and any needed **Shell**, **Protect**, or **Berserk**. Sacred restores HP while grounded; use Float on him when you are ready to finish this first encounter. He retreats after taking enough damage, so do not mistake the retreat for a completed sidequest.

From Sacred's chamber, follow the camera-relative exits **down -> up -> right -> up -> right -> up -> right** to chamber **2**. Cross the gap, collect the **Float** draw point, then pull the chain to open the sluice. Retrace across the gap and follow **down -> up -> right -> up -> right -> up -> right** to chamber **3**. Search the far corner for the **invisible Cura** draw point, then operate the mechanism on the left to start the water wheel; use the Save Point here if you want a second safety save. To reach the center, backtrack with **down -> up -> right -> up -> up -> left**, then cross the bridge into chamber **4**. The camera turns with each entrance, so check the in-game map if the directions stop matching your view.

{{CALLOUT:hint|Brothers boss preparation}} The central fight awards **40 AP** across the two enemies. Heal, check that the active party is junctioned, and set GF learning targets before touching the figure at the back of chamber 4. The encounter panel lists both enemies' Draws and other level-dependent data.

**Boss: Sacred**

**Boss: Minotaur**

Strategy: Draw **Double** from Minotaur and **Life** from Sacred if useful, plus any shared spells you still need. Both enemies regenerate while grounded: cast Float on each boss to stop that recovery. Float on your party as well to evade the duo's Earth-based Mad Cow Special. Minotaur absorbs Earth, so avoid Quake and Earth-junctioned attacks; Wind or Poison damage works well. Keep healing through the group attacks and finish only after taking the Draws you want.

The victory adds **Brothers** to the GF list and gives the **Sacred Card** and **Minotaur Card**, advancing the Queen of Cards chain. The fight also awards the G-Item rewards listed in the encounter panel. To leave, return through the center route to the sword chamber; reread the sword if you did not record the ID. Walk out through the entrance rather than using the map escape. Return to Deling City with the number for Caraway's guard.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Brothers ability order}} Prioritize **Str-J** and **Elem-Atk-J** for immediate junction coverage, then work through the HP+ abilities toward **HP Bonus** if you plan to invest the AP. Choose **Spr-J** before the HP chain if Spirit coverage matters more for your party right now; HP Bonus takes longer because its HP+ prerequisites must be learned first.

{{CALLOUT:card|Queen of Cards - Sacred step}} Before giving Caraway the ID and starting the operation, you can detour to Dollet for the next Queen of Cards step. If you previously sent the Queen there during the MiniMog setup, save and deliberately lose the **Sacred Card** to her; the desired destination is **Balamb**, so reload if she names another town. Then win Sacred back from her son in the artist’s house if you want to keep or refine it. If the Queen is not in Dollet yet, leave this optional step for a later visit.

{{CALLOUT:refinement|Minotaur Card refinement}} If you completed the Brothers route, the **Minotaur Card** Card Mods into **10x Adamantine**. Adamantine is needed for several ultimate weapons and can also teach **Vit+60%**. Do not mod the **Sacred Card** until its Queen of Cards step is done; it mods into **100x Dino Bone** for easy Quake stock, but the quest timing matters more.

Back in Deling City, use the Shopping Arcade and Hotel prep window. Stay at the Hotel for **100 Gil** to heal, then pick up the **Timber Maniacs** issue near the far bed in the hotel room. A woman across the street from the Hotel uses **Fisherman’s Horizon rules**. This is an early opportunity to prepare that region before you arrive; save in the Hotel before trying to change its rules.

Give the correct ID number to the mansion guard and enter Caraway's Mansion. Talking to Rinoa in the waiting room advances the story; if Rinoa was in the active party, reform the party but do not spend time moving junctions yet. Follow General Caraway through the city plan, then make final purchases/preparations and return to the mansion to begin the operation.

{{CALLOUT:point|Assassination operation start}} As Quistis, try to leave the room after the scene. As Squall, follow Caraway, talk to him under the arch, then continue toward the Presidential Palace entrance. Collect the **Thundara draw point** along this walk before the teams split. When control returns to Quistis's party, leave junctions alone for the moment and return to Caraway's Mansion through the park.

Inside the mansion, control switches to Rinoa. Ignore the crates at first and examine the manhole cover to enter the sewers. Junction her if needed, run west until the magazine on the ground appears, collect **Weapons Mon May**, then return to the starting point. Climb the crates to the roof path, follow it until the scene, then walk forward.

Back with Quistis, examine the glasses on the shelf near the door, then use the statue near the window to reveal the hidden passage. Junction the party if the sewer encounters worry you, use the Save Point, and continue until the view returns to Squall.

As Squall, run right between scenes until reaching the gate, then enter. Move GFs and key magic off inactive characters and onto **Squall and Irvine**. Climb the same crate route Rinoa used. Junction **Quake** to Elem-Atk if available, Fire-elemental magic to Elem-Def, and Petrify protection to ST-Def if available. At least one character must have **Draw** equipped before entering Rinoa's room.

{{CALLOUT:achievement|Draw Carbuncle}} The Iguions begin with Reflect. Draw **Carbuncle** from either one immediately to earn the GF achievement and remove Reflect from both.

**Boss: 2x Iguion**

Strategy: After securing **Carbuncle**, draw **Break** here if you need it, though low Magic can make stocking slow. The Iguions use Magma Breath for single-target Fire damage plus Petrifying, Resonance for magical damage to all, and claw attacks. **Quake** with a decent Magic stat can wipe both out; otherwise physical attacks are enough. Mugging earns **6x G-Returner** instead of the **4x G-Returner** drop, but the item is low priority.

{{CALLOUT:story|Edea parade scene}} After naming Carbuncle, use the hatch in the hallway to reach the clock tower. Examine the sniper rifle to switch back to Quistis's party.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Carbuncle ability order}} If you have a **Turtle Shell** from Armadodo or Card Mod, use it on Carbuncle to teach **Vit+20%** and unlock Vit+40% faster. If you obtained an **Orihalcon** from X-ATM092, it can teach **Vit+40%** and unlock Vit Bonus immediately. Ability priority: **Recov Med-RF -> Vit+% abilities -> Vit Bonus -> Mag-J -> other junctions -> Counter -> Auto-Reflect -> remaining abilities**. If Vit+40% was taught early, leave Vit+20% until immediately after Auto-Reflect. Carbuncle's summon applies Reflect to the whole party without dealing damage.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|GF grouping note}} At this point, balance stat Bonus growth and junction coverage across Strength, Defense, and Magic groups. The important local rule is: keep the active party fully junctioned, give everyone who will draw from upcoming bosses access to Mag-J when possible, and move Diablos to the Magic group once Carbuncle learns Mag-J if you want that group to gain HP-J later. Carbuncle's Mag-J is a priority because several upcoming boss spells are not easy to refine yet.

{{ENCOUNTERS:1}}

{{CALLOUT:point|Deling sewer route}} In Quistis's sewer route, water wheels are one-way, some doors open and others do not, and ladders facing the wrong way can be dropped to make bridges. From the regain-control screen, head north, travel left/clockwise around the square of screens, return on the far side of the water, follow the linear path to a water wheel, ride it upward, and continue toward the exit.

Detailed sewer route: in the first screen north, cross and go left. Ignore the ladder side route unless you want the draw point. Continue around until the first water wheel after that draw point, cross the bridge, open the door, and continue. In the next water-wheel screen, cross back if you want the **Zombie draw point**; otherwise ride the two water wheels across. At the next junction, use the water wheel to drop down, go as far south as possible, drop the ladder to create a shortcut back to Caraway's side, then follow the path right until a water wheel. Ride it and follow the walkway to the exit. In the tower, flip the switch.

After the scene, set the active battle party to **Squall, Irvine, and Rinoa**. Move all GFs, commands, and useful magic to them. Bio on Squall's Elem-Atk is useful, Fire protection on Elem-Def helps, and Slow on Squall's ST-Atk is useful. ST-Def is not important for the next two fights. Give Squall Mug if convenient, or leave Mug on the Diablos holder.

**Boss: Seifer**

Strategy: Seifer is a solo Squall fight and is mostly a formality, but he is the first mandatory boss here with multiple level groups. Check the encounter panel or his Draw list to confirm which version you are facing before stocking magic. He relies on Hyperion attacks, rarely pulls the trigger, and can cast Fira. Mug a **Hero** if possible, draw any needed Fire/Cure/Life-family spells, then finish him.

**Boss: Edea**

Strategy: Edea uses -aga elemental spells for heavy damage, can rarely cast Protect and Shell on herself, and will spend turns casting Dispel on party members with Reflect. Immediately summon **Carbuncle** to put Reflect on the whole party, let Edea waste three turns Dispelling it, then resummon as needed. Draw **Cura**, **Dispel**, **Life**, and **Double** if you need stock. Mug the **Elixir** if possible, then win the fight for the AP. Losing does not cause Game Over, but it forfeits the AP.

Watch the scenes after Edea as Galbadia takes the party into custody.

chapters.title: Winhill
chapters.content:
{{CALLOUT:story|Laguna’s Winhill dream}} After the scenes in Deling City, you regain control as Laguna at **Winhill**. Before leaving his room, use the hidden **Curaga Draw Point** beside the wardrobe/armoire; this is the earliest opportunity to take it. Go downstairs, speak to **Ellone**, then leave the house and enter the pub immediately south of the town square.

{{CALLOUT:missable|Missable - Eyes On Me}} During the pub conversation, exhaust Kiros's topics and ask about **Julia** before ending the conversation. This one-time answer unlocks the **Eyes On Me** tutorial entry; there is no later recovery.

Choose **Let's talk later** after the topics to bring Kiros along. Laguna inherits Squall's junctions and Kiros inherits Irvine's. If the menu was opened before Kiros joined, check both characters' GF and ability assignments before leaving.

{{ENCOUNTERS:0}}

Before setting out, take the **Dispel Draw Point** near the river at the lower-right side of the square: go down the steps, then return to the square and cross the bridge. Check the **Drain Draw Point** along the road beyond the bridge. At the fork, either branch reaches the patrol route; the lower branch passes a hidden **Reflect Draw Point** beside a truck. Continue south until Laguna says the patrol is over.

Spend Laguna's separate **3,000 Gil** at the Winhill shop on the southern edge of the village before returning. The items you buy carry into Squall's inventory, but the dream's Gil does not; Tents or Remedies are sensible supplies if you have no preference. Then return to the town square and go back to the pub.

If desired, rest in Laguna's house before the next scene. Go upstairs in the pub, speak with Raine after the scene, then return to Laguna's room, examine the bed, and choose **Rest** to end the dream. Triple Triad and the village's optional sidequests become relevant on the later real-world visit, after Balamb Garden is mobile.

chapters.title: The Escape
chapters.content:
{{CALLOUT:point|D-District Prison opening}} At first control, speak with Rinoa, then check Zell and Quistis when they are available; return to Rinoa when the scene needs to advance. Stop the guard when prompted. As Squall, choose **Just let me die** for the preferred scene route. Talk to Quistis and leave the cell, then head up from Floor 7 to trigger Zell's short fight against **2x Guard**.

When the junction menu opens, equip all three characters before continuing. Give everyone **Draw** and assign **Mug** to at least one character. A nonlethal status in ST-Atk-J can help against the next pair; Fire and Lightning magic in Elem-Def-J are useful if available.

{{CALLOUT:boss|Biggs and Wedge}} These returning soldiers are easy to control with **Blind** or **Silence**; **Slow** makes them even less active. While both are alive, draw any magic you still need for junctions, especially the stronger support spells shown in the encounter panel. Stock up to 100 where useful. Mug each soldier after drawing: their one-time steals are more valuable than their ordinary drops, but the steal can fail, so retry while the target is still alive. Once finished, equip Lightning magic to Elem-Atk-J for the prison machines.

{{ENCOUNTERS:0}}

{{CALLOUT:route|D-District Prison route}} The cell block has floors 1–15. You begin on Floor 7. Sweep down to Floor 1 first for the lower-cell pickups, then return to Floor 7 and climb through the upper floors to the Torture Room on Floor 13. On barrier floors, walk around the partition to reach the stairs; the three no-barrier floors let you cross directly. Cell sides below use the prison's left/right layout.

| Floor | Notes | Left Cell | Right Cell |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 15 | Exit |  |  |
| 14 | Control Room; hidden Save Point (Move-Find) |  |  |
| 13 | Torture Room; story objective |  |  |
| 12 | Empty | N/A | N/A |
| 11 |  | Card Player (200 Gil) | Hidden Thundaga Draw Point |
| 10 |  | Save Point | Card Player (300 Gil; Character Report) |
| 9 |  |  | Berserk Draw Point |
| 8 | No barrier | Man from Garden Shop | N/A |
| 7 | No barrier | Starting location | N/A |
| 6 | Save Point | N/A | N/A |
| 5 |  | N/A | Card Player (500 Gil; one-time Luck Up chance) |
| 4 |  | Tent | N/A |
| 3 |  | N/A | Pet House |
| 2 |  | Pet Nametag | Str Up |
| 1 | No barrier | Hidden Save Point (Move-Find) | Combat King 001 |
| Below Floor 1 | Empty hallway |  |  |

On the first sweep, take the one-time **Luck Up** chance from the Floor 5 card player if you want it. The Floor 8 shop is a useful restock stop on the return climb; the route table above lists the other pickups.

{{CALLOUT:missable|Missable - Pet Nametag}} Take the Floor 2 left-cell **Pet Nametag** before leaving. It is one of the limited copies available through normal play; other access depends on version and Chocobo World availability.

The Floor 1 right cell contains **Combat King 001**. Reading it adds **Dolphin Blow** to Zell's Limit Breaks. With **Move-Find** equipped, reveal the hidden Floor 1 Save Point before heading back up.

On the upper route, Floor 9 has a **Berserk Draw Point**. Floor 10 has a visible Save Point and a 300-Gil card player.

{{CALLOUT:missable|Character Report}} If you received the Battle Meter from Cid in Balamb, beat the Floor 10 right-cell player once before leaving. This one-time Battle Meter upgrade has no later prison replacement; if you missed the original Battle Meter, you cannot earn it here.

Floor 11's right cell contains a hidden **Thundaga Draw Point**, revealed by **Move-Find**. The left-cell player charges 200 Gil and can award a **Rosetta Stone** at very low odds; a one-time **HP Up** is also available. For the optional timing method, save on Floor 10, equip Enc-None, and—if the Queen of Cards is not in Deling City and players are not prompting to change rules—decline 54 challenges before playing and winning for the Rosetta Stone, or 64 before playing and winning for HP Up. Corridor movement can shift the refusal count, so treat this as an optional exploit rather than a guaranteed quick reward.

Floor 12 has no pickup. Continue to Floor 13 only after finishing the cell sweep and card-player rewards you want; the Torture Room advances the story. Speak to the nearby Moomba and then Squall. The Moombas can open three floor barriers; clear Floor 9 first so the upper route is easier. At the control panel, press the red button when prompted, then examine the door.

As Zell, keep moving through the prison. If guards catch you, the pursuit fights are manageable with basic attacks or Limit Breaks. After the scenes, choose one additional character to join Squall and Rinoa; Quistis is useful if you want another Draw user. Recheck junctions before climbing, since the active party has changed.

Control switches to Irvine. Reassign junctions to his group and descend to the crane on Floor 3. After the scene, control returns to Squall. The Moomba by the stairs gives a **Cottage**; the one farther away gives a **Rename Card**. Move junctions to the current team again before continuing upward.

Near the top of the prison, equip **Move-Find** and collect the hidden Floor 14 Save Point if you have the ability. Before leaving, assign Mug and Lightning Elem-Atk-J. The next scripted group is **Elite Soldier + 2x GIM52A**; these prison encounter entries have a Lv70 cap even though the enemies' general data scales higher. Use the encounter panel for level-dependent details, defeat the soldier first, and Mug **Missile** from a GIM52A before finishing the robots. Use the item on Quistis afterward to teach **Micro Missiles**.

After the escape scenes, hold **Right** during the bridge run. Releasing the direction or moving the wrong way causes a Game Over.

{{CALLOUT:point|Desert party split}} In the Galbadia desert, collect the **Aero Draw Point** if useful, then speak to Selphie twice. Choose teams: Selphie leads the Missile Base group and Squall leads the Garden group. Put **Zell with Squall** to improve a later reward to **Mega Phoenix** instead of **Remedy**; the choice does not block progress. Squall's team then travels west toward Deling City.

During the westbound train sequence, an optional Triple Triad player is available if you want another match. After the story returns you to world travel, finish any Deling City detour before driving to the Missile Base.

{{CALLOUT:refinement|Optional Deling City supply stop}} Before the Missile Base, you can restock in Deling City. If Carbuncle has **Recovery Med-RF**, buying Tents from the Item Shop and refining them into Mega-Potions is a repeatable cash source, yielding roughly **25,000 Gil per 100-Tent batch**. Keep some Tents for healing and avoid spending more time than you need, since more efficient shop options arrive later.

{{CALLOUT:card|Caraway and the Rinoa Card}} At Caraway's Mansion, you can deliberately lose the **Ifrit Card** to General Caraway, then speak to him again to make him play the **Rinoa Card**. Win Rinoa now and keep it. This first Ifrit transfer sends the card to Martine, who can be challenged for it later at Fisherman's Horizon; it is a planned, recoverable loss. The prison and Deling players use Galbadia's **Same** rule, so review the active regional rules before risking valuable cards. Timber and Dollet roads are blocked for now, and the Missile Base is reached by car near the desert station.

chapters.title: Missile Base
chapters.content:
{{CALLOUT:story|Selphie's mission}} Control passes to Selphie and the two companions assigned to her team. Drive west from Deling City to the Galbadia Missile Base and park outside the facility. Before entering, save and check that the active trio has Draw, useful status protection, and a way to Mug; you can still adjust junctions before the mission's forced fights.

{{CALLOUT:achievement|Protect your SeeD score}} Your dialogue, combat, and escape time here can affect your **SeeD score**, so keep the disguise intact and fight only when the game forces you to. When the first guard checks the card reader, choose **Walk by quietly**. The other noncombat lines are safe, but fighting, running, or giving away the mission can trigger avoidable encounters and rank penalties. The ten-minute escape setting later gives the best time result, but cannot guarantee Rank A by itself.

{{ENCOUNTERS:0}}

Enter through the left side of the building and save at the point in the first room. Examine the lit panel between the two doors on the left to open the left-hand door. Pass the guard with **Walk by quietly**, cross the exterior walkway, and descend the stairs to the next landing and its Save Point.

{{CALLOUT:achievement|Magic Miner and hidden Draw Point}} The landing has two maintenance soldiers beside the stairs. Speak with them, then take the lower-left exit. With **Move-Find** equipped, reveal and draw from the hidden **Blind Draw Point** in the side passage before talking to the guard on the left. Draw Points on this route also advance **Magic Miner**; take the Blizzara and Full-Life points ahead before leaving.

Return upstairs and take the upper door. Tell the red-light guard that the maintenance crew sent you and that he can go ahead. Go back to the pair at the landing and pass along his reply. Then return to the guard who checked the card reader; speak to him until he leaves his post, which opens the way into the control room.

The control room contains a visible **Blizzara Draw Point**. Draw here before touching the controls. Use any harmless panel options; the resulting commotion brings other workers in. Keep the cover story: choose the noncombat response to talk your way out, then say you were about to make the call. If you start a fight here, the disguise route is lost and extra encounters can follow.

Leave the control room and go downstairs to the launcher area. Agree to help when the soldiers ask. Choose **Play it cool** and then **Help out** when questioned, stand between the workers and the launcher, and press the action button repeatedly until it locks into place. Speak to the supervising soldier, but stay in the room.

With **Move-Find** equipped, reveal and draw from the hidden **Full-Life Draw Point** on the left side of the room, in front of the missile silos. The point gives a small stock, but Full-Life is valuable and this is the only point for it on the mission route. Then return to the Save Point room and examine the control panel. Choose **Target**, raise **Error Ratio** to its maximum, select **Data Upload**, and confirm. Leaving the ratio lower makes the missile strike hit its target and ends the run. Exit the terminal and speak to the guard on the right side of the room.

Before returning upstairs, check junctions for the mandatory security fight. Put Silence or Pain on Status Attack if available; Silence is especially effective against the Base Leader. Bio on Elemental Attack is useful, and Ice or Lightning on Elemental Defense can reduce incoming damage. Keep Draw equipped if you want the Base Leader's **Reflect** or the soldiers' spells, and Mug equipped if you want their items.

{{ENCOUNTERS:1}}

The **Base Leader and two Base Soldiers** are a mandatory battle and do not cost SeeD points. Silence the Leader early to stop its status and support magic, then use Blind or Sleep to slow the soldiers. Draw **Reflect** from the Leader if the party needs it. If you want to Mug, control the soldiers first; the encounter panel shows the level-dependent item results.

After the security fight, examine the missile-control panel on the left and identify the missile settings. Then inspect the panel on the left in the next room to find the self-destruct system. Set the timer only after junctions are ready: Choose **10 minutes** for the best SeeD time score if you can move quickly; choose **20 minutes** if you want a wider margin. The longer countdowns leave more time for the same exit route. Save at the nearby point before starting if it is available.

{{CALLOUT:preparation|BGH251F2 preparation}} The countdown leads to the parking lot and a fight with **BGH251F2**. Change Elemental Attack to Lightning, Water, or Earth if you have those spells junctioned; all three exploit its weakness. Prioritize Slow and quick damage. Blind can stop its Chaingun but not its Beam Cannon, so do not spend time on it if the timer is tight. The warning **Standby for beam cannon** means the cannon fires on the next turn: choose **Defend** to halve the hit. Shell does not reduce this attack. As the machine loses turrets, the cannon becomes more frequent and can fire every turn near the end. Draw Shell, Protect, or Stop only if time permits.

{{ENCOUNTERS:2}}

Sprint out to the parking lot to trigger the **BGH251F2 (Missile Base)** encounter. This is the fixed-level version, unlike the machine's Deling City encounter; use the encounter panel for its level cap and other data.

When BGH251F2 falls, the encounter continues with a second forced round against **one Elite Soldier and two G-Soldiers**. Defeat this group as well; the machine's defeat alone does not clear the escape sequence. The timer is still relevant, so heal with quick items or spells and finish the soldiers promptly rather than stopping to Draw. The encounter panel lists the enemies' current level-based opportunities.

After both rounds, the mission awards **Weapons Monthly, June Issue**. It is guaranteed; no Mug or extra pickup is needed.

Follow the escape prompts in order: run to the **front gate** and use its action point, then reach the **complex door** and activate it. Return to the center of the lot for the next scenes. The story shifts back to Squall's group, which now has to get Balamb Garden moving before the missiles arrive.

{{CALLOUT:missable|Timber journalist reward}} If you encouraged the man outside the Timber Maniacs building to become a journalist during Disc 1, the Disc 2 **Pet Nametag** reward is now available from him in Timber. Take it at the first chance to travel there after this mission; if the story does not yet allow a detour, keep it on the list for the upcoming mobile-Garden free-roam window. The D-District Prison Pet Nametag from the previous chapter is a separate copy.
