checkpoints.description: Requires Laguna to operate the right excavation panel and its blue switch during the Disc 1 visit.

checkpoints.label: Combat King 005
checkpoints.description: Requires Laguna to set both detonator switches for the ground pickup; otherwise buy Combat King 005 later at the Esthar Book Store with Familiar.

checkpoints.label: Spd-J Scroll
checkpoints.description: Requires Laguna to push the tunnel-wall rock; search the left-wall cavity on the Elevator 1 route.

enemies.name: Imp
enemies.notes: A low-risk AP fight if you want to learn abilities while keeping levels down.

chapters.title: Lunar Base
chapters.content:
After the Lunar Base scenes, speak to **Piet**, the man in the white coat, then pick up Rinoa and carry her through the green door into the treatment room. Use the nearby **Save Point** before leaving; follow Piet north through the passageways to the **control room**.

{{CALLOUT:card|Alexander Card setup}} Before checking the monitor, challenge Piet to Triple Triad and repeatedly start and quit until a rule abolishes. All seven rules are active here. Aim to remove **Random or Plus**; if another rule abolishes, reload. Once one of those two is gone, save and play Piet for the **Alexander Card**. Keep it for the **Queen of Cards** quest and do not Card Mod it yet. Piet can be challenged again at the escape-pod Crash Site if you postpone the match.

After the card game, inspect the **monitor** beside your partner to trigger the scene. Speak to Piet if you need the direction to Ellone, save again, then go upstairs to the residential area. The female researcher there can tell you about the Lunar Base; this conversation is optional.

{{CALLOUT:card|Laguna Card}} Before speaking to **Ellone**, challenge her and win the **Laguna Card**. She only accepts this match before her story conversation. If you miss it, the completed CC Group can recover the card in Disc 4.

{{CALLOUT:refinement|Laguna Card Refinement}} The **Laguna Card** refines into **100 Hero** items. Sell any Heroes already in your inventory first if needed to make room for the full yield, then Card Mod Laguna if you want the invincibility items.

When ready, speak to Ellone and go to the **med bay**. After the scene, talk to Rinoa there, then return to the control room. Wait for Rinoa to arrive; if she does not appear after a while, follow her route to trigger the scene. Once she leaves, inspect the monitor.

Go upstairs to the room beside the unconscious man and examine the **locker** to put on a space suit. Follow Rinoa toward the airlock. When the door closes, return to the hallway outside the locker room.

Return to the control room. Speak to Piet and Ellone for the scene, then leave on the right and take the elevator down to the escape pod. Save at the pod, talk to Ellone again, and enter the capsule.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Space rescue}} Catch Rinoa before the timer ends. Steer the view toward her and center her on screen; use directional input to make gradual corrections and Triangle to speed up. Save at the pod beforehand and prioritize controlled aim through the timer. Catching her and reaching the Ragnarok unlocks the **Ragnarok** achievement; the next chapter covers clearing the Propagators to secure the ship.

checkpoints.label: Alexander Card
checkpoints.description: Win from Piet after abolishing Random or Plus if possible. If postponed, Piet is available again at the escape-pod Crash Site. Do not Card Mod before the Queen of Cards step.

checkpoints.label: Laguna Card
checkpoints.description: Win from Ellone before speaking to her; this is her only match. If missed, recover it from the CC Group on Disc 4 if the group was defeated by the end of Disc 3.

checkpoints.label: Ragnarok
checkpoints.description: Catch Rinoa during the space rescue and reach the ship to unlock the achievement. The next chapter covers the Propagator pairs needed to secure the airship.

chapters.title: Ragnarok
chapters.content:
When control returns aboard the Ragnarok, use the nearby **Save Point** so you can skip replaying the long Lunar Base scenes. Go into the next room for the scene, then continue through the door for another. Examine the panel beside the door to close the hatch, then head downstairs to the first Propagator.

{{CALLOUT:preparation|Propagator junction setup}} Move any junctions and magic off **Edea** and onto active characters before the fights. Put **Death** or another useful status on **ST-Atk**; instant KO is especially effective. Junction **Lightning** to **Elem-Def**. **Pain** on **ST-Def** covers several of the status attacks; if you do not have it, protect against **Darkness and Silence**.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Rinoa's Angel Wing}} Rinoa's **Angel Wing** Limit Break is available after the Lunar Base events. While it is active, she casts a random spell from her stocked magic at five times its normal strength without consuming that stock, but you cannot direct her actions. Keep only the offensive spells you want her to use in stock if you choose this limit.

{{ENCOUNTERS:0}}

The first Propagator is purple. Each defeated color returns if you fight a different color before defeating its partner; the slow fallback is to defeat **25 total Propagators**. **Confuse** does not work. Use an instant-KO effect for a quick fight, or use **Silence** and **Blind** to reduce their attacks.

{{CALLOUT:route|Propagator pair route}} After the first purple Propagator, go through the large door and quickly run through the door on the left before the red Propagator catches you. Defeat the second purple one in the entrance area. Return to the aisle, go right once, and defeat the first red Propagator. Go back through the previous area, take the left route again, ignore the green Propagator, and go south to defeat the second red one.

For the yellow pair, go north two screens while leaving the green Propagator alone. Defeat the yellow one, then continue south along the upper level to the second yellow Propagator in front of the **air lock**. Once the yellow pair is defeated, you can go south to save.

Return to the hangar where the first purple fight occurred. Take the small door on the right to defeat the first green Propagator; save here if needed. Then go to the elevator room and defeat the matching green Propagator. Ride the elevator after all four color pairs are cleared to finish the sequence and continue into **Back on Earth**.

enemies.name: Propagator
enemies.notes: Eight total, two per color. Defeat same-color pairs consecutively to prevent respawns.

chapters.title: Back on Earth
chapters.content:
After the scenes, **Rinoa will be unavailable**. Go back inside the Ragnarok, enter the **cabin** to the **left of the elevator**, then try to leave.

{{CALLOUT:point|Shumi Village Ultima Draw Point}} If the point has recharged, stop in **Shumi Village** before the Memorial to draw Ultima again; it will refill as you travel through the optional routes.

{{CALLOUT:map|Sorceress Memorial Location}} Fly to the **Sorceress Memorial** on the **peninsula east of Esthar**. Go inside as far as the game allows for the scenes. Afterward, **Rinoa returns** to the crew and you can set any party you like as long as Squall remains in it.

{{CALLOUT:story|The Promise}} After Rinoa returns at the Sorceress Memorial, make the optional visit to **Edea’s House**. Follow Angelo, speak to Rinoa to trigger the promise scene, then return to the Ragnarok. This scene follows the reunion and belongs before the Esthar Presidential Palace briefing.

{{CALLOUT:point|Full-Life Draw Point — missed pickup}} Completing both Shumi Village quest phases during Disc 2 and returning to the workshop for its scene makes a **Full-Life Draw Point** appear at the Master Fisherman’s former seat in FH. If you saw that scene but did not collect the point after the FH fisherman quest, return to the seat now; finishing Shumi for the first time in Disc 3 does not trigger the point.

{{CALLOUT:sidequest|Aerial Exploration}} This is the Disc 3 open-world cleanup window. Use the **Sidequests** tab for the full optional routes. Resume the Queen of Cards chain with the Alexander, Doomtrain, and Phoenix steps below; keep Alexander and Doomtrain unrefined through their handoffs and recovery, and finish before the Mobile Type 8 cutoff. For Disc 4 card farming, move the Queen to **Shumi Village** and set the **Trabia** trade rule to **Diff** before the cutoff; the Queen movement and rule tables in **Triple Triad Rules** cover the steps.

{{CALLOUT:route|Late optional route order}} The Ragnarok opens a large Disc 3 cleanup window. A practical sweep is **Cactuar Island** for Cactuar and stat Bonus abilities, **Deep Sea Research Center** for Bahamut (then decide whether to descend for Eden), the fixed Esthar **Elnoyle** encounter and high-level island Draw Points once prepared, then **Obel Lake** and **PuPu** while Enc-None keeps travel manageable. Optional branches can be interleaved; this order puts the power gains and difficult battles before the clue hunts.

{{CALLOUT:gf|Cactuar Island}} Requirements: after Lunar Base. Fly to Cactuar Island near the Kashkabald Desert AP-farming spot. Junction **Water** to Elem-Atk, push Strength as high as possible, enter with low HP if you want Limit Break access, and remove **Mug** because stealing is not useful here.

{{ENCOUNTERS:0}}

Strategy: Treat this as a high-HP Limit Break race. Water-boosted physicals, Aura-backed Renzokuken, Shot, and Duel all work well. **10,000 Needles** deals exactly 10,000 damage to one target, so keep recovery ready. If Jumbo Cactuar starts hesitating, finish the fight quickly before it flees. After winning, Cactuar joins as a GF. Teach **Luck-J**, **Eva+30%**, **Defend**, **Luck+50%**, **Kamikaze**, then the rest. Put the stat Bonus abilities on the character you intend to level; prioritize **Str Bonus**, **Mag Bonus**, **Vit Bonus**, and **Spr Bonus**, leaving HP Bonus out if only four slots are available.

{{CALLOUT:enemy|Deep Sea Research Center}} The Deep Sea Research Center is in the southwestern ocean and requires the Ragnarok to enter. Enemies here calculate normal levels, then add **+15 levels** after the final level calculation, so equip stat Bonus abilities before exploring. Save outside. In the Laboratory, move only while the core is not glowing; moving during the glow triggers encounters.

Before touching the core, prepare for Ruby Dragons: give someone **Magic** with Blind and Shell, equip Auto-Shell where possible, cover Lightning and Wind in Elem-Def, and protect against Stop or equip Auto-Haste. Equip **Draw** on everyone and remove Mug.

Core answers: choose **"It is not our will to fight"** for the first Ruby Dragon, **"Never"** for the second Ruby Dragon back attack, then choose the **hidden bottom option** for Bahamut.

{{ENCOUNTERS:1}}

Strategy: Keep Shell active, inflict **Darkness and Slow**, and use the setup above. **Full-Life** is the priority Draw here; stock it before finishing the fight. After the fight, Bahamut joins as a GF. Teach **Boost**, **Mug**, **Auto-Protect**, and **Rare Item**, then everything else. Rare Item is not a general upgrade; it shifts drops toward the second slot and can make fourth-slot items impossible.

{{CALLOUT:route|Deep Sea Deposit}} After Bahamut, the core room gains a save point and random encounters. Climb down the vine into the steam-unit puzzle. The area has two practical paths: the **fixed encounter path** with Zell, which is better for Perfect Game farming and repeatable fixed enemies, and the more direct final-boss path, which spends more steam and opens the Steam Room but skips the fixed Deep Sea Deposit farming route. You need **10 steam units** after the final area to engage the boss at the bottom.

{{CALLOUT:route|Steam-unit routes}} At Level 1, spend **4 units**. For the fixed-encounter route, bring Zell and spend **1 unit each on Levels 2, 3, 4, and 5**; Zell opens Level 6 without steam. For the direct boss route, spend **2 on Level 2**, **1 on Level 3**, **4 to open the Steam Room** (which restores 7), **1 each on Levels 4 and 5**, and **4 on Level 6**. The Level 1 computer can reset the puzzle if needed.

The fixed encounter path is valuable because Deep Sea Deposit screens can be re-entered to farm fixed enemies. Tri-Face is the standout target for Curse Spikes and Dark Matter routing; other useful fixed encounters include Ruby Dragon, Behemoth, and Iron Giant. Use the Bestiary and Items tabs for level-banded draw, mug, and drop tables instead of duplicating every farming table here. On the descent, the **third screen has a Triple Draw Point**, the **fifth screen has a hidden Ultima Draw Point**, and the bottom level has a **hidden Save Point** revealed by Move-Find.

{{ENCOUNTERS:2}}

Strategy: Raise Speed, use Auto-Haste / Auto-Shell / Auto-Protect if available, and cover Earth damage. Keep Draw on everyone and **draw Eden before killing Ultima Weapon**; Tiamat in Ultimecia Castle is the later fallback. Light Pillar is the danger spike, so keep the party healthy and use Meltdown plus Limit Breaks for damage. Defeating Ultima Weapon closes the fixed Deep Sea Deposit encounter route; if you want to farm Tri-Face there, leave it alive until the farming is complete.

{{CALLOUT:perfect-game|Fixed Elnoyle in Esthar}} On the former **Combat King 004** screen in Esthar, speak to the man to trigger the fixed Elnoyle fight. Leave and re-enter the screen to repeat it. This is the easiest source of **Energy Crystals** and **Moon Stones** for ultimate-weapon materials; Elnoyle is much rarer later, and card farming takes longer.

{{CALLOUT:point|Islands Closest to Hell and Heaven}} Both islands use **Level 100 encounters** and have hidden field Draw Points. Equip Siren’s **Move-Find** to reveal them. The hidden field Draw Points include high-tier spells such as **Ultima, Triple, Meteor, Full-Life, and Flare**, though the yield per point can be poor. Draw from them as you travel to advance the Steam **Magic Miner** achievement; prepare junctions before landing if you intend to fight.

{{CALLOUT:sidequest|Obel Lake Quest}} Equip Enc-None. At Obel Lake near Timber, hum at the small peninsula until the shadow asks you to find **Mr. Monkey**. Mr. Monkey is in the forest near Dollet; find him, throw a rock, sing, then return to Obel Lake. Collect the required clues: examine **Eldbeak Peninsula** for the Minde Island clue; search the thin island east of Timber's Mandy Beach and **Balamb Beach** for two rocks; and inspect the nest atop the **Monterosa Plateau** waterfall for another rock (defeat the two Thrustaevis or keep leaving until they depart). Then return to Obel Lake, skip rocks until one skips "many many times," and throw rocks at Mr. Monkey until he gives the final rock.

Assemble the rocks to point to **Mordred Plains** north of Esthar. Red rocks lie: do the opposite of what they say. When a red rock says the treasure is not here, examine the same spot again for **Three Stars**. Then fly to **Minde Island** southwest of Esthar and examine the pictured location for a **Luck-J Scroll**. Completing the route unlocks the **Obel Lake Secret** achievement.

{{CALLOUT:sidequest|PuPu Sidequest}} Enc-None works for UFO sightings. Visit the four sighting regions: Winhill Bluffs, Mandy Beach, Heath Peninsula, and Kashkabald Desert. Then land on the canyon top near Chocobo Sanctuary in Grandidi Forest and fight the UFO? enemy until it falls for an **Aegis Amulet**.

Bring at least **5 Elixirs** and the Item command, then run around the Balamb crater edge until PuPu appears. Give PuPu five Elixirs for the one-of-a-kind **PuPu Card**. Killing PuPu gives an Accelerator, and Devour gives Speed +1 to the Devourer, but neither reward is unique; the card is the completion route and unlocks the **UFO** achievement. Do **not** Card Mod the PuPu Card; it cannot be reacquired.

{{CALLOUT:warning|Omega handoff}} Omega Weapon is in Ultimecia Castle, not the open world. Before going there, stock Megalixirs, Phoenix Downs or Life/Full-Life, Death for ST-Def, Meltdown access, Aura or Aura Stones, and Defend users. The optional fight is inside the castle; use **Ultimecia’s Castle** for the bell route and battle plan before starting the timer.

{{CALLOUT:perfect-game|Perfect Game pacing}} Finish any remaining Disc 3 fights, card route steps, weapon-material farming, and world-map collection before proceeding beyond Mobile Type 8 in **The Final Mission**.

checkpoints.label: The Promise

checkpoints.label: Aerial exploration window

checkpoints.label: Cactuar
checkpoints.description: Defeat Jumbo Cactuar on Cactuar Island to unlock the Cactuar GF.

checkpoints.label: Bahamut
checkpoints.description: Answer the Deep Sea Research Center core prompts correctly and defeat Bahamut.

checkpoints.label: Eden
checkpoints.description: Draw Eden from Ultima Weapon in the Deep Sea Deposit, or use the later Tiamat fallback.

checkpoints.label: Obel Lake Secret
checkpoints.description: Complete the Obel Lake side quest; its rewards are Three Stars and the Minde Island Luck-J Scroll.

checkpoints.label: PuPu Card
checkpoints.description: Give PuPu five Elixirs at the Balamb crater encounter instead of killing or devouring him.

checkpoints.label: UFO
checkpoints.description: Complete PuPu's side quest by finishing the sightings, defeating UFO?, and resolving the PuPu encounter.

enemies.name: Ultima Weapon
enemies.notes: Eden is missable here; draw it before defeating Ultima Weapon.

chapters.title: The Final Mission
chapters.content:
For the first time in a long while, it is **mission time**.

{{CALLOUT:story|The Briefing}} Head to **Esthar's Presidential Palace**. There are **random encounters in Esthar City**, but landing directly at the **Airstation** saves time. Inside the Palace, if the Queen of Cards route has reached its Phoenix step, challenge the **Presidential Aide in the room where Rinoa was held earlier** and win Phoenix; the Queen route in the **Sidequests** tab covers its prerequisites and recovery. Then follow the hallway past the waiting room and enter the section that was previously ignored.

Speak to **President Laguna**. Ask any background questions you want, then ask about the **mission to defeat Ultimecia**. Speak to him again and answer yes to advance the dialogue. After the scenes, return to the Ragnarok cabin and challenge Laguna to Triple Triad for the **Squall Card**.

{{CALLOUT:refinement|Squall Card refinement}} The Squall Card refines into **3 Three Stars**. Each Three Stars can become **100 Triple**, or can teach a GF **Expendx3-1**.

When ready, **fly the Ragnarok into the Lunatic Pandora** for the final Disc 3 mission.

{{CALLOUT:warning|Final cleanup opportunity}} Flying into Lunatic Pandora begins the final mission, but it is **not yet the irreversible cutoff**. You can still return through Elevator #2 and leave aboard the Ragnarok until you proceed beyond Mobile Type 8's room. Use this earlier opportunity for cleanup if desired.

{{CALLOUT:preparation|Storming setup}} Exit the Ragnarok by taking the cockpit elevator and using the right-hand door. Before running forward, set **Poison-elemental Magic** on Elemental Attack, use **Sleep or Darkness** on Status Attack, defend **Wind and Lightning**, and cover statuses in this order: **Confuse, Darkness, Silence, Slow, and Poison**. Remove Mug before the first boss pair.

{{ENCOUNTERS:0}}

**Boss: Fujin** (Lv 1-44) - HP: 5,300-18,200 | AP: 8 | EXP: 0
- Draw: Lv 1-19: Aero, Cure, Life | Lv 20-29: Aero, Cura, Life | Lv 30-44: Aero, Curaga, Full-Life, Tornado
- Mug: 2x Megalixir (25%)
- Drop: Megalixir (100%)
- Card drop: Nothing
- Weakness: Poison x1.5
- Resist: Wind absorbs
- Vulnerable: Gravity; Darkness, Drain, Sleep, Slow, The End

**Boss: Raijin** (Lv 1-44) - HP: 5,400-22,600 | AP: 12 | EXP: 0
- Draw: Lv 1-19: Thunder, Protect, Shell | Lv 20-29: Thunder, Thundara, Shell, Protect | Lv 30-44: Thundara, Thundaga, Shell, Protect
- Mug: Power Wrist (25%)
- Drop: 3x Str Up (69.5%); 4x Str Up (19.9%); 5x Str Up (5.9%); 6x Str Up (4.7%)
- Card drop: Nothing
- Weakness: Poison x1.5
- Resist: Lightning absorbs
- Vulnerable: Gravity; Darkness, Drain, Sleep, Slow, The End

Strategy: Start with Sleep or Slow and reapply if it misses. Decide whether you value Raijin's **Power Wrist** mug more than his guaranteed Str Up drop table; remove Mug if you want the Str Up result. Fujin is a clean Megalixir source either way. After the fight, **Biggs and Wedge** appear but do not fight; talk to them if you want the scene, use the **Save Point**, then enter the doorway.

{{CALLOUT:point|Level 1 interior}} **All enemies here except bosses will be Level 1**. At the next fork, follow the normal route to the elevator room; the stairway still has a **Meteor Draw Point**; drawing from it contributes to the cumulative Steam **Magic Miner** achievement. If you missed conditional pickups during the earlier visit, use the left-hand tube and tunnel detour from this section to revisit the treasure route before the final **Elevator #1**. Only rewards unlocked by Laguna's Disc 1 excavation actions will be available; see **The Resistance** for the excavation flags and late recovery route. Return to the main hall, then take Elevator #1 toward Mobile Type 8.

Ride **Elevator #1**, follow the path north, and save. Equip Lightning-elemental magic to Elemental Attack and re-equip Mug only if you want the probes' stat-ups; Mobile Type 8's Laser Cannon drop is already guaranteed. Continue to fight the guardian robot.

**Boss: Mobile Type 8** (Lv 1-41) - HP: 30,300-42,300 | AP: 40 | EXP: 0
- Draw: Lv 1-19: Fire, Blizzard, Thunder, Flare | Lv 20-29: Fira, Blizzara, Thundara, Flare | Lv 30-41: Firaga, Blizzaga, Thundaga, Flare
- Mug: Laser Cannon (69.5%); 2x Laser Cannon (19.9%); 3x Laser Cannon (5.9%); 4x Laser Cannon (4.7%) - overall 12.5%
- Drop: Laser Cannon (69.5%); 2x Laser Cannon (19.9%); 3x Laser Cannon (5.9%); 4x Laser Cannon (4.7%) - 100%
- Card drop: Nothing
- Weakness: Lightning
- Vulnerable: Gravity; The End

**Boss: Left Probe** (Lv 1-41) - HP: 5,100-9,100 | AP: 0 | EXP: 0
- Draw: Lv 1-19: Cure, Esuna | Lv 20-29: Cura, Esuna | Lv 30-41: Curaga, Esuna
- Mug: 2x Vit Up (89.5%); 4x Vit Up (10.5%) - overall 12.5%
- Drop: Nothing

**Boss: Right Probe** (Lv 1-41) - HP: 5,100-9,100 | AP: 0 | EXP: 0
- Draw: Lv 1-19: Fire, Blizzard, Thunder | Lv 20-29: Fira, Blizzara, Thundara | Lv 30-41: Firaga, Blizzaga, Thundaga
- Mug: 2x Str Up (89.5%); 4x Str Up (10.5%) - overall 12.5%
- Drop: Nothing

Strategy: In **Mobile Mode**, damaging the main body triggers Twin Homing Laser while both probes remain. In **Support Mode**, attacking a probe triggers Homing Laser; the main body opens with **Corona** (party HP to 1), then follows on its next turn with **Megiddo Flame**, about 2,000 party-wide damage that ignores Spirit. Heal immediately after Corona. Mug the probes only if you are willing to fish for the 12.5% chance at **Vit Up** or **Str Up**; do not Mug the main body because its Laser Cannon table is also its guaranteed drop. After the fight, go back and save; use **another slot** in case you want to return to this point.

{{CALLOUT:missable|Actual end-of-Disc-3 cutoff}} You can still backtrack through **Elevator #2** to the Ragnarok now. Proceeding beyond Mobile Type 8's room is the real irreversible cutoff for towns and other civilized areas. Before crossing it, collect every remaining **Timber Maniacs** issue for the Steam achievement; finish the Queen of Cards creation route; confirm that the Queen is at **Shumi Village** and the **Trabia** trade rule is **Diff** if you plan to use her for Disc 4 card farming; complete the **Dollet Bone Quest**, **CC Group**, and **Shumi Village** routes; and register any shops you want to reach with **Call Shop**. If Queen steps remain, the Disc 4 CC Group can still recover rare cards; the Queen herself will be unavailable for card play and rule changes. The **Man from Garden Shop** remains available later; the other shops close. Use the Shumi **Ultima Draw Point** and fixed Esthar **Elnoyle** encounter as needed, and decide whether to recruit **Odin** now if you want the Gilgamesh outcome. After the cutoff, the accessible areas are Fire Cavern, Tomb of the Unknown King, Centra Ruins, the Chocobo Forests, Trabia Canyon, the Crash Site, Tears' Point, and the world map.

Switch the Lightning spell in Elemental Attack to **Bio** and remove Mug unless you specifically want Seifer's Hero/Holy War table. Continue past Mobile Type 8's room for the final Disc 3 duel.

**Boss: Seifer** (Lv 1-45) - HP: 3,700-34,500 | AP: 40 | EXP: 0
- Draw: Lv 1-19: Fire, Blizzard, Thunder | Lv 20-29: Fira, Blizzara, Thundara | Lv 30-45: Firaga, Blizzaga, Thundaga, Aura
- Mug: Hero (89.5%); Holy War (10.5%) - overall 12.5%
- Drop: Hero (89.5%); Holy War (10.5%) - 100%
- Card drop: Nothing
- Weakness: Poison x1.5
- Vulnerable: Drain, The End

Strategy: If the party is Lv 30+, stock Aura here before finishing the fight. If Odin was recruited, he appears automatically and is replaced by Gilgamesh; the battle ends after 13 turns or when Seifer reaches zero HP. The only way to avoid that replacement is not to recruit Odin before this fight. After Seifer falls, watch the scenes and reform the party if Rinoa was active. This is the transition into the next disc sequence.

checkpoints.label: Squall Card
checkpoints.description: Win the Squall Card from Laguna after the Esthar briefing scenes.

checkpoints.label: Conditional Lunatic Pandora treasures
checkpoints.description: Conditional rewards from the Laguna excavation include LuvLuv G, Phoenix Pinion, Power Generator, Combat King 005, Spd-J Scroll, the Silence Draw Point, and the one-time Ultima Draw Point; see The Resistance for the excavation flags and this chapter for the late recovery route.

checkpoints.label: Actual end-of-Disc-3 cutoff
checkpoints.description: After Mobile Type 8, backtrack via Elevator #2 for final cleanup before proceeding beyond its room.

checkpoints.label: Aura from Seifer
checkpoints.description: At Lv 30+, the final Disc 3 Seifer fight is a rare chance to draw Aura directly from an enemy.

chapters.title: The Awakening
chapters.content:
When control returns, make sure everyone is **Junctioned properly**, especially if the game forced you to use **changed party members** after Seifer.

Return to the room where you fought **Mobile Type 8**. Climb the crane-like structure on the right, go right, then continue up two screens for a scene. You can revisit other areas in **Lunatic Pandora**, but you **cannot leave**.

{{CALLOUT:preparation|Adel setup}} Before advancing, give an active character **Mug** and the **Draw** command. Raise your stats as much as practical and junction **Earth and Holy** to Elemental Defense; Adel uses Quake and Holy. Shell halves the damage from her Ultima, so have it ready for the whole party.

{{ENCOUNTERS:0}}

**Battle plan:** Rinoa does not act while Adel drains her HP each turn. If Rinoa dies, it is **Game Over**. Draw-cast **Regen** from Rinoa onto herself at the start and refresh it as needed. When **“Magical powers are concentrated on Adel!”** appears, Ultima is next; make sure Shell is active and heal the party beforehand.

Use **single-target attacks only** while Rinoa is attached. Do not summon GFs or choose attacks and Limit Breaks that can hit multiple targets. In particular, avoid Squall's multi-target Renzokuken finishers, Zell's My Final Heaven, and Irvine's Flame Shot, Scatter Shot, or Hyper Shot. Protect against Quake and Holy as prepared; if you must choose, heal instead of risking a multi-target hit.

Optional Mug: Try Adel's one-time steal only once Regen is active. Skip Mugging Rinoa; neither prize is worth risking her life. After Adel falls, watch the scenes.

checkpoints.label: Samantha Soul
checkpoints.description: Optional 6.25% Mug chance from Adel during the fight; prioritize Rinoa's survival.

checkpoints.label: 8x Megalixir
checkpoints.description: Optional 25% Mug chance from Rinoa during the Adel battle; only attempt if healing is stable.

chapters.title: Commencement Room
chapters.content:
After the scenes, you wake in a room with a **Save Point**. Use it once to spawn a dozen fake save points; the original is the only real one. Save at the original and use a **Tent** if needed.

{{CALLOUT:preparation|Element defense check}} Before leaving, set junctions for the active party and put **Draw** on at least one character if you still want enemy magic. Cover as many elements as practical in **Elem-Def**: Fire, Thunder, Ice, Wind, and Earth appear among the first ten fights. Full absorption is unrealistic. **Shell** and high Spirit help against Sorceress C's non-elemental **Ultima**, while Protect or Defend can help against the physical punches and counters.

{{ENCOUNTERS:0}}

Leave the room to start **11 consecutive one-enemy fights**: six Type A, four Type B, then the final Type C. Take any Draws you want before each enemy falls: Type A offers **Firaga, Thundaga, and Blizzaga**; Type B offers **Haste and Double**; Type C offers **Flare and Holy**. A and B give **0 AP**; C gives **55 AP**. None give EXP or card drops. Each can be Mugged for a Spell Stone: the listed Mug chance is **50%**, with a Meteor Stone in the first item slot (69.5% of successful Mugs) and an Ultima Stone in the other three (20%, 5.8%, 4.7%). Their guaranteed drop table is Flare Stone (69.5%), Holy Stone (20%), Meteor Stone (5.8%), or Ultima Stone (4.7%).

{{CALLOUT:enemy|First ten Sorceresses}} The first six Type A enemies each use a different signature spell in order: **Fire, Thunder, Fira, Blizzara, Thundara, Aero**. They also share Telekinetic Punch and Esuna, and are weak enough to often fall in one hit. The four Type B fights are #7 **Double then Thundaga**, #8 **Quake and Meltdown**, #9 **Meteor every turn**, and #10 **Double then Flare**. These usually take about two hits, but keep HP up against the stronger spells. If Meltdown inflicts Vit 0, remove it with **Esuna** or **Treatment**.

The final Type C is much more dangerous. When she is **not counting down**, any damage triggers **Creepy Touch**, a guaranteed critical physical counter. During the visible **5-4-3-2-1** countdown she does not counter; **Ultima** follows after 1. Keep Shell active, heal before the spell, and use the countdown window to attack. **Meltdown**, **Aura**, and strong single-target Limit attacks help end the fight before a second Ultima.

After the scene, you appear at **Edea’s House**. Run through the right-hand door, then out the back door for another scene. You cannot exit to the world map from here.

After the back-door scene, follow the linear path to the **Triple Draw Point** on the next screen and draw **Triple** if you need stock. Drawing here advances Steam **Magic Miner** if you still need draws. Continue to the Save Point and steps toward the castle. The portals to the left of the large chain return to the world map; if **Eden** is still missing, continue into the castle, where Tiamat is the final Draw opportunity, rather than taking a detour now.

checkpoints.label: Real Save Point
checkpoints.description: The original Save Point is real; the extra spawned ones are fake.

checkpoints.label: Triple Draw Point
checkpoints.description: Draw Triple on the path after Edea’s House; this Draw Point also advances Steam Magic Miner.

enemies.name: "Sorceress" C
enemies.notes: The final enemy counts down to Ultima and counters damage with Creepy Touch.

chapters.title: Ultimecia's Castle
chapters.content:
Before entering, save outside, stock recovery items, and check junctions for all six characters. The castle seals **Item, Magic, GF, Draw, Command Ability, Limit Break, Resurrection, and Save**, restoring one function after each guardian. **Attack, Junctions, Character Abilities, and Party Abilities** remain usable, and GFs can continue learning. Split into two functional parties: Green Party Switch Points let you change teams, and the Floodgate Key route and Omega setup require both.

{{ENCOUNTERS:0}}

{{CALLOUT:enemy|Castle random encounters}} Most **regular enemies** can appear somewhere in the castle, and their **levels will be completely random** instead of following the party average. Use the encounter list as a local checklist, but farm specific enemies elsewhere when possible.

{{CALLOUT:enemy|First guardian — Sphinxaur/Sphinxara}}

**Boss: Sphinxaur** (Lv 1-50) — HP: 10,000 | AP: 0
- Draw: Lv 1-19: Fire, Thunder, Cure | Lv 20-29: Fira, Thundara, Cura | Lv 30-50: Firaga, Thundaga, Curaga
- Mug: Elixir (25%)
- Drop: Nothing
- Weakness: Holy

**Boss: Sphinxara** — HP: 10,000 | AP: 30
- Draw: Lv 1-19: Fire, Thunder, Blizzard, Cure | Lv 20-29: Fira, Thundara, Blizzara, Cura | Lv 30-50: Firaga, Thundaga, Blizzaga, Curaga
- Mug: Nothing (0%)
- Drop: Megalixir (100%)
- Weakness: Holy

Strategy: With most abilities sealed, attack directly. **Mug Elixir** from Sphinxaur. Sphinxara uses Doom, Slow, Sleep, and Zombie, and summons Jelleye → Forbidden → Tri-Face in sequence. Zombie status makes Doom miss; if Sphinxara casts Zombie on a character already under Doom, the countdown is removed. Finish quickly with physical attacks. Holy junctioned to Elemental Attack deals double damage (Sphinxaur/Sphinxara have Holy ×2 weakness). After this fight, **unlock Draw first**. Several later guardians hold missed GFs, and Tiamat is the last chance to draw Eden if you missed it at the Deep Sea Research Center; each other GF opportunity is named beside its boss.

Proceed through the door behind Sphinxaur. The chandelier drops — inspect the floor hatch and descend. Junction **Thundaga to Elem-Def-J** for all three party members before going down.

**Boss: Tri-Point** (Lv 1-51) — HP: 2,400-22,400 | AP: 30
- Draw: Haste, Tornado, Blind, Siren
- Weakness: Fire ×4, Ice ×4

Strategy: Tri-Point counterattacks with **Mega Spark** (ignores Spr) whenever it is hit with the wrong element. With Thunder class magic on El.Def-J, Mega Spark heals the party. Tri-Point alternates between Fire and Ice weaknesses — attacking with the current weakness does NOT trigger a counter, and shifts the weakness to the other element. Exploit this: alternate members with Fire and Ice on El.Att-J. When Tri-Point uses **Scan** on a party member, cast **Protect** on that character or defeat Tri-Point before it acts again. Its next attack is Onrush, which ignores Vit and can deal up to 9,999 damage depending on Tri-Point's level. Draw **Siren** here if it was missed. Tri-Point drops a **Rocket Engine**, which teaches a GF **Spd+40%**. **Unlock Magic** after this fight.

With **Draw** and **Magic** restored, return to the main hall, go left down the hallway, then right to enter the Art Gallery. Examine all paintings. The clock reads VIII, VI, and IIII — find those numerals in the paintings and enter **VIVIDARIUM** · **INTERVIGILIUM** · **VIATOR** into the large left painting. Trauma appears from behind.

**Boss: Trauma** (Lv 1-56) — HP: 5,555-34,114 | AP: 30
- Draw: Meltdown, Leviathan
- Weakness: Wind ×2

**Boss: Droma** (Lv 1-56) — HP: 1,010-3,128 | AP: 30
- Draw: Esuna, Dispel
- Mug: 2x Meteor Stone (25%)
- Drop: Nothing

Strategy: Open with **Meltdown** on Trauma — draw it directly from Trauma for a free cast. Trauma creates two Dromas at the start. Keep the Dromas alive — if both Dromas are killed, Trauma uses the devastating **Mega Pulse Cannon** (ignores Spr and Shell), then creates two new ones. Trauma will eventually Drain its own Dromas to recover HP. Simply keep attacking Trauma; let it consume the Dromas itself. Draw **Leviathan** if missed. **Mug 2× Meteor Stone** from each Droma. Trauma drops an **Elem Atk**, which teaches El.Att-J to a GF.

Unlock **Item** if it is still sealed; otherwise unlock Limit Break. From the Art Gallery, go north twice and down the stairs. Take the upper-left exit, grab the key in the prison cell, then fight Red Giant.

**Boss: Red Giant** (Lv 1-52) — HP: 30,000 | AP: 30
- Draw: Demi, Pandemona

Strategy: Red Giant has **no elemental weaknesses** (all elements ×1) — its defenses come from extremely high Vitality (255) and Spirit (255), not elemental resistance. Cast **Meltdown** immediately — Red Giant has fixed HP at 30,000 regardless of level. Cast Blind to reduce its physical attacks (80% Darkness success rate). **Gravity and Demi work against Red Giant** despite its imposing appearance — draw and cast Demi from Red Giant itself to deal 25% current HP per cast, making it a useful self-damaging strategy early in the fight when raw damage is limited. When its HP falls below 9,000 it loses its sword and switches to unarmed punches. Draw **Pandemona** if missed. Red Giant drops **Diamond Armor**, which teaches GFHP+40%.

After Red Giant, unlock **Limit Break** if it is still sealed; otherwise unlock GF. Return to the Main Hall. Switch to the secondary party and move them left through the hall to the chandelier room — lower the lever. Switch back to the primary party and go upstairs through the doors, over the chandelier, to the balcony.

**Boss: Krysta** (Lv 1-55) — HP: 5,200-16,000 | AP: 30
- Draw: Holy, Carbuncle

Strategy: Krysta has extremely high Vitality, so Meltdown helps physical damage but is not required. Additionally, Krysta has **zero Spirit**, so magic damage lands without Spirit reduction. Krysta nullifies **Ice**, while Gravity attacks are effective. Krysta answers attacks with her Counter Rocket. Stay at high HP before the final blow — when Krysta is defeated, it uses **Ultima** as a desperate last strike. Draw **Carbuncle** if missed. Krysta drops **Elem Guard** items (teach El.Def-Jx4 to a GF — very valuable).

After Krysta, unlock **GF** if it is still sealed; otherwise unlock Command Ability. If Command Ability remains sealed, restore it at the next guardian so Mug and Defend are available for the later rooms; Draw was restored after Sphinxaur. Navigate through the Chapel. Head upstairs, across the bridge — **walk, do not run** across this bridge or the Armory Key may be knocked into the water below. If it falls, take the ladder on the right and retrieve it from the lower path. Use the Armory Key to unlock the door before the Flood Gate room. Fight Gargantua.

**Boss: Gargantua** (Lv 1-54) — HP: 10,100-15,400 | AP: 30
- Draw: Bio, Quake, Reflect, Cerberus
- Drop: Magic Armlet (100%)

Strategy: Starts as Vysage, Lefty, and Righty — defeat them to trigger the true Gargantua. Every non-fatal damaging hit can trigger **Counter Twist**, so avoid a prolonged direct-damage exchange. Gargantua's **Evil-Eye** inflicts Slow and Curse on a single target — keep Esuna or Remedy+ on hand; protect directly against **Curse and Slow** on St.Def-J. Quake targets all party members (Earth on El.Def-J to absorb). Inflict **Zombie**, then use Revive, Recover, or an X-Potion to finish it without a damaging counter; KO status is another lower-accuracy option. Draw **Cerberus** if missed (Cerberus can also be drawn from Gargantua). Also draw **Reflect** from Gargantua — this is one of the few available sources of Reflect magic at this point in the game. Gargantua always drops a **Magic Armlet**, which teaches Spr+60% to a GF.

After Gargantua, unlock **Command Ability** if it is still sealed; otherwise unlock Resurrection. Head to the fountain area below and check the **left side of the fountain** for the **Treasure Vault Key**. Go back to the Main Hall, upstairs, west, down the stairs, and find the difficult-to-see door on the left. Open the puzzle — the goal is to have all four vault boxes open simultaneously. Leave and re-enter to reset the puzzle, then touch boxes **2, 3, 1, 4** in that order.

**Boss: Catoblepas** (Lv 1-57) — HP: 10,500-38,500 | AP: 30
- Draw: Meteor, Alexander
- Weakness: Earth ×2, Water ×2

Strategy: Catoblepas is weak to **Earth (×2) and Water (×2)** — junction Quake or Water to El.Att-J. **Catoblepas absorbs Lightning** — it is healed by any Thunder-class magic, so remove Lightning from El.Att-J entirely for this fight. Catoblepas has low Vitality and low Spirit — both physical and magical damage land cleanly. Apply Blind to greatly reduce its claw and Deadly Horn physical attacks (60% Darkness success rate). Keep Thunder class magic on El.Def-J to handle Thundaga. Catoblepas uses **Thunder Summon** (area Thunder attack that ignores Spr) after it has used Thundaga three times — the damage is mitigated by junctioning **Thundaga** to El.Def-J. Before landing the killing blow, ensure Shell is active on all party members — Catoblepas uses **Meteor** as a final desperate strike. Draw **Alexander** if missed. Catoblepas always drops **Status Atk** items (teach St.Att-J to a GF). If you already own the Catoblepas Card (the boss does not drop it), Card Mod turns it into **1× Rename Card**. Rename Cards are the only in-game way to change a GF's name.

{{CALLOUT:point|Rosetta Stone}} After defeating Catoblepas, unlock **Resurrection** if it is still sealed. At the Elevator Room, put one team on the left lift, switch parties, and ride the matching lift to raise them into the Storage Room for the **Floodgate Key**. A supported split is Quistis/Selphie/Irvine on the left and Squall/Zell/Rinoa on the right; Quistis/Selphie/Zell vs. Squall/Irvine/Rinoa and Selphie/Quistis/Rinoa vs. Squall/Zell/Irvine also work. Return to the Flood Gate near the Red Giant/Armory route, unlock the chained lever with the key, and drain the water. In the Chapel, **press all eight controller buttons simultaneously** and hold until the chord ends. Release them together so the note cuts off cleanly. Return south to the courtyard, then go northeast through the lowered spikes and east along the waterways to the **Rosetta Stone** chest. The south route from the waterway opens a shortcut to the prison cell.

Continue to the clock tower. **Move-Find reveals a hidden Save Point** in the tower. Then climb the stairs, cross the bridge, and wait until the swinging bell moves left, then press the action button to ride it to the right side. Fight Tiamat on the balcony.

**Boss: Tiamat** (Lv 1-58) — HP: 21,200-89,600 | AP: 30
- Draw: Flare, Eden

Strategy: Tiamat spends several turns counting down before unleashing **Dark Flare**, a party-wide **Fire-elemental** attack that ignores Spirit. Junction enough Fire protection to nullify or absorb it; Firaga alone supplies 150% Fire resistance. Do not junction Fire, Thunder, or Wind class magic to El.Att-J — Tiamat resists both Fire and Thunder (×0.5 each) and is fully immune to Wind. **Draw GF Eden from Tiamat if it was not obtained from Ultima Weapon** — this is the absolute last opportunity in the game. Drawing Eden here triggers **Achievement: Eden** upon obtaining the GF. Cast Meltdown and use Aura + Renzokuken to end the fight quickly. Tiamat always drops **Status Guard** items (teach St.Def-Jx4 to a GF). If **Save** is still sealed, unlock it here; on the standard route this is the final seal. If it is already open, restore any other remaining function.

{{CALLOUT:preparation|Omega Weapon setup}} Before starting the timer, prepare both teams. Give **Defend** to everyone who has it (normally two characters), put **Item** on all three active characters, and use HP+80% as needed to reach exactly **9,999 HP**. Leave Elem-Atk empty and junction **Death** to St.Def-J; prioritize Auto-Haste, Auto-Protect, Auto-Shell, then Str+60%. Make sure someone can cast Meltdown and stock Megalixirs plus Phoenix Downs or Life/Full-Life/Revive.

{{CALLOUT:enemy|Omega Weapon}} Optional trigger: stage the prepared battle team at the courtyard/fountain Party Switch Point, then take the other team to the room just before the Art Gallery and pull the bell cord. The timer lasts about **60 seconds**. Use the nearby green switch point to change back to the waiting team, then run north through the courtyard into the Chapel and touch Omega's smoke before time expires. If the timer runs out, ring the bell again.

**Boss: Omega Weapon** — AP: 250
- Draw: Flare, Holy, Meteor, Ultima

Omega absorbs all elements, cannot be Slowed or Blinded, and has no Mug result.

{{CALLOUT:hint|Omega's fixed attack pattern}} Random physical swipes can occur between these steps:
1. **Lv5 Death** → Death on St.Def-J ignores this; cast Meltdown on Omega
2. **Meteor** → use Megalixir to restore full HP on all members
3. **Megido Flame** (fixed 9,998 to all — requires exactly 9,999 HP or someone dies) → all members at 1 HP; unleash the strongest Limit Breaks available. Squall's Renzokuken, Irvine's Armor Shot, and Quistis's Shockwave Pulsar are options if those characters are in the party
4. **Gravija** (75% current HP — at 1 HP deals zero damage) → Squall Renzokuken; two others use Defend
5. **Terra Break** (12 physical hits distributed randomly) → have Defend users guard; revive anyone KO'd and restore the party before Ultima
6. **Ultima** → use the strongest available Limit Breaks; higher Spirit and Shell help reduce the damage
7. **Light Pillar** (9,999 to one character — unavoidable unless Invincible) → Revive the KO'd member; use Megalixir
8. **Repeat from Meteor**


{{CALLOUT:hint|Alternate Invincible strategy}} Use a **Holy War** for whole-party Invincible or a Hero for one character, then reapply it if the status expires. The Gilgamesh Card refines into **10 Holy Wars**; the Laguna Card refines into **100 Heroes**. If Aura is scarce, a Power Wrist or Hypno Crown refines into **10 Aura Stones**, and each Aura Stone refines into **1 Aura**.

Drop: **Three Stars** — teaches any GF the **Expend×3-1** ability (while under Triple status, each spell cast draws from only 1 stock instead of 3; from a 100-stock supply that means 100 casts instead of 33, tripling magic endurance). Extra Three Stars beyond the three needed can also be refined into **100× Triple each** via Time Mag-RF. **Achievement: Omega Destroyed** — awarded upon defeating Omega Weapon.

From the Chapel, ascend the clock tower, cross the clock hands, and reach the final Save Point. If **Save** is restored, save here; it is the last safe save before the final chamber. If Save is still sealed, use a Tent here if Item is open, then return to the castle entrance and save outside before entering the point of no return. Finish junctioning all six characters in Final Preparations.

checkpoints.label: Omega Destroyed
checkpoints.description: Defeat Omega Weapon in Ultimecia's Castle. Station the primary party near the chapel, switch to the reserve party, ring the bell in the room before the art gallery to spawn Omega, then engage with the primary party. Card Mod the Gilgamesh Card → 10× Holy War for full party invincibility.

checkpoints.label: Missed GFs
checkpoints.description: If you missed any missable GFs (any of the ones listed above), Draw them from the bosses in Ultimecia Castle. (Not possible in the original JP version.)

checkpoints.label: Eden
checkpoints.description: Draw from Tiamat in Ultimecia Castle (preferable), or from Ultima Weapon.

enemies.name: Armadodo
enemies.notes: **Roll Attack** is always critical. A physical hit can make Armadodo fall over, halving its Vit/Spr for four turns; exploit that phase with magic.

enemies.name: Tri-Face
enemies.notes: Continue farming only if you still need Curse Spikes for refinement.

enemies.name: Hexadragon
enemies.notes: Found in the Grand Hall and Storage Room areas.

enemies.name: Malboro
enemies.notes: Rare Wine Cellar encounter (7.5%); Bad Breath can inflict all statuses at once, so protect the party’s status defenses.

enemies.name: Tonberry
enemies.notes: Found in Passageway (Screen 17); Chef’s Knife is used for Tonberry GF compatibility.

enemies.name: Elnoyle
enemies.notes: Found in Prison Cell and Chapel; Energy Crystals from Elnoyle can be refined into Pulse Ammo.

enemies.name: Adamantoise
enemies.notes: Found in Fountain Square; Adamantine is useful for Lion Heart and Ehrgeiz upgrades.

enemies.name: Grand Mantis
enemies.notes: Found in Screens 16, 17, and 25; Sharp Spikes are useful for crafting Save the Queen and Cardinal.

enemies.name: Blobra
enemies.notes: Found in Main Hall and Passageway. Blobra Cards refine into Rune Armlets for GF Spr+20%; Sticky Icky inflicts Slow, so consider Slow protection.

chapters.title: Final Preparations
chapters.content:
{{CALLOUT:point|Recovering Ragnarok}} Start the Disc 4 cleanup loop by leaving Ultimecia Castle through the portals one screen south of the entrance Save Point and taking the **middle portal**. On the large island north of Centra, go around the mountain range to the northeast and reach the **Forest of Solitude**. Solve its Chocobo puzzle if needed and ride out of the forest. Cross the southwestern shallows to the Centra coast near Edea’s House, then travel east to **Kashkabald Desert** to find Ragnarok. Use the nearby portal to add a convenient return route beside the castle portal chain.

{{CALLOUT:card|Ragnarok card and shop stop}} Board the ship and speak with **Man from Garden/Joker**. He is present whether or not the CC Group quest was completed; he runs a basic Item Shop and Junk Shop, and carries the **Leviathan Card** only if you never won it earlier.

{{CALLOUT:route|Disc 4 cleanup access}} Towns and most field areas are sealed, but these locations remain accessible: **Fire Cavern, Tomb of the Unknown King, Centra Ruins, Chocobo Forests, Deep Sea Research Center, Trabia Canyon, Crash Site, and Tears’ Point**. Encounters in the open areas use the same state as at the end of Disc 3. The Ragnarok provides the remaining world-map travel; use it to reach the Crash Site and cleanup branches before returning to the castle.

{{CALLOUT:perfect|Odin timing}} If you deliberately postponed recruiting Odin so he would not be replaced by Gilgamesh during the Disc 3 Seifer fight, Centra Ruins is available now. For a perfect-file item sweep, finish all desired Mug farming first: Odin can randomly defeat an enemy before you steal from it. Recruit him after that if you still want the Odin GF on this file.

{{CALLOUT:point|Islands Closest to Hell and Heaven}} For EXP and late Draw Point cleanup, the **Island Closest to Hell** is immediately west of the Galbadia continent; the **Island Closest to Heaven** is the largest island northeast of Grandidi Forest. Both use fixed **Level 100** encounters. Equip Siren’s **Move-Find** to reveal the hidden field Draw Points, which include high-level magic such as Ultima, Triple, Meteor, Full-Life, and Flare. Drawing from them also contributes to Steam’s **Magic Miner** achievement. The optional ultimate monster is fought inside Ultimecia Castle; see the Castle chapter for its strategy.

{{CALLOUT:perfect|Final-file checks}} Before committing to the ending, confirm that the CC Group was completed by the end of Disc 3 if you need its Ragnarok card players, and that every Esthar shop you need is already listed through Call Shop. Keep **Ultima Weapon alive** if you still need its fixed Deep Sea Research Center encounters for Tri-Face and Luck Up farming. Siren must be Level 100 to refine Dark Matter. For item routes and abilities, use the canonical Cards, GFs, Abilities, Refine, and Items tabs. If you want to fight Omega Weapon again after defeating it, do not save afterward.

{{CALLOUT:refinement|Final refinement routes}} Eden’s GFAbl Med-RF and late-game rare-card recovery open the final refinement tier. Only one copy of each rare card can be held at a time, so refine each card before winning another if a recipe needs multiple copies. Useful routes include **100 Tri-Face Cards → 100 Curse Spikes → Dark Matter → Shaman Stone → Rosetta Stone**; **2 Minotaur Cards → 20 Adamantine → Steel Curtain**; **5 Irvine Cards → 15 Rocket Engines → 3 Spd Ups**; and **Ward Card → 3 Gaea’s Rings → 3 HP Ups**. Use the Refine and Items tabs to look up other recipe ratios and item sources.

With the castle guardians defeated and the seals restored, verify that all six characters have the intended commands back: **Items, Magic, GF, Draw, Command Abilities, Limit Breaks, and Resurrection**.

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Endgame GF grouping strategy}} Keep the active three-person party carrying the full GF loadout whenever possible, then use Switch/Junction Exchange when party members change. The endgame grouping below aims to spread junction coverage, stat Bonus abilities, and role focus across three setups instead of stacking all power on one character.
| Strength | Defense | Magic |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cactuar / Alexander / Pandemona / Diablos / Shiva | Eden / Tonberry / Doomtrain / Leviathan / Carbuncle / Brothers | Bahamut / Cerberus / Siren / Ifrit / Quezacotl |

{{CALLOUT:mechanics|Endgame magic junction templates}} These are role-focused examples, not mandatory builds. Use them as a fast baseline, then adjust around your actual party, spell inventory, enemy elements, and status threats. Avoid Elemental Attack unless the enemy weakness is known; the wrong element can heal enemies.
| Junction | Strength | Defense | Magic |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| HP | Full-Life | Ultima | Full-Life |
| Str | Ultima | Meteor | Meteor |
| Vit | Meltdown | Meltdown | Meltdown |
| Mag | Meteor | Holy | Ultima |
| Spr | Reflect | Full-Life | Reflect |
| Spd | Triple |  |  |
| Eva | Tornado |  |  |
| Hit | Double |  |  |
| Luck | Aura |  |  |
| Elem-Atk | Nothing/Depends |  |  |
| Elem-Def | Flare / Life / Shell / Protect |  |  |
| ST-Atk | Depends (Death, Sleep, Pain) |  |  |
| ST-Def | Berserk / Confuse / Two of Death, Sleep, Pain |  |  |

{{CALLOUT:enemy|Optional Omega Weapon}} Omega is optional. Use the **Ultimecia’s Castle** chapter’s **Omega Weapon** section for the full setup and attack pattern.

For the final save route, use the **Ultimecia’s Castle** chapter. Finish junctioning all six characters before entering the final chamber.

checkpoints.label: Recover Ragnarok
checkpoints.description: Take the middle portal, use a Chocobo from Forest of Solitude to cross the shallows, and recover Ragnarok in Kashkabald Desert.

checkpoints.label: Omega Weapon Bell Route
checkpoints.description: If Omega remains undefeated, return to Ultimecia Castle and follow the complete bell route in that chapter’s Omega Weapon section; skip after defeating Omega.

chapters.title: The Final Battle
chapters.content:
From the pendulum section of the clock tower, ascend the rest of the tower. At the clock exterior, cross the hands, climb down the ladder on the far side, continue to the bridge, and save. The door ahead is the point of no return: finish any remaining outside cleanup before opening it. This is the last calm moment before the full final sequence.

{{CALLOUT:spoiler|Final battle party rules}} **three party members are selected at random** to begin. If a KO'd character is left down too long, they are **absorbed into time** and removed from the battle; another reserve character enters if one is available. If no reserves remain, that slot stays empty. Revive wanted party members quickly, or deliberately let unwanted members be replaced. If all current fighters are KO'd at once, it is Game Over. Also, **any abilities still sealed remain sealed** for the entire final battle.

{{CALLOUT:preparation|Final junction setup}} Because the opening trio is random, give **all six characters** enough junctioned HP and elemental defense, plus an Item/revival option, before entering. Put your strongest junctions on your three favored fighters; give **Tonberry to a fourth member** so at least one reserve has useful abilities. Junction **Water or Wind elemental magic to Elem-Atk**; ST-Atk is not useful here. Prioritize status defense against Stop, Pain, Curse, and Slow in that order; Auto-Haste already blocks Stop and Slow. Pain on ST-Def is excellent because it covers Curse plus Darkness, Poison, and Silence. For passive abilities, prioritize Auto-Haste, Auto-Shell, Auto-Protect, then stat boosts. Focus especially on Spr, and **do not use Mug or Rare Item** because nothing in the sequence has useful mugs or drops.

In **Final Fantasy VIII Remastered**, choose **“Get it over with”**; on the original PlayStation version, choose **“Hell, let’s go in.”** The battle begins after the scene.

**Boss: Ultimecia** (Lv 1-65) - HP: 4,600-43,000 | AP: 0 | EXP: 0
- Draw: Haste, Slow, Reflect, Demi
- Mug: Nothing (0%)
- Drop: Nothing (0%)
- Card Drop: Nothing
- Weakness: Poison [1.5x]
- Element Resist: Holy nullifies
- Status Weak: The End

Strategy (Ultimecia): Keep **Draw** available if you need Haste, Slow, Reflect, or Demi. Apply Meltdown and use Aura-backed Limit Breaks. Maelstrom sharply lowers the whole party's HP and can inflict Curse or Slow, so heal and clear statuses immediately; use Dispel if she casts Double. Keep HP high and revive characters you want to retain before Ultimecia absorbs a KO'd fighter into time. She can also destroy a GF if allowed to take a turn during a summon, so avoid long summons.

**Boss: Griever** (Lv 1-65) - HP: 16,750-115,950 | AP: 0 | EXP: 0
- Draw: Bio, Quake, Tornado
- Mug: Nothing (0%)
- Drop: Nothing (0%)
- Card Drop: Nothing
- Weakness: Wind, Holy [2.5x]
- Element Resist: Flying, Poison absorbs
- Status Weak: The End

Strategy (Griever): Remove Poison from Elem-Atk before attacking because Griever absorbs Poison. Wind and Holy hit hardest; draw Bio, Quake, or Tornado if you still need stock. If Griever uses Triple, Dispel it. Keep Spirit high and Shell active for Shockwave Pulsar; it is used once, and may be a parting attack if Griever is defeated before using it. Griever can inflict Doom, so clear it with Treatment, Remedy+, Elixir, or Megalixir. Revive wanted characters immediately.

**Boss: Ultimecia/Griever** (Lv 1-65) - HP: 13,050-176,250 | AP: 0 | EXP: 0
- Draw: Firaga, Thundaga, Blizzaga
- Mug: Nothing (0%)
- Drop: Nothing (0%)
- Card Drop: Nothing
- Weakness: Lightning, Water
- Element Resist: Flying, Poison nullifies, Holy absorbs
- Status Weak: The End

**Boss: Helix** (Lv 1-65) - HP: 4,400-30,000 | AP: 0 | EXP: 0
- Draw: Esuna, Dispel
- Mug: Nothing (0%)
- Drop: Nothing (0%)
- Card Drop: Nothing
- Weakness: None
- Element Resist: Flying
- Status Weak: The End

Strategy (Ultimecia/Griever): The **Helix support units** can be drawn from for Esuna and Dispel. One Helix adds Ultima to the main body's attack list; two add Meteor and enable Great Attractor every second turn. Great Attractor is heavy physical damage, so Protect or Defend helps. If a Helix appears, either destroy it (Ultimecia can summon another) or focus the main body until it has lost about 65% of its maximum HP. At that threshold its tail disappears, both Helixes vanish, and the safer second stage begins. Use Lightning or Water damage on the main body and keep Protect/Shell up.

**Boss: Ultimecia (Final Form)** (Lv 1-65) - HP: 16,500-278,900 | AP: 0 | EXP: 0
- Draw: Flare, Holy
- Mug: Nothing (0%)
- Drop: Nothing (0%)
- Card Drop: Nothing
- Weakness: None
- Element Resist: Flying
- Status Weak: The End

**Boss: Ultimecia (Lower Portion)** (Lv 1-65) - HP: 2,300-21,500 | AP: 0 | EXP: 0
- Draw: Apocalypse
- Mug: Nothing (0%)
- Drop: Nothing (0%)
- Card Drop: Nothing
- Weakness: None
- Element Resist: Flying
- Status Weak: The End

Strategy (Final Form): **Warning:** Ultimecia can destroy an entire random spell stock from a character, potentially stripping an important junction bonus mid-fight. Prioritize killing her quickly before she can repeat this. Apply Meltdown as needed and continue with Aura-backed Limit Breaks. Hell's Judgment drops everyone to 1 HP; respond immediately with healing such as a Megalixir. Keep **Draw** equipped on a character if you want to stock Apocalypse. When the lower portion appears, Ultimecia uses Draw Apocalypse and casts it on her next turn; the lower portion itself does not attack. Draw a few casts if desired (Apocalypse cannot be junctioned in a normal game), then destroy the lower portion quickly to stop that attack. Keep Shell up and heal after Hell's Judgment while finishing the main body.

{{CALLOUT:spoiler|Ending}} After Ultimecia falls, the conclusion plays. The ending is long and fully cinematic, so enjoy it once the battle is done.

**Congratulations - Final Fantasy VIII Remastered is complete.**

checkpoints.label: Final Bridge Save
checkpoints.description: Save after crossing the clock hands and reaching the bridge before entering the final chamber.

checkpoints.label: End of Game
checkpoints.description: Defeat Ultimecia and finish the final-battle sequence to unlock the Steam achievement.

achievements.title: Magic Miner
achievements.description: Draw magic 100 times from draw points throughout the game. Activate the Move-Find ability (Siren) to reveal hidden field draw points. Begin drawing every draw point encountered from the start.

achievements.title: Magician
achievements.description: Draw (Stock) magic from enemies 100 times in battle. Junction the Draw command to a character before each encounter to ensure actions are counted. Draw from every enemy throughout the game.

achievements.title: 100 Kills
achievements.description: Defeat 100 enemies. Achieved through standard story progression. If using the No Encounters booster or running from battles, disable it during normal play to accrue kills naturally.

achievements.title: 1000 Kills
achievements.description: Defeat 1,000 enemies. If this remains after the other achievements, revisit an area with frequent, weak encounters and keep fighting.

achievements.title: Quezacotl
achievements.description: Unlock Guardian Force Quezacotl. Interact with the desk in Squall's classroom, select "Turn on the power," then "Tutorials." Quistis forces acquisition at the front gate if missed.

achievements.title: Shiva
achievements.description: Unlock Guardian Force Shiva. Obtained simultaneously with Quezacotl via the classroom desk tutorial sequence at Balamb Garden.

achievements.title: Ifrit
achievements.description: Unlock Guardian Force Ifrit. Defeat Ifrit in the Fire Cavern east of Balamb Garden within the chosen time limit. A 10-minute limit is sufficient.

achievements.title: Siren
achievements.description: Unlock Guardian Force Siren. Draw Siren from Elvoret atop the Dollet Radio Tower. Missing this leaves only the Disc 4 Tri-Point fallback in Ultimecia's Castle.

achievements.title: Diablos
achievements.description: Unlock Guardian Force Diablos. Use the Magical Lamp (received from Cid after graduation) to trigger the Diablos battle. Save beforehand; cast Demi twice to reduce its HP, then defeat it.

achievements.title: Brothers
achievements.description: Unlock Guardian Force Brothers (Sacred + Minotaur). Complete the Tomb of the Unknown King northeast of Deling City. At every 4-way crossroad, take the right-hand route to reach each directional chamber.

achievements.title: Carbuncle
achievements.description: Unlock Guardian Force Carbuncle. Draw it from either Iguion during the Deling City assassination attempt; if missed, draw it from Krysta in Ultimecia's Castle on Disc 4.

achievements.title: Leviathan
achievements.description: Unlock Guardian Force Leviathan. Missable — draw from NORG aboard Balamb Garden. Damage the pod to expose NORG's body, then draw Leviathan immediately.

achievements.title: Tonberry
achievements.description: Unlock Guardian Force Tonberry. Defeat Tonberries in the lower Centra Ruins until Tonberry King appears; the threshold varies from 18 to 24 defeated Tonberries. Defeat Tonberry King to receive the GF.

achievements.title: Pandemona
achievements.description: Unlock Guardian Force Pandemona. Draw from Fujin during the boss fight in Balamb Town; if missed, draw it from Red Giant in Ultimecia's Castle on Disc 4.

achievements.title: Cerberus
achievements.description: Unlock Guardian Force Cerberus. Defeat it in Galbadia Garden's main hall; if missed, draw it from Gargantua in Ultimecia's Castle on Disc 4.

achievements.title: Alexander
achievements.description: Unlock Guardian Force Alexander. Draw it from Edea during the final Galbadia Garden battle; if missed, draw it from Catoblepas in Ultimecia's Castle on Disc 4.

achievements.title: Cactuar
achievements.description: Unlock Guardian Force Cactuar. After obtaining Ragnarok, locate Cactuar Island (small island off the eastern coast of the Esthar continent). Interact with Jumbo Cactuar on the world map to begin the encounter.

achievements.title: Doomtrain
achievements.description: Unlock Guardian Force Doomtrain. Acquire the Solomon Ring from Tears' Point (near Esthar). Collect 6× Remedy+, 6× Steel Pipe, and 6× Malboro Tentacle, then use the Solomon Ring from the Items menu.

achievements.title: Bahamut
achievements.description: Unlock Guardian Force Bahamut. Navigate to the core of the Deep Sea Research Center (southwest of Esthar). At the steam room panel choose: "It's not our will to fight" → "Never" → the bottom option. Awarded upon victory.

achievements.title: Eden
achievements.description: Unlock Guardian Force Eden. Draw from Ultima Weapon deep in the Deep Sea Research Center after defeating Bahamut. Last opportunity: draw from Tiamat in Ultimecia's Castle on Disc 4.

achievements.title: First Salary
achievements.description: Receive the first SeeD salary. Awarded automatically after the Training Center incident and the return to the dormitory.

achievements.title: Timber Maniacs
achievements.description: Collect all 12 Timber Maniacs magazines. Locations span the full game: Balamb Hotel, Timber Maniacs Office, Timber Hotel, Deling City Hotel, Dollet Hotel, Dollet Pub, FH Inn, FH rail dead-end house, Shumi Village, Trabia Garden Graveyard, Edea's Orphanage, White SeeD Ship.

achievements.title: Card Player
achievements.description: Play Triple Triad. The achievement is available as soon as you receive the starter cards and challenge an NPC who accepts games; a win is not required.

achievements.title: Loser
achievements.description: Lose a rare card in a Triple Triad game. An early option is intentionally surrendering the Ifrit Card, but it is useful for card play and later card goals; you can earn this later with another rare card.

achievements.title: Cards Club Master
achievements.description: Defeat every CC Group member at Triple Triad. After 15 qualifying Garden wins, defeat Jack (Main Hall) → Club (back of the 1F circle) → Diamond (Main Hall) → Spade (2F Hallway) → Heart/Xu (Bridge) → King (Dormitory rest event after playing Kadowaki). Joker appears on the Training Center bridge and may be defeated any time after challenging Jack, but must be beaten before King appears.

achievements.title: Chocobo
achievements.description: Capture a Chocobo. Visit the Beginner Forest (northernmost continent near Shumi Village). Purchase ChocoWhis for 1,000 Gil, then use the whistle in the upper-left corner where only one Chicobo appears.

achievements.title: Ragnarok
achievements.description: Find Ragnarok. Catch Rinoa during the space rescue to reach the ship and unlock this achievement; then clear the Propagator pairs in the next chapter.

achievements.title: Handyman
achievements.description: Upgrade any weapon at a Junk Shop. Balamb Town is an early opportunity after the SeeD Exam if you have the materials; Deling City and later shops remain alternatives. The Lionheart is not required.

achievements.title: Obel Lake Secret
achievements.description: Complete the Obel Lake side quest. Hum at the lake peninsula (Trabia continent) → find Mr. Monkey near Dollet → collect 4 stone inscriptions across the world map → decode "TREASUREATMINDEISLE" → retrieve Luck-J Scroll at Minde Isle. Must be completed before Disc 4.

achievements.title: UFO
achievements.description: Complete PuPu's side quest. Witness the four UFO flyovers at Mandy Beach, Kashkabald Desert, Winhill Bluffs, and Heath Peninsula; defeat UFO? north of the Chocobo Sanctuary area, then meet PuPu at the former Balamb Garden site and feed it 5 Elixirs.

achievements.title: Omega Destroyed
achievements.description: Defeat Omega Weapon in Ultimecia's Castle. Station the primary party near the chapel, switch to the reserve party, ring the bell in the room before the art gallery to spawn Omega, then engage with the primary party. Card Mod the Gilgamesh Card → 10× Holy War for full party invincibility.

achievements.title: End of Game
achievements.description: Finish the game.

achievements.title: Top Rank
achievements.description: Reach SeeD Rank A. Written SeeD tests in Menu → Tutorial → TEST each raise the rank to the next threshold and are available only up to Squall's current level; use as many as needed alongside normal SeeD Exp gains.

achievements.title: Maximum HP
achievements.description: Reach 9,999 HP on any character. Junction high-HP magic, equip HP+ abilities, and stack character HP bonuses if needed.

missables.title: Siren
missables.description: Draw Siren from Elvoret atop the Dollet communications tower before ending the battle.

missables.title: X-ATM092
missables.description: Destroy X-ATM092 before it reaches the town.

missables.title: Battle Meter, Magical Lamp
missables.description: Obtain both items from Cid before boarding the train to Timber. (Diablos can be obtained at any point in the game so long as you have the Magical Lamp.)

missables.title: Angelo Recover, Angelo Reverse
missables.description: Do not teach Rinoa these skills until you're completely finished with Angelo Searching.

missables.title: Girl Next Door
missables.description: Grab from Timber Maniacs building before Disc 4.

missables.title: Pet Nametag #2
missables.description: After leaving Timber, encourage the man outside the Timber Maniacs building to become a journalist (must be done before finishing Disc 1), then return here after completing Missile Base and speak to him.

missables.title: Location Displayer
missables.description: Buy it from the soldier outside Caraway's Mansion before giving him the student's ID number.

missables.title: Carbuncle
missables.description: Draw Carbuncle from the Iguion bosses during the Deling City assassination sequence before defeating them.

missables.title: Eyes on Me
missables.description: When speaking to Raine in Winhill, ask her about Julia before leaving the conversation. This unlocks the Eyes on Me entry and the opportunity does not return.

missables.title: Pet Nametag #1
missables.description: Obtain from D-District Prison (Level 2, left cell).

missables.title: Character Report
missables.description: Beat the Floor 10 right-cell card player once before leaving D-District Prison to obtain Character Report, the Battle Meter upgrade.

missables.title: Leviathan
missables.description: Draw Leviathan from NORG after the pod opens during the Balamb Garden basement fight.

missables.title: Master Fisherman's Quest, Occult Fan III
missables.description: Do this before going upstairs in Mayor Dobe's house (this is the house at the middle of the solar panel array).

missables.title: Pandemona
missables.description: Draw from Fujin in Balamb.

missables.title: Cerberus
missables.description: Defeat Cerberus before the end of Disc 2.

missables.title: Alexander
missables.description: Draw Alexander from Edea during the final Disc 2 battle before she is defeated.

missables.title: Esthar / Time Compression tutorial entries
missables.description: On Disc 3, talk to Edea until Adel is mentioned in yellow to unlock Esthar (1) and Esthar (2), then talk to Cid until he has no new lines for Time Compression and The Great Hyne.

missables.title: Timber Maniacs
missables.description: Pick up the Timber Maniacs issue on the White SeeD Ship while the ship is accessible; after this story window, the ship disappears.

missables.title: Zone
missables.description: Do not give Zone the Girl Next Door. It's unique, but nothing he gives in return can't be gotten through other methods.

missables.title: Occult Fan IV
missables.description: Before going to Lunar Gate, speak to the Presidential Aide near the Airstation in Esthar, then again in the Presidential Palace, then pick up the magazine off the ground.

missables.title: End of Disc 3
missables.description: All towns and most world locations become inaccessible on Disc 4. Finish desired sidequests before entering Lunatic Pandora; after defeating Mobile Type 8, crossing the next screen into the Seifer sequence is the final irreversible cutoff.

missables.title: Missed GFs
missables.description: Ultimecia Castle provides fallback Draw opportunities for the seven earlier drawable GFs: Siren, Carbuncle, Leviathan, Pandemona, Cerberus, Alexander, and Eden. This fallback is not present in the original Japanese release.

missables.title: Eden
missables.description: Draw Eden from Ultima Weapon in the Deep Sea Deposit when first available; if missed, the final fallback is Tiamat in Ultimecia's Castle.

missables.title: PuPu Card
missables.description: Finish PuPu's Quest by feeding PuPu 5 Elixirs to receive this.

abilitySections.title: Abilities
paragraphs: Use this tab to check which abilities can be assigned to characters, which GFs learn them, and which items can teach them. Magic spell data, GF data, and item data live in their own top-level tabs so this view stays focused on ability assignment.
Available To lists the GFs that come with the ability or can learn it through AP. AP is the learn cost; if every native GF already has the ability learned, the cost is shown as N/A.

Description mirrors the in-game function. Taught By lists the teaching item when one exists. If Taught By is N/A, do not remove that ability from a GF with Amnesia Greens on a perfect-file route because there is no item-based way to relearn it.

To assign an ability, junction a GF that knows it, open the Junction menu, then equip the command, character, or party ability in an available slot. Attack remains available even without a GF, though some abilities modify or replace that command.

abilitySections.title: Junction Abilities
paragraphs: These abilities open up Junction slots (remember that no Magic and no more than 3 Command Abilities and 2 total Character/Party Abilities can be Junctioned without a proper Junction Ability learned), allowing you to increase stats, modify elemental or status properties, or assign more than two Character/Party Abilities.

In this section, the stat Junctions will each contain ranked lists of spells in order of best to worst (excluding Apocalypse, as it can't be Junctioned in a normal game, but you can still look at its stats if you feel like using a cheating device to hack it in), while the Elem and Status Junction abilities have spell effects covered in their respective Junction Reference sections, with the idea of helping you make efficient use of whatever Magic you have at the moment.

Allows you to junction Magic to a character's Strength stat, increasing your physical attack power. The spells, in order of strength:

Allows you to Junction Magic to a character's Evasion stat, causing enemy physicals to miss more often. The most useful choices are:

(Note: Due to the mechanics of the Evasion stat (it's derived from Speed), the exact value of your Evasion% may vary by a point from the spell values listed below. This is because Eva Junctions don't actually Junction directly to Eva; instead, they increase the character's Speed for the sole purpose of calculating Evasion. Thus, the spells Junctioned to Spd-J (as well as any increases through Items) will increase the character's Eva proportional to the amount they raise Speed.)

Allows you to Junction Magic to Elem-Atk, giving your basic attack the associated elemental property.
Allows you to Junction Magic to ST-Atk, giving your basic attack the associated status effects.

Allows you to Junction up to two spells to Elem-Def, reducing damage taken from elemental attacks.
Allows you to Junction up to four spells to Elem-Def, reducing damage taken from elemental attacks.
Allows you to Junction one spell to ST-Def, reducing the probability of associated status ailments being inflicted.
